requirements.text: The "Type", "Code", and "Subject" values MUST be as specified in error's specification. The "Title" field MAY be modified as needed based on the context in which the implementation is running. This includes being specified in a language other than English, however it MUST still include the same substitution values (possibly in a different order).

review.note: The directly reviewed catalog vectors assert exact Type/status/Subject and substitution values. The unrestricted all-errors and localized-title contract remains pending, and binding-specific Code mapping is recorded separately rather than reopened as an old HTTP error defect.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing

requirements.text: Most of the error conditions mentioned in this specification will include a reference to one of the errors listed in this section. While it is RECOMMENDED that implementations use those errors (for consistency), they MAY choose to use a more appropriate one. Implementations MAY define additional extension fields, as well as new error definitions. For new errors, it is RECOMMENDED that the "Subject" value appears within the "Title" field, when appropriate.

review.note: The source permits appropriate alternative/extension errors and recommends style for custom diagnostics; server_error is optional for unexpected failures. These permissions are not coverage promotions and do not permit leaking untrusted exception data.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing

requirements.text: While not a requirement, it is RECOMMENDED that custom errors adhere to the following rules for consistency:

review.note: The source permits appropriate alternative/extension errors and recommends style for custom diagnostics; server_error is optional for unexpected failures. These permissions are not coverage promotions and do not permit leaking untrusted exception data.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing / action_not_supported

requirements.text: In the case of using the HTTP protocol binding, this error MUST include the HTTP `Allow` header in the response indicating which HTTP methods the API supports, if any.

review.note: Actual action_not_supported HTTP vectors assert 405 and the complete expected Allow method list for supported route shapes, not merely presence of an Allow header.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing / bad_request

requirements.text: This error is purposely generic and can be used when there isn't a more condition-specific error that would be more appropriate. Implementations SHOULD attempt to use a more specific error when possible. Notice, the `Title` field is just a substitution value and MUST NOT be empty.

review.note: Current bad_request paths contain concrete nonempty details, and more specific catalog errors are preferred. No direct reviewed generic bad_request response vector proves its title substitution/emptiness contract; other error titles are not the same case.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing / not_found

requirements.text: Note, this SHOULD only be used when the request was directed to an entity that does not exist. For cases where the target entity does exist, but there is an invalid attempt to reference one that doesn't, the [unknown_id](#unknown_id) error SHOULD be used instead.

review.note: Direct absent entities return not_found, while a valid Resource with a nonexistent requested default Version returns unknown_id with the correct Resource subject and Version arguments.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing / parsing_data

requirements.text: This is a fairly generic error, so if a more focused one (e.g. [invalid_attribute](#invalid_attribute)) can be used instead, then it SHOULD be. `<data_description>` is meant to be a phrase, or identifier, of the data being parsed; e.g. `/model`.

review.note: Malformed/duplicate JSON uses parsing_data with the exact entity subject and nonempty detail; typed metadata violations use more specific errors. The actual wire vectors make the intended distinction explicit.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing / server_error

requirements.text: This error MAY be used when it appears that the incoming request was valid but something unexpected happened in the server that caused an error condition.

review.note: The source permits appropriate alternative/extension errors and recommends style for custom diagnostics; server_error is optional for unexpected failures. These permissions are not coverage promotions and do not permit leaking untrusted exception data.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing / unknown_group_type

requirements.text: Attempts to reference an unknown Group type MUST generate an error ([unknown_group_type](#unknown_group_type)).

review.note: Unknown Group and Resource types are directly rejected with their distinct catalog errors, exact typed request subjects and required type-name arguments. This does not infer producer model absence semantics from the full server.

source.section: xRegistry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Error Processing / unknown_resource_type

requirements.text: Attempts to reference an unknown Resource type MUST generate an error ([unknown_resource_type](#unknown_resource_type)).

review.note: Unknown Group and Resource types are directly rejected with their distinct catalog errors, exact typed request subjects and required type-name arguments. This does not infer producer model absence semantics from the full server.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Notations and Terminology / Notational Conventions

requirements.text: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in [RFC 2119](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2119).

review.note: RFC 2119 interpretation, not an executable feature. This proposal reviews the entire active HTTP source, including subordinate rules, wire sketches and examples; implementation suggestions are not execution receipts.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Notations and Terminology / Notational Conventions

requirements.text: For clarity, OPTIONAL attributes (specification-defined and extensions) are OPTIONAL for clients to use, but the servers' responsibility will vary. Server-unknown extension attributes MUST be silently stored in the backing datastore. Specification-defined attributes and server-known extension attributes MUST generate an error if the corresponding feature is not supported or enabled. However, as with all attributes, if accepting the attribute results in a bad state (such as exceeding a size limit or resulting in a security issue), then the server MAY choose to reject the request.

review.note: Model-permitted extension values pass through validation, Merge and publication without feature-specific handlers. Closed-model unknown names remain errors, not silently accepted extensions. Disabled metadata and finite host budgets are explicit rejections.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Notations and Terminology / Notational Conventions

requirements.text: In the pseudo JSON format snippets `?` means the preceding item is OPTIONAL, `*` means the preceding item MAY appear zero or more times, and `+` means the preceding item MUST appear at least once. The presence of the `#` character means the remaining portion of the line is a comment. Whitespace characters in the JSON snippets are used for readability and are not normative.

review.note: Defines pseudocode cardinality and comments. The sketches were interpreted as notation, not JSON payloads containing comments, ellipses or optionality markers.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Binding Overview / HTTP API Patterns

requirements.text: While these APIs are shown to be at the root path of a host, implementations MAY choose to prefix them as necessary. However, the same prefix MUST be used consistently for all APIs in the same Registry instance.

review.note: MapXRegistry applies one MountPath/PathBase prefix; navigation is generated from configured PublicRoot, never Host. The client appends escaped relative paths below its one configured root. Error subjects have a separate prefix defect recorded on the request_path clause.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Binding Overview / HTTP API Patterns

requirements.text: If an OPTIONAL HTTP path is not supported by an implementation, then any use of that API MUST generate an error ([api_not_found](#api_not_found)).

review.note: The implementation supplies the listed optional administrative paths. Unsupported administrative subpaths produce HTTP 404 api_not_found. A supported but capability-disabled metadata API instead uses Core not_available; that distinction is deliberate and directly asserted.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Binding Overview / HTTP API Patterns

requirements.text: If an HTTP method is not supported for a supported HTTP path, then an error ([action_not_supported](./spec.md#action_not_supported)) MUST be generated.

review.note: TryAction, model-aware Allowed and the adapter reject unsupported verbs before body consumption. The catalog emits 405 action_not_supported and Allow; document PATCH uses the more specific details_required error.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Binding Overview / HTTP API Patterns

requirements.text: Implementations MAY support extension APIs, however, the following rules apply:

review.note: Permission to add APIs, not a requirement to provide an arbitrary extension-API facility. The mapped handler implements explicit registry routes and the defined shortself mechanism; extension path restrictions are reviewed in the following records.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Binding Overview / HTTP API Patterns

requirements.text: - New HTTP paths that extend non-root paths MUST NOT be defined as they might conflict with URLs of entities within the system.

review.note: No custom subordinate administrative API is registered. The adapter rejects /model/extra and similar paths, while RegistryPath permits only the defined entity, meta and versions shapes. Shortself navigation reuses canonical routes rather than adding arbitrary child APIs.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Binding Overview / HTTP API Patterns

requirements.text: - New root HTTP paths MAY be defined as long as they do not use Registry-level HTTP paths or attribute names. This includes extension and Groups collection attribute names.

review.note: Optional root-extension permission. No arbitrary root extension registry is adopted by MapXRegistry; independently mapped application APIs remain a host integration responsibility. This is not evidence that arbitrary host extensions have been collision-checked.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Binding Overview / Adherence to HTTP Standards

requirements.text: - A `PUT` or `POST` operation is a full replacement of the entities processed. Any missing attributes MUST be interpreted as a request for them to be deleted. However, attributes that are managed by the server might have specialized processing in those cases, in particular, mandatory attributes, as well as ones that have default values defined, MUST be reset to their default values rather than deleted.

review.note: Merge starts replacement metadata from an empty object, retains managed fields and then completes defaults. Document headers intentionally use PATCH-like metadata semantics. The complete PUT/POST omission-and-default matrix is not directly established by the existing HTTP assertions.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Binding Overview / Adherence to HTTP Standards

requirements.text: - A `PATCH` operation MUST only modify the attributes explicitly mentioned in the request. Any attribute in the request with a value of `null` MUST be interpreted as a request to delete the attribute, and as with `PUT`/`POST`, server-managed attributes might have specialized processing.

review.note: PATCH clones existing attributes, overwrites supplied complete values and lets completion remove nullable optional attributes. Missing values persist; server-managed epochs/timestamps and related lifecycle changes are not mistaken for forbidden side effects.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Binding Overview / Adherence to HTTP Standards

requirements.text: - `PUT` MUST NOT be targeted at xRegistry collections. A `POST` or `PATCH` MUST be used instead to add entities to the collection, and a `DELETE` MUST then be used to delete unwanted entities.

review.note: Allowed groups all three collection kinds into PATCH/POST/DELETE with no Replace action. The raw route matrix asserts PUT /teams is 405; collection mutation/deletion semantics are exercised through the public engine and actual Resource collection routes.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Binding Overview / Adherence to HTTP Standards

requirements.text: - Unknown query parameters SHOULD be silently ignored by servers. This includes specification-defined but unsupported query parameters.

review.note: HTTP-SEM-001 is fixed: only an enabled, recognized inline parameter marks an explicit override. Disabled inline is ignored on ordinary GET and cannot suppress mandatory export defaults. Actual MapXRegistry regression was red before the fix and the focused matrix passes on net8.0/net10.0.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Binding Overview / No-Code Servers

requirements.text: In the [core specification](./spec.md) there is a discussion about ["no-code servers"](./spec.md#design-no-code-servers). In the case of HTTP, simple file servers SHOULD support exposing Resources where the HTTP body response contains the Resource's domain-specific "document" as well as exposing the serialization of the Resource's xRegistry metadata via the [`$details`](#resource-metadata-vs-resource-document) suffix on the URL path. This can be achieved by creating a secondary, sibling, file on disk with `$details` at the end of its filename.

review.note: Conditional advice to no-code file-server producers. This HTTP review does not claim a static-file deployment or re-review the File specification. The actual dynamic host's Document/$details pairing is covered by the Resource representation records.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs

requirements.text: This section mainly focuses on the successful interaction patterns of the APIs. For example, most examples will show an HTTP "200 OK" as the response. Each implementation MAY choose to return a more appropriate response based on the specific situation. For example, in the case of an authentication error the server could return `401 Unauthorized`.

review.note: Success sketches do not override authentication, authorization, limits or uncertain commit outcomes. The host uses explicit 401/403/413/503 results; the client preserves error statuses without retries or success-shaped body substitution.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: Creating or updating entities MAY be done using HTTP `PUT`, `PATCH` or `POST` methods:

review.note: Introduces the five entity/collection mutation patterns. Their concrete body, dispatch and response obligations are reviewed separately below, rather than treating this introductory permission as additional executed evidence.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: See the [`Request Flags`](#request-flags--query-parameters) section for the list of flags/query parameters that MAY be used for each API.

review.note: Cross-reference to per-operation flag rules. RequestFlags and query/projection consumers were inspected; concrete flag syntax, applicability and defects are recorded under the flag clauses.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: The `PUT` variant MUST adhere to the following:

review.note: PUT umbrella introducing lines 222-235. The individual rules have their own decisions and gaps; this heading is not a separate claim that every PUT permutation has direct tests.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - The URL MUST be of the form: `<PATH-TO-ENTITY>`.

review.note: RegistryPath separates entity and collection shapes; Allowed does not grant PUT to collections. Client relative-path construction preserves the requested entity below the registry prefix.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - The HTTP body MUST contain the full updated serialization of the entity to be processed.

review.note: The adapter distinguishes a nonempty JSON metadata body from exact Document input, then Replace dispatches a full entity replacement. Body presence is directly tested, but complete metadata replacement of previously populated mutable attributes needs a direct operation vector.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - The entity processed MUST either be created (if it does not already exist), or updated (if it does exist).

review.note: EnsureGroup/EnsureResource and ApplyVersion select existing staged/snapshot identities or create new entities. Actual HTTP PUT creates a Resource, then updates the same identity and advances its epoch without creating another Version.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - Any mutable attribute which is either missing or present with a value of `null`, MUST be interpreted as a request to delete the attribute.

review.note: Metadata Replace builds a fresh mutable attribute map, and completion removes optional nulls. Existing null-deletion assertions concern PATCH/header semantics; they do not establish omitted-attribute deletion for metadata PUT.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - Excluding any Registry collection attributes, all mutable attributes specified MUST be a full serialization of the attribute. Any missing nested attribute MUST be interpreted as a request to delete the attribute.

review.note: Merge assigns each submitted complex value as one DeepClone, not a recursive merge. Scalar-map headers have direct replacement tests; nested metadata objects/arrays on entity PUT are a separate direct-evidence gap.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - After processing the request, if there are any missing REQUIRED attributes then an error ([required_attribute_missing](./spec.md#required_attribute_missing)) MUST be generated.

review.note: Complete checks required model attributes before publication and supplies required_attribute_missing with the affected entity and list argument. An actual HTTP Resource creation missing a required Version field asserts the exact error contract.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: The `PATCH` variant when directed at a single entity, MUST adhere to the `PUT` semantics defined above with the following exceptions:

review.note: PATCH umbrella. The following records review preserved omissions, null deletion, details_required and create-with-required-values independently.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - Any mutable attribute which is missing MUST be interpreted as a request to leave it unchanged. However, modifying some other attribute (or some other server semantics) MAY modify it. A value of `null` MUST be interpreted as a request to delete the attribute.

review.note: PATCH preserves omitted ordinary attributes and interprets explicit null as deletion. Required/default and generated-field semantics are applied during completion, not by inventing values in the client codec.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - When processing a Resource or Version, whose Resource type has its [`hasdocument`](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringhasdocument) model aspect set to `true`, the URL accessing the entity MUST include the `$details` suffix, and MUST generate an error ([details_required](#details_required)) in the absence of the `$details` suffix. This is because when it is absent, the processing of the HTTP `xRegistry-` headers are already defined with "PATCH" semantics so a normal `PUT` or `POST` can be used instead. Using `PATCH` in this case would mean that the request is trying to "patch" the Resource's "document", which this specification does not support at this time.

review.note: Allowed removes PATCH for document-bearing Resource/Version paths lacking $details, and the adapter returns the specific 405 details_required rather than attempting to patch bytes. Metadata-only types remain patchable without the suffix.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - `PATCH` MAY be used to create new entities, but as with any of the create operations, any missing REQUIRED attributes MUST generate an error ([required_attribute_missing](./spec.md#required_attribute_missing)).

review.note: PATCH shares Ensure/New and Complete with PUT, so creation is implemented and required fields are enforced. Existing required-field HTTP evidence is PUT, not PATCH creation.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: The `POST` variant when directed at a single entity other than a Resource, MUST adhere to the following:

review.note: Introduces POST-to-owner collection-map rules; supported owners are Registry and Group. Concrete map validation, unchanged owner metadata and response selection follow below.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - The HTTP body MUST contain only a JSON map where the key MUST be the attribute (collection) name of a nested xRegistry collection. The value of each map entry MUST be a map of nested entities where the key is the entity's `<SINGULAR>id` and the value is a serialization of the entity itself.

review.note: ApplyContainerAsync(collectionsOnly=true) accepts model collection names, and ApplyCollectionAsync requires ID-keyed object entries. Public engine tests assert the owner/collection envelope and reject ordinary owner attributes with groups_only/resources_only.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - The processing of each top-level map entry MUST follow the same rules as defined for `POST` to the nested xRegistry collection where the map entry's value is the input.

review.note: Each owner-map entry calls the same ApplyCollectionAsync implementation used by POST to that collection. Existing owner POST assertions do not compare mixed collection types against equivalent direct collection POST operations.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - The root of the JSON object in the HTTP body MUST NOT contain any attributes of the targeted entity other than the nested collections, and none of that entity's attribute are to be updated. This operation allows for an update to multiple nested collections in a single operation without modifying the owning entity.

review.note: collectionsOnly skips Merge on the owner and rejects noncollection attributes after requested ignore processing. Membership-driven counts/epochs remain Core-managed effects. Rejection is tested; preservation of a preexisting owner's ordinary attributes needs its own direct assertion.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - The response message MUST be a map of the nested entity types with just the changed entities that were processed. No top-level entity attributes are to appear - similar to the request message.

review.note: HTTP-SEM-002 is fixed: validated owner POST retains its normalized collection input for response selection, rather than re-reading raw configuration fields. Actual HTTP tests verify multiple Group collections, exact processed keys, unchanged ignored configuration and deterministic empty responses for only-ignored input.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: The `POST` variant when directed at a Resource entity, MUST adhere to the following:

review.note: Resource POST umbrella, distinct from POST to Registry/Group owners. The concrete single-Version body and PUT-like processing rules are reviewed next.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - The HTTP body MUST contain the serialization of the single Version to be created, however, it MAY include Resource-level read-only attributes (such as `versionscount`), and if they are present, then they MUST be silently ignored by the server. This is done as a convenience for users who might have obtained the Version's serialization from a query to a Resource (not a specific Version), in which case those extra Resource-level attributes would be included in the serialization.

review.note: Resource POST calls VersionInput and ApplyVersion for one Version; VersionInput strips read-only Resource projection fields. Existing POST tests use Version input, not a copied Resource response carrying versionscount/metaurl.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - The 'PUT' variant rules above MUST apply to the new Version entity.

review.note: Metadata Resource POST passes patch=false for the selected Version; Document mode preserves the special header PATCH semantics. Direct POST replacement of an existing explicitly selected Version is not asserted by the creation-focused tests.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: The `PATCH` variant when directed at an xRegistry collection, MUST adhere to the following:

review.note: Introduces collection PATCH. Individual keyed-map, subset-value and per-entity PATCH obligations are separately reviewed below.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - The HTTP body MUST contain a JSON map where the key MUST be the `<SINGULAR>id` of each entity in the map. Note, that in the case of a map of Versions, the `versionid` is used.

review.note: Collection PATCH parses a JSON object, derives each child path from its key and retains nested ID checks. Actual Resource collection PATCH asserts only the requested unlocked entry is returned; a wrong nested ID remains an error under ignore.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - Each value in the map MUST contain just the attributes that are to be updated for that entity.

review.note: Collection PATCH forwards partial entity objects with patch=true; it does not require a full entity serialization. Existing public operation and actual HTTP tests exercise partial name/rank changes without supplying generated attributes.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - The processing of each individual entity in the map MUST follow the same rules as defined for `PATCH` of a single entity above.

review.note: All three collection branches forward the PATCH selector to the same entity mutation routines. Direct subset/filter assertions cover Groups and Resources; Version collection omission/null/default behavior lacks an equivalent direct operation case.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: The `POST` variant when directed at an xRegistry collection MUST adhere to the following:

review.note: Collection POST umbrella; the following keyed-map, replacement and missing-Version requirements carry the behavioral decisions.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - The HTTP body MUST contain a JSON map where the key MUST be the `<SINGULAR>id` of each entity in the map. Note, that in the case of a map of Versions, the `versionid` is used.

review.note: Collection POST uses the same ID-keyed parser as collection PATCH. A real Resource collection POST creates locked/open entries and public engine Group POST creates separate a/b entries; Version keys are passed directly to ApplyVersion.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - Each value in the map MUST be the full serialization of the entity to be either added or updated. Note that `POST` does not support deleting entities from a collection, so a separate delete operation might be needed if there are entities that need to be removed.

review.note: ApplyCollectionAsync iterates supplied entries only and passes replacement semantics for POST; it never deletes omitted members. Membership retention is asserted, but replacing an existing member's omitted ordinary fields is not directly covered.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - The processing of each individual entity in the map MUST follow the same rules as defined for `PUT` above.

review.note: Collection POST invokes the same ApplyContainer/ApplyResource/ApplyVersion paths as PUT with patch=false. This is implementation evidence, not a substitute for the missing existing-member replacement comparison.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - In the case of an empty map of Versions and the Resource being referenced does not exist yet, an error ([missing_versions](#missing_versions)) MUST be generated because a Resource can not exist without any Versions. If the intent was to create a Resource with a Version that has just default values, then there are other APIs that can be used that make that intent clear (e.g. `PUT` to the Resource itself).

review.note: ApplyCollectionAsync explicitly throws missing_versions for an empty Version map when the owning Resource is absent. The matching 400 HTTP catalog entry exists. No direct existing test assertion for this exact absent-versus-existing boundary was found.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - If an entity with the specified `<SINGULAR>id` already exists then it MUST be interpreted as a request to update the existing entity. Otherwise, it MUST be interpreted as a request to create a new entity with that `<SINGULAR>id`.

review.note: Find/Ensure/New determines update versus creation from the canonical target identity. Escaped spellings share identity, while case-conflicting sibling IDs are rejected rather than creating ambiguous duplicates.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - Unless otherwise noted, all non-xRegistry collection attributes present MUST be a full representation of their values. This means any complex attributes (e.g. objects, maps), MUST be fully replaced by the incoming value.

review.note: Merge overwrites submitted attributes as complete values, including on PATCH. Header-map replacement is directly established, but a nested metadata object replacement is not proved by a scalar-map header test.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - A request to update, or delete, a read-only attribute MUST be silently ignored. However, a request that includes a `<SINGULAR>id` MUST be compared with the entity's current value and if it differs then an error ([mismatched_id](./spec.md#mismatched_id)) MUST be generated. This includes both `<RESOURCE>id` and `versionid` in the case of Resources and Versions. This is to prevent accidentally updating the wrong entity.

review.note: Ordinary read-only input is discarded before value validation, but engine Guard/CheckId preserves Resource ID and versionid comparisons. The header codec similarly retains identity/epoch guards, including exact large integers, instead of treating them as ignorable read-only fields.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - A request to update a mutable attribute with an invalid value MUST generate an error ([invalid_attribute](./spec.md#invalid_attribute)) (this includes deleting a mandatory mutable attribute that has no default value defined).

review.note: HTTP-SEM-003 is fixed and directly verified: explicit null removal of an existing required value reports invalid_attribute with the actual attribute name. Top-level/nested objects, array/map items, Version/projection and Document-header mutations preserve rollback. Initial absence or PUT omission keeps required_attribute_missing; defaults still reset. This is diagnostic classification, not permission to accept invalid state.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - Registry collection attributes MUST be processed per the rules specified in the [Updating Nested Registry Collections](./spec.md#updating-nested-registry-collections) section.

review.note: Nested registry collections are dispatched separately from ordinary attributes; supplied children are processed without replacing whole collections. Nested Version input takes precedence over the Resource default projection, and nested failures roll back the request.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - Write operations that are meant to include xRegistry metadata in the HTTP body MUST NOT be empty, and if detected MUST generate an error ([missing_body](#missing_body)). To denote an empty set of metadata, `{}` MUST be used instead.

review.note: The adapter reads bounded metadata bytes and rejects a zero-length write with missing_body; {} is a present JSON object. This rule is not applied to Document-mode writes, where an empty body is real content.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - Any error during the processing of an entity, or its nested entities, MUST result in the entire request being rejected and no updates performed.

review.note: The engine stages the entire mutation, authorizes affected descendants, validates content, renders and prepares headers before one persistence candidate is committed. Failures before publication have no effects. Transport failure after commit is explicitly not advertised as rollback or retried.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - When a write operation request includes the Resource/Version's metadata in the HTTP body, then the inclusion of any xRegistry `xRegistry-` HTTP headers MUST generate an error ([extra_xregistry_header](#extra_xregistry_header)).

review.note: All metadata-body writes reject any xRegistry-prefixed request header before parsing the body. The actual HTTP extra-header assertion targets a Group; the required Resource/Version $details combinations are not directly asserted through the server.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - When a write operation request includes a domain-specific document in the HTTP body, and the `<RESOURCE>url` xRegistry HTTP header is present with a non-null value, the HTTP body MUST be empty. If the `<RESOURCE>url` attribute is absent, then the contents of the HTTP body (even if empty) are to be used as the entity's document.

review.note: ApplyDocument requires an explicit external-reference policy and probes for an empty body when a non-null URL is supplied; otherwise it consumes even zero bytes as the Document. source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Resource Entity / Resource Metadata vs Resource Document

requirements.text: The core specification's [Resource Metadata vs Resource Document](./spec.md#resource-metadata-vs-resource-document) section explains how Resource types might be defined to have a domain-specific document associated with them via their [`hasdocument` model aspect](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringhasdocument) being set to `true`. For HTTP, clients indicate whether they want to interact with the Resource's xRegistry metadata or the Resource's domain-specific document by the use of a `$details` suffix on the `<RESOURCE>id` in its URL. Presence of the `$details` suffix MUST be interpreted as a request to interact with the xRegistry metadata of the Resource, while its absence MUST be interpreted as a request to interact with the Resource's domain-specific document.

review.note: Literal $details selects metadata for document-bearing Resource/Version paths; otherwise the exact domain Document is read/written. RegistryPath keeps suffix syntax distinct from an encoded dollar in an ID, and both actual HTTP representations are asserted.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Resource Entity / Resource Metadata vs Resource Document

requirements.text: Use of `$details` on a non-Resource entity MUST generate an error ([bad_details](./spec.md#bad_details)).

review.note: Suffix use on Group, collection, Meta and administrative shapes is rejected as bad_details. The later explicit Version APIs clarify that Version $details is supported; the shorthand 'non-Resource' sentence is not used to prohibit those Version routes.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Resource Entity / Resource Metadata vs Resource Document

requirements.text: If a Resource type does not support domain-specific documents (i.e. [`hasdocument`](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringhasdocument) is set to `false`), then use of the `$details` suffix in a request URL MUST be treated the same as if it were absent and any URLs in server response messages referencing that Resource (e.g. `self`) MUST NOT include it.

review.note: HasDocument=false bypasses Document mode even if $details was requested. Response self and navigation remain suffix-free. Actual metadata-only and shortself tests assert this and preserve arbitrary domain URL strings without rewriting them.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Resource Entity / Resource Metadata vs Resource Document / Serializing Resource Domain-Specific Documents

requirements.text: When a Resource is serialized as its underlying domain-specific document, in other words `$details` is not appended to its URL path, the HTTP body of requests and responses MUST be the exact bytes of that document. If the document is empty, then the HTTP body MUST be empty (zero length).

review.note: Document mode never parses or reformats domain bytes. Bounded upload, persisted read, prepared response and client copying preserve binary, JSON-looking and invalid-UTF8 payloads, including present zero length. Inline metadata serialization is a separate representation.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Resource Entity / Resource Metadata vs Resource Document / Serializing Resource Domain-Specific Documents

requirements.text: In this serialization mode, it might be useful for clients to also interact with some of the Resource's xRegistry metadata. To support this, some of the Resource's xRegistry metadata MAY appear as HTTP headers in messages.

review.note: The optional Document-plus-metadata-header facility is adopted by both client and server through the same explicit model-aware codec. Header reading does not consume the Document or trigger a model fetch; actual wire assertions independently establish the encoding.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Resource Entity / Resource Metadata vs Resource Document / Serializing Resource Domain-Specific Documents

requirements.text: On responses, unless otherwise stated, all top-level scalar attributes of the Resource SHOULD appear as HTTP headers where the header name is the name of the attribute prefixed with `xRegistry-`. Note, the optionality of this requirement is not to allow for servers to decide whether or not to do so, rather it is to allow for [No-Code Servers](#no-code-servers) that might not be able to control the HTTP response headers.

review.note: Response encoding enumerates top-level scalar metadata, including read-only and active conditional fields, using xRegistry- names except the standard Content-Type mapping. The dynamic host does not invoke the no-code exception to omit supported scalar metadata.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Resource Entity / Resource Metadata vs Resource Document / Serializing Resource Domain-Specific Documents

requirements.text: The `<RESOURCE>` and `<RESOURCEbase64>` attributes MUST NOT be serialized as HTTP headers, even if their values can be considered "scalar", because their values will appear in the HTTP body.

review.note: Response encoding excludes the singular Document and base64 fields before considering scalar types, so even scalar JSON content cannot leak into a duplicate metadata header. Their payload remains in the HTTP body.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Resource Entity / Resource Metadata vs Resource Document / Serializing Resource Domain-Specific Documents

requirements.text: Top-level map attributes whose values are of scalar types SHOULD also appear as HTTP headers (each key having its own HTTP header) and in those cases the HTTP header names will be of the form: `xRegistry-<MAPNAME>.<KEYNAME>`. Note that map keys MAY contain the `.` character, so any `.` after the `<MAPNAME>.` is part of the key name. See [HTTP Header Values](#http-header-values) for additional information and [`labels`](#labels-attribute) for an example of one such attribute.

review.note: Scalar-valued maps emit one field per member and decode only the first dot as the map separator. Remaining dots and percent signs belong to the key, not a path or second decoding pass. Named conditional maps take precedence over active wildcards.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Resource Entity / Resource Metadata vs Resource Document / Serializing Resource Domain-Specific Documents

requirements.text: Complex top-level attributes (e.g. arrays, objects, non-scalar maps) MUST NOT appear as HTTP headers.

review.note: Complex response arrays/objects/non-scalar maps are omitted; attempts to send their values as request headers fail before dispatch. A null deletion sentinel is not a serialized complex value. An any-typed object does not become a JSON string header.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Resource Entity / Resource Metadata vs Resource Document / Serializing Resource Domain-Specific Documents

requirements.text: On update requests, similar serialization rules apply. However, rather than these headers being REQUIRED, the client would only need to include those top-level attributes that they would like to change. But, including unchanged attributes MAY be done. Unless otherwise stated, any attributes not included in request messages MUST be interpreted as a request to leave their values unchanged. Using a value of `null` (case-sensitive) MUST be processed as a request to delete that attribute.

review.note: Document header writes preserve omitted metadata, allow unchanged writable discriminator context and interpret exactly lowercase decoded null as deletion. Null, empty and absent are distinct. A literal request string null requires $details; quoting or percent-encoding does not invent an escape from the frozen sentinel.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Resource Entity / Resource Metadata vs Resource Document / Serializing Resource Domain-Specific Documents

requirements.text: Any top-level map attributes that appear as HTTP headers MUST be included in their entirety and any missing keys MUST be interpreted as a request to delete those keys from the map.

review.note: The codec assembles supplied map members into one complete map, and Merge replaces the old map even though other Document metadata is patch-like. Actual HTTP assertions prove old map keys disappear while supplied empty-string values persist.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Resource Entity / Resource Metadata vs Resource Document / Serializing Resource Domain-Specific Documents

requirements.text: Since only some types of attributes can appear as HTTP headers, in order to manage the full set of attributes, the xRegistry metadata view (via use of the `$details` URL suffix) MUST be used instead.

review.note: $details plus SendAsync remains the full-metadata route. Literal null strings, empty maps, non-string any values and complex values are explicitly directed there, without synthetic escaping, default context, extra GETs or replay. Missing conditional context is a named error, not evidence that conditional scalars/maps are unsupported.

If supported, the Registry-based discovery file, for an HTTP server, MUST be available at the root of the Registry (e.g. as a sibling API to `/model`) via the `/.xregistry` API:

review.note: Registry-based discovery is .xregistry below the configured root, distinct from explicitly selected host /.well-known/xregistry. Both actual client destinations are asserted; unavailable registry discovery does not trigger a hidden host probe, and advertisements do not authorize fetching peers.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Request Flags / Query Parameters

requirements.text: The [core xRegistry specification](./spec.md) defines a set of [request flags](./spec.md#request-flags) that MAY be used to control the processing of requests as well as influence how response messages are generated. Each flag is mapped to an HTTP query parameter per the following rules:

review.note: Introduces HTTP serialization of Core flags. The following records separately evaluate null flags, singleton parameters, repeated values and the filter/ignore/inline/sort exceptions; no aggregate test count is used to close them.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Request Flags / Query Parameters

requirements.text: - When the flag is a boolean type of flag then it MUST be serialized as `?FLAG_NAME`, all lower case.

review.note: Client query pairs with null values serialize as bare flags, distinct from an empty value's equals sign. Callers supply the specified lower-case names; the server matches known flag names case-sensitively rather than normalizing arbitrary extension keys. Actual doc/binary flags affect projection.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Request Flags / Query Parameters

requirements.text: - When the flag has a single value associated with it, then it MUST be serialized as `?FLAG_NAME=VALUE`, where the `FLAG_NAME` MUST be all lower case. The flag MUST NOT be specified more than once.

review.note: BuildUri emits lower-case caller-supplied names with escaped =VALUE values; RequestFlags tracks recognized singletons and rejects repetitions. Existing raw tests assert valued flags and invalid values, but not duplicate singleton query rejection through the host.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Request Flags / Query Parameters

requirements.text: - When the flag allows for multiple values, then each value MUST be serialized as a separate query parameter per the previous bullets.

review.note: The client retains ordered repeated pairs, and ParseQuery produces one entry per field instead of collapsing values. Actual wire assertions preserve repeated filter values; actual filter OR and repeated ignore tests prove the server consumes repeats with their defined exceptions.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Request Flags / Query Parameters / `?filter` Flag

requirements.text: A server MAY support the `?filter` query parameter allowing clients to reduce the response entities to just the ones that match certain criteria.

review.note: filter is enabled and uses the shared Core QueryPlan/Evaluation over authorized logical facts before rendering. Independent raw tests assert selected IDs and typed comparisons; it is not a pass-through flag or a silent empty result for malformed supported queries.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Request Flags / Query Parameters / `?filter` Flag

requirements.text: This query parameter MUST be serialized as:

review.note: The client URI-encodes filter values once; the host decodes one UTF-8 query pass before the Core grammar splits conjunctions. Actual requests carry escaped operators/commas and return independently expected records.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Request Flags / Query Parameters / `?filter` Flag

requirements.text: - All `<EXPRESSION>` values within the scope of one `?filter` query parameter MUST be evaluated as a logical `AND` per the [core specification](./spec.md#filter-flag).

review.note: QueryPlan groups comma-separated expressions into one branch, and Evaluation intersects matching subtree leaves within that branch. Direct tests prove conjunction does not combine different sibling witnesses and that counts/inline results reflect the intersection.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Request Flags / Query Parameters / `?filter` Flag

requirements.text: - The `?filter` query parameter MAY appear multiple times and if so MUST be evaluated as a logical `OR` with the other `?filter` query parameters that appear - per the [core specification](./spec.md#filter-flag).

review.note: Repeated filter parameters become separate branches whose matches are unioned in a HashSet, not ANDed or concatenated with duplicates. Selection drives child membership and URL/count projection; direct raw and subtree tests assert the resulting union independently.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Request Flags / Query Parameters / `?ignore` Flag

requirements.text: A server MAY support the `?ignore` query parameter on any write operation to indicate that certain aspects of the request message MUST be ignored by the server.

review.note: HTTP-SEM-002 is fixed by reusing normalized owner input, not by weakening ignore or validation. Actual tests cover ignored invalid configuration, partial/unignored configuration rejection, disabled-ignore rejection, only-ignored authenticated writes, descendant denial and invalid-child atomic rollback.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Request Flags / Query Parameters / `?ignore` Flag

requirements.text: This query parameter MUST be serialized as:

review.note: RequestFlags accepts bare ignore, empty value and '*' as the enabled ignore set, plus comma-separated named values. Direct engine cases assert each alias skips readonly entries while retaining nested identity checks; the client preserves bare versus empty wire syntax.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Request Flags / Query Parameters / `?ignore` Flag

requirements.text: - The `?ignore` query parameter MAY be specified more than once.

review.note: Repeated ignore fields union their supported values. The actual HTTP request contains ignore=readonly and ignore=epoch and proves the unlocked Resource changes despite a stale epoch while the locked Resource is omitted and remains protected.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Request Flags / Query Parameters / `?inline` Flag

requirements.text: A server MAY support the `?inline` query parameter on any request to indicate which nested collections/objects, or potentially large attributes, are to be included in the response message.

review.note: inline controls nested collections, meta, configuration and Document projection through ValidateInline/Includes/Child. Supported explicit inline works in actual HTTP queries. Ordinary extension objects are not falsely treated as separately inlineable entities.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Request Flags / Query Parameters / `?inline` Flag

requirements.text: This query parameter MUST be serialized as:

review.note: The client can emit bare inline or an escaped path list; the host treats absent/empty inline value as '*' and validates model-relative paths. Actual requests exercise explicit inline paths and wildcard projection, while invalid name inlining returns the exact Core error.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Request Flags / Query Parameters / `?inline` Flag

requirements.text: - The value portion of the `?inline` query parameter MAY Include a single `<PATH>` value or be a comma-separated list of `<PATH>` values.

review.note: RequestFlags splits a supplied inline value on commas, and projection handles each requested path with implicit collection ancestors. Actual HTTP requests assert simultaneous meta and versions.schema inlining, not just one path.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Request Flags / Query Parameters / `?inline` Flag

requirements.text: - The `?inline` query parameter MAY be specified more than once.

review.note: Each repeated inline field appends paths and Includes/Child evaluates their union. The inspected tests cover comma lists and generic repeated query transport, but not multiple actual inline fields selecting different branches.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Request Flags / Query Parameters / `?sort` Flag

requirements.text: A server MAY support the `?sort` query parameter on any request directed to a collection of Groups, Resources or Versions.

review.note: QueryPlan allows sorting only direct Group, Resource and Version collections and rejects owner sorting. Direct tests establish Group scalar ordering and Resource meta sorting; an explicit Version collection sort operation is not directly evidenced.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Request Flags / Query Parameters / `?sort` Flag

requirements.text: This query parameter MUST be serialized as:

review.note: sort is serialized as one attribute expression with optional =asc/desc; the host decodes it once and QueryExpression validates a known scalar projection/direction. Actual HTTP uses escaped rank=desc and checks returned order; direct cases cover default direction and invalid projections.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Header Values

requirements.text: Some attributes can contain arbitrary UTF-8 string content, and per [RFC7230, section 3][rfc7230-section-3], HTTP headers MUST only use printable characters from the US-ASCII character set, and are terminated by a CRLF sequence with OPTIONAL whitespace around the header value.

review.note: Header encoding produces printable ASCII; the decoder rejects unencoded controls/non-ASCII and handles optional transport whitespace. PreparedResponse validates emitted fields before publication, and Kestrel/HttpClient own HTTP CRLF framing rather than concatenating decoded attribute text into fields.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Header Values

requirements.text: When encoding an attribute's value as an HTTP header, it MUST be percent-encoded as described below. This is compatible with [RFC3986, section 2.1][rfc3986-section-2-1] but is more specific about what needs encoding. The resulting string SHOULD NOT be further encoded. (Rationale: quoted string escaping is unnecessary when every space and double-quote character is already percent-encoded.)

review.note: RegistryHeaderEncoding encodes spaces, quotes, percent and nonprintable/non-ASCII UTF-8 bytes once, with no added quoted-string layer. Literal independent HTTP assertions cover percent, controls and Unicode. Standard Content-Type retains its separate HTTP media-type syntax, as reviewed on its dedicated clause.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Header Values

requirements.text: When decoding an HTTP header into an attribute's value, any HTTP header value MUST first be unescaped with respect to double-quoted strings, as described in [RFC7230, section 3.2.6][rfc7230-section-3-2-6]. A single round of percent-decoding MUST then be performed as described below. HTTP headers for attribute values do not support parenthetical comments, so the initial unescaping only needs to handle double-quoted values, including processing backslash escapes within double-quoted values. Header values produced via the percent-encoding described here will never include double-quoted values, but they MUST be supported when receiving events, for compatibility with older versions of this specification which did not require double-quote and space characters to be percent-encoded.

review.note: Legacy quoted strings are unescaped before exactly one percent-decoding pass; backslash escapes inside quotes are handled and parentheses are not stripped as comments. Tests prove %2520 remains %20 and quoted/encoded null cannot become a request literal-string escape.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Header Values

requirements.text: Percent encoding is performed by considering each Unicode character within the attribute's canonical string representation. Any character represented in memory as a [Unicode surrogate pair][surrogate-pair] MUST be treated as a single Unicode character. The following characters MUST be percent-encoded:

review.note: Strict UTF-8 conversion treats a valid surrogate pair as one Unicode scalar before byte percent encoding; lone surrogates fail. The required character set and exact encoded-byte limits are independently asserted, including boundary-plus-one failure.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Header Values

requirements.text: Percent-encoding SHOULD be performed using upper-case for values A-F, but decoding MUST accept lowercase values.

review.note: The encoder uses a fixed uppercase hex alphabet; HexValue accepts both cases. Independent lower-case UTF-8 input vectors and an actual host request prove decoding is not accidentally uppercase-only.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Header Values

requirements.text: When performing percent-decoding, values that have been unnecessarily percent-encoded MUST be accepted, but encoded byte sequences which are invalid in UTF-8 MUST generate an error ([header_error](#header_error)). For example, "%C0%A0" is an overlong encoding of U+0020, and would be rejected.

review.note: Unnecessary valid escapes are decoded, but strict UTF-8 rejects overlong, surrogate, out-of-range and truncated sequences. The host converts codec errors into the HTTP header_error catalog with the actual header name and rejects publication.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.required`

requirements.text: - When set to `true`, this specification does not mandate how this attribute's value is populated (i.e. by a client, the server or via a default value), just that by the end of the server's processing of any request it MUST have a non-null value, and generate an error ([invalid_attribute](./spec.md#invalid_attribute)) if not. Note that this implies that a REQUIRED attribute does not mean that clients are mandated to include that attribute in their requests. If the attribute will automatically be populated by the server (e.g. it has a default value defined) the client MAY omit it.

review.note: ClientInput permits omission until server completion/defaulting. The parent's current diagnostic fix now reports invalid_attribute for explicit null deletion of an existing required value; direct tests verify no publication. Creation/replacement omissions still report required_attribute_missing, and defaults still reset successfully. The earlier claim that all required failures are normalized alike is withdrawn.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.required`

requirements.text: - A `true` value also implies that this attribute MUST be serialized in any response from the server - with the exception of the optimizations specified for [document view](./spec.md#registry-model).

review.note: Completed metadata retains required/defaulted values, and normal render paths clone them; document view intentionally omits the Resource's default-Version projection. Tests separately assert a populated default and the document-view omission, but do not enumerate every required attribute across all server response shapes.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.required`

requirements.text: - When not specified the default value MUST be `false`.

review.note: Required defaults false for new definitions. The optional-parent test successfully omits an object whose own required aspect is absent; required child/default processing occurs only when that object exists.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.required`

requirements.text: - When the attribute name is `*` then `required` MUST NOT be set to `true`.

review.note: Required:true on * is rejected by the dedicated wildcard aspect guard. The exact-path model table directly asserts model_error for that prohibited combination.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.required`

requirements.text: - When a default value (`attributes.<STRING>.default`) is defined, then this aspect MUST be `true`, otherwise an error ([model_required_true](./spec.md#model_required_true)) MUST be generated.

review.note: A non-null default requires required:true; omission of required does not silently promote it. Core asserts model_required_true at the required pointer, and the engine contract test preserves the model-specific error and attribute name without publishing.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.default`

requirements.text: - Type: MUST be a non-`null` value of the type specified by the `attributes.<STRING>.type` model attribute and MUST only be used for scalar types. Attempts to define a `default` value for a non-scalar type MUST generate an error ([model_scalar_default](./spec.md#model_scalar_default)).

review.note: Non-null defaults are restricted to scalar types and checked without numeric narrowing; nonscalar defaults yield model_scalar_default. The later null/absence paragraph is honored: explicit default:null means no default, not a stored null default. Tests cover nonscalar, fractional integer and large exact defaults.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.default`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

review.note: A default may be absent; explicit null is also absence in the compiled definition while the original Source keeps the explicit null. The ownership/presence test checks both representations rather than equating null with an empty string or zero.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.default`

requirements.text: - This value MUST be used to populate this attribute's value if one was not provided by a client. An attribute with a default value does not mean that its owning Object is mandated to be present; rather the attribute would only appear when the owning Object is present. By default, attributes have no default values.

review.note: Validator.Object inserts defaults only in completed, present objects and before required checks/conditional activation. Core tests distinguish an omitted optional parent from present empty/null-child cases. The current server test additionally null-resets existing top-level/nested required values and directly observes fallback after the diagnostic fix.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.default`

requirements.text: - When a default value is specified, this attribute MUST be serialized in responses from servers as part of its owning entity, even if it is set to its default value. This means that any attribute that has a default value defined MUST also have its `required` aspect set to `true`.

review.note: Defaulted attributes must be required in the model and remain explicit values in normalized metadata. Tests read back the actual default, including a Group-constraint-supplied value from an engine response; this is not inferred from a successful compile alone.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.default`

requirements.text: - If the default value of an attribute changes over time, all existing instances of that attribute MUST retain their current values and not be automatically changed to the new default value. In other words, a new default value MUST only apply to new or subsequent updates (when set to `null`, which would reset it to the current default value) of existing instances of the attribute.

review.note: Default application only replaces absent/null values, so existing non-null values survive model revalidation; a later null reset uses the current definition. Existing tests cover default insertion, not a model-default change followed by retained old values and an explicit reset.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.default`

requirements.text: - If the attribute is defined to have an `enum` list, and its `strict` aspect is `true`, then if a `default` value is specified it MUST be one of those `enum` values.

review.note: After reading enum/default, CompileAttribute checks the effective default with Allowed. The direct string c versus enum [a,b] case fails, and the shared exact scalar comparator avoids floating-point equivalence errors for numeric values.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.attributes`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

review.note: Nested object attributes are optional and compile to an empty set when omitted; explicit maps recursively compile. Nested-object tests cover present definitions, but no direct successful empty or omitted child-definition map assertion was found.

requirements.text: - MAY be present when the owning attribute's `type` is `object`, otherwise it MUST NOT be present. It MAY be absent or an empty list if there are no defined attributes for the nested `object`.

review.note: A non-null attributes aspect is accepted only on object; the compiler rejects attributes:{} on string. Empty/absent object maps are supported in source, but the compound permission has no direct positive empty-map assertion alongside the tested invalid placement.

review.note: Item describes the nested array element or map value; a string-typed owner with item is rejected at /item. The compiled nested array-of-map-of-object test observes the ultimate x:string definition rather than merely successful parsing.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.item.item`

requirements.text: - REQUIRED when `item.type` is `map` or `array`.

review.note: Recursive collection items require their own item definition, using the same array/map guard. A nested array/map/object chain is directly inspected; the negative missing-item assertion is only at the first collection level, so recursive rejection evidence is incomplete.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.ifvalues`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

review.note: Ifvalues is optional; definitions without it retain an empty branch dictionary and ordinary typed validation proceeds without conditional siblings. The exact scalar tests exercise this nonconditional path, while absent branches never enable undeclared attributes.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.ifvalues`

requirements.text: - This map can be used to conditionally include additional attribute definitions based on the runtime value of the current attribute. If the string serialization of the runtime value of this attribute matches the `ifvalues` key (case-insensitive), then the `siblingattributes` MUST be included in the model as siblings to this attribute.

review.note: RESOLVED MODEL-REV-001: Retained top-level PATCH discriminator context is explicitly supplied to ClientInput validation. Submitted discriminator changes/null, readonly values, nested object replacement, defaults and subsequent complete validation retain their original rules. No HTTP prefetch or implicit partial-header context is introduced.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.ifvalues`

requirements.text: While maps will automatically prevent two entries with the same key, they will not prevent two entries that only differ in case. Therefore, during a model update, servers MUST ensure that no two entries are the same irrespective of case, otherwise an error ([model_error](./spec.md#model_error)) MUST be generated.

review.note: Conditional branch keys use an OrdinalIgnoreCase dictionary and are checked before insertion. The direct A/a case produces model_error at the second branch; JSON duplicate-name rejection is a separate earlier ingestion check, not a replacement for case-folded uniqueness.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.ifvalues`

requirements.text: If attribute's `enum` aspect is not empty and its `strict` aspect is `true` then this map MUST NOT contain any value that is not specified in the `enum` array.

review.note: Nonempty strict enums restrict branch keys using the scalar's string serialization and case-insensitive comparison. The direct enum [x] with branch y case is rejected. Numeric and timestamp serialization variants are not directly asserted, so this evidence supports the tested string discriminator rather than every scalar representation.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.ifvalues`

requirements.text: This aspect MUST only be used for scalar attributes.

review.note: Ifvalues requires ModelTypes.IsScalar; any, object, array and map are excluded by that guard. The aspect table directly rejects ifvalues:{} on a map with a valid item, isolating conditional eligibility from missing-item errors.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.ifvalues`

requirements.text: All attributes defined for this `ifvalues` MUST be unique within the scope of this `ifvalues` and MUST NOT match a named attribute defined at this level of the entity. If multiple `ifvalues` sections, at the same entity level, are active at the same time then there MUST NOT be duplicate `ifvalues` attribute names between those `ifvalues` sections and a runtime error ([invalid_attribute](./spec.md#invalid_attribute)) MUST be generated.

review.note: CheckConditionalNames prevents static/conditional collisions recursively; active independent branches use TryAdd and report invalid_attribute. Tests directly reject a static a collision and assert duplicate reading from two active branches for validator and header codec. Cross-plane reserved names remain the separate compiler defect.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.ifvalues`

requirements.text: - `ifvalues` `<STRING>` MUST NOT be an empty string.

review.note: CompileAttribute explicitly rejects an empty discriminator key before indexing its first character. The exact invalid-aspect case asserts model_error at /attributes/a/ifvalues/, so an empty key cannot become an always-active branch.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.ifvalues`

requirements.text: - `ifvalues` `<STRING>` MUST NOT start with the `^` (caret) character as its presence at the beginning of `<STRING>` is reserved for future use.

review.note: Caret-prefixed conditional keys are rejected, not interpreted as a regex or future matching operator. The ^future test checks the exact branch pointer and model_error.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.ifvalues`

requirements.text: - `ifvalues` `siblingattributes` MAY include additional `ifvalues` definitions.

review.note: Conditional siblings can themselves discriminate further siblings; the shared queue processes them rather than stopping after one level. The nested fixture asserts exact decimal, map and readonly semantics, with explicit depth/node rejection in header lookup. Server partial-state use is not covered by those core/helper assertions.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups`

requirements.text: - Type: Map where the key MUST be the plural name (`groups.plural`) of the Group type (`<GROUPS>`) being defined.

review.note: Group map keys determine plural names; an explicit different plural is rejected. The abbreviated specification sample omits redundant plural, and the compiler supplies it only in EffectiveModel. Tests assert both the source omission and effective value.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups`

requirements.text: - REQUIRED if there are any Group types defined for the Registry.

review.note: Groups may be absent when there are no Group types; every effective model writes a groups map. An empty source under a one-node expansion budget is directly asserted to produce zero groups, while the independent model proves declared groups are represented.

A model replacement may remove an unused type and add another; this is not automatically a rename. No direct lifecycle assertion distinguishes permitted type replacement from prohibited identity mutation.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.plural`

review.note: A shared ordinal peer-name set covers Group plural and singular names; Core's lowercase grammar removes case ambiguity. The direct two-Group case where one plural equals the other's singular is rejected, instead of relying only on JSON map-key uniqueness.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.plural`

requirements.text: - MUST be non-empty and MUST be a valid attribute name with the exception that it MUST NOT exceed 57 characters (not 63).

review.note: CheckNames uses the strict attribute grammar with a 57-character Group-plural ceiling, not the general 63-character limit. The direct test accepts exactly 57 and rejects 58 at the plural pointer.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.singular`

requirements.text: - REQUIRED.

review.note: Singular is not inferred by English inflection: CheckNames requires a supplied valid string. Positive singular identity is directly asserted, but missing/null/non-string singular cases are not directly exercised in the inspected model tests.

review.note: RESOLVED MODEL-REV-006: Model replacement compares retained Group/Resource plural identities and rejects changes to their immutable singular names even when no instances exist. Rejection preserves the prior model and persistence generation.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.singular`

requirements.text: - MUST be unique across all Group types (plural and singular names) in the Registry.

review.note: The Group singular shares the same peer-name set as plural, so cross-kind collisions across Group types fail. The direct a/as collision test observes this rather than just duplicate object-key rejection.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.singular`

requirements.text: - MUST be non-empty and MUST be a valid attribute name. For clarity, it MUST NOT exceed 63 characters.

review.note: The Group singular uses strict name grammar and the explicitly stated 63-character ceiling, unlike Group plural/Resource singular. The test accepts 63 and rejects 64 with the precise singular diagnostic path.

requirements.text: These restrictions are designed to only allow subsetting of the constraints specified by the Resource type model. They MUST NOT be used to extend the allowable values of the attributes being constrained.

review.note: CompileConstraints checks candidate defaults/enums against the scalar's type and strict base enum; GroupForValidation additionally rejects widening a Group-model constraint. Direct compiler and engine cases prove invalid expansion is rejected and the previous constraint survives a failed update.
