requirements.text: The format of a constraint map MUST adhere to the following:

review.note: The complete displayed constraint shape is implemented as an object keyed by Resource-plus-path, with only default, enum and equals aspects. Tests inspect all three compiled aspects and reject an unknown member or non-array enum.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.constraints`

requirements.text: These constraints MUST be applied to all instances of this Group type. Group instances MAY choose to add additional entries, or further restrict the ones defined here, via use of the Group instance's [`constraints` attribute](./spec.md#constraints-attribute).

review.note: RESOLVED MODEL-REV-003: The final-candidate xref constraint gate now applies the shared pure enum/equals checker to every retained target Version and reverse target/Group/model updates. It uses bounded indexed collection traversal, honors one-hop/dangling behavior, applies no referring defaults, checks forward read authorization before values and avoids disclosing private alias identities in reverse diagnostics. RESOLVED MODEL-REV-010: Empty instance enum/equals facets are treated as absent before merging with inherited constraints. They neither widen nor replace the inherited restriction; omitted/null/empty forms have equivalent enforcement, and stored instance metadata is not mutated by normalization.

It uses bounded indexed collection traversal, honors one-hop/dangling behavior, applies no referring defaults, checks forward read authorization before values and avoids disclosing private alias identities in reverse diagnostics.

It uses bounded indexed collection traversal, honors one-hop/dangling behavior, applies no referring defaults, checks forward read authorization before values and avoids disclosing private alias identities in reverse diagnostics.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.constraints`

requirements.text: - The `default` values specified MUST NOT be applied to the Resource since its presence in the Group is just a "reference" (or "read-only"). Write operations on the Resource need to be done in its original location.

review.note: Constraint defaults are not applied through an xref: the alias has no local Version finalization, and writes through its target projection are rejected. That avoids modifying the original Resource, but no direct test checks a conflicting referring-Group default leaves target bytes/metadata untouched.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.constraints.<RESOURCES>.<PATH>`

requirements.text: This map key MUST reference the Resource attribute that is to be constrained. It MUST reference a scalar attribute (top-level, or nested within objects) but MUST NOT reference items in arrays or maps. It MUST only reference statically-defined attributes, not ones that are dynamically added via an `ifvalues` clause or via a `*` extension definition.

review.note: ModelPaths.ResolveAttribute walks only static dictionaries and requires object intermediates plus a final scalar; maps, arrays, wildcard names and ifvalues-only names are not resolvable. Current constraint tests do not directly exercise this complete forbidden-path matrix.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.constraints.<RESOURCES>.<PATH>`

requirements.text: The `<RESOURCES>` portion of the map key MUST be the plural name of the Resource type being referenced.

review.note: CompileConstraints resolves the first path component only through the Resource dictionary's plural key. A positive schemas.format test observes ResourceType/attribute-path separation, but no direct singular-instead-of-plural or unknown-Resource assertion was found.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.constraints.<RESOURCES>.<PATH>`

requirements.text: The `<PATH>` portion of the map key MUST be a [dot (`.`) notation](spec.md#xregistry-dot--notation) traversal to the Resource attribute being constrained.

review.note: The local path parser supports dot access and single/double-quoted brackets with quote/backslash escapes, while rejecting array-index syntax for constraints. The referenced full dot-notation table was read; direct quoted Resource-path and malformed-operator assertions are missing.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.constraints.<RESOURCES>.<PATH>.default`

requirements.text: This aspect defines the default value that MUST be used for the referenced Resource attribute. This Group type value MUST override any default value specified in the model for that attribute.

review.note: Group constraint defaults are applied before attribute defaults and only inside present owners; the Resource definition is not mutated and need not become required. Compiler tests preserve the base default and inspect the override; the engine test observes the populated constrained value.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.constraints.<RESOURCES>.<PATH>.default`

requirements.text: Note, if the constraint does not define a new `enum` set, but a `default` value is defined, then if the referenced attribute has an `enum` set and has its `strict` aspect set to `true` then this `default` value MUST be one of those `enum` values.

review.note: A constraint default is checked against the referenced scalar's strict enum even without a constraint enum. The direct default:outside case uses the base [a,b] enum and rejects compilation, so a Group default cannot widen the Resource definition.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.constraints.<RESOURCES>.<PATH>.enum`

requirements.text: This aspect defines the set of values that the referenced Resource attribute MUST be restricted to regardless of whether the Resource's [`strict`](#attributesstringstrict) attribute is set to `true` or not. The list's values MUST be valid per the Resource attribute's model definition (i.e. a proper subset of any `enum` defined if the Resource's `enum` is [`strict`](#attributesstringstrict), and of the same type).

review.note: Constraint enum members must have the scalar type and belong to a strict base enum; at runtime a nonempty constraint enum is enforced regardless of the attribute's Strict flag. Base-subset rejection is directly tested, but strict:false base attributes with restrictive Group enums are not.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.constraints.<RESOURCES>.<PATH>.enum`

requirements.text: As with the [`enum` attribute](#attributesstringenum) defined for attributes, an empty `enum` list in a constraint MUST be treated the same as no `enum` aspect at all and no further constraints on the allowable attribute values are applied beyond what the attribute itself defines.

review.note: RESOLVED MODEL-REV-010: Empty instance enum/equals facets are treated as absent before merging with inherited constraints. They neither widen nor replace the inherited restriction; omitted/null/empty forms have equivalent enforcement, and stored instance metadata is not mutated by normalization.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.constraints.<RESOURCES>.<PATH>.enum`

requirements.text: If an `enum` set is defined, but a constraint `default` value is not, then any `default` value specified in the attribute itself MUST be part of the `enum` set.

review.note: CompileConstraints selects the constraint default when present, otherwise the attribute default, then requires it to belong to a nonempty constraint enum. The direct enum:[b] case with inherited default a fails instead of silently discarding/changing the default.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.constraints.<RESOURCES>.<PATH>.equals`

review.note: RESOLVED MODEL-REV-003: The final-candidate xref constraint gate now applies the shared pure enum/equals checker to every retained target Version and reverse target/Group/model updates. It uses bounded indexed collection traversal, honors one-hop/dangling behavior, applies no referring defaults, checks forward read authorization before values and avoids disclosing private alias identities in reverse diagnostics.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.constraints.<RESOURCES>.<PATH>.equals`

review.note: FinalizeResource orders/prunes one Version at a time, rebuilding ancestry; it skips the selected default except at limit one. Tests prove limit-two deletion/rerooting and limit-one replacement after compatibility checking, but not all versionmode, tie and sticky-default pruning combinations in this compound algorithm.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.versionmode`

requirements.text: - `manual` - Newest Version: MUST be determined by finding all Versions that are not referenced as an `ancestor` of another Version, then finding the one with the newest `createdat` timestamp. If there is more than one, then the one with the highest alphabetically case-insensitive `versionid` value MUST be chosen. - Oldest Version: MUST be determined by finding all root Versions (ones that have an `ancestorid` value that points to itself), then finding the one with the oldest `createdat` timestamp. If there is more than one, then the one with the lowest alphabetically case-insensitive `versionid` MUST be chosen. - Ancestor Processing: typically provided by clients. During a "create" operation, all new Versions that do not have an `ancestorid` value provided MUST be sorted/processed by `versionid` (in case-insensitive ascending order) and the `ancestorid` value of each MUST be set to the current "newest Version" per the above semantics. Note that as each new Version is created, it MUST become the "newest". If there is no existing Version then the new Version becomes a root and its `ancestorid` value MUST be its own `versionid` attribute value. - Deleted Ancestor: if a Version's ancestor is deleted, then this Version MUST become a root, and its `ancestorid` value MUST be set to its own `versionid` value. - The name of this versionmode is a bit of a misnomer in that it is not 100% "manual". As stated above, as a convenience, by default new Versions will point to the "newest" Version as their ancestor. If this behavior is not desired, then during the "create" operation, the `ancestorid` can be set to point to itself (or any other Version) if desired.

review.note: All manual subclauses were read: newest leaf, oldest root, createdat/ID ties, sorted implicit creations, self-root initialization and reroot after deletion. Source implements these paths using ordinal-ignore-case ID ordering. Tests prove ordinary chains/deletion, not multi-root backdated batches or every tie/pruning case.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.versionmode`

requirements.text: - `createdat` - Newest Version: MUST be determined by finding the Version with the newest `createdat` timestamp. If there is more than one, then the one with the highest alphabetically case-insensitive `versionid` value MUST be chosen. - Oldest Version: MUST be determined by finding the Version with the oldest `createdat` timestamp. If there is more than one, then the one with the lowest alphabetically case-insensitive `versionid` value MUST be chosen. Note that this MUST also be the one and only "root" Version. - Ancestor Processing: The `ancestorid` value of each Version MUST be determined via examination of the `createdat` timestamp of each Version and the Versions sorted in ascending order, where the first one will be the "root" (oldest) Version and its `ancestorid` value MUST be its `versionid`. If there is more than one Version with the same `createdat` timestamp then those MUST be ordered in ascending case-insensitive order based on their `versionid` values. - Deleted Ancestor: if a Version's ancestor is deleted, then this Version's `ancestorid` value MUST be determined by the "ancestor processing" logic as stated above. - When this `versionmode` is used, the `singleversionroot` aspect MUST be set to `true`.

review.note: Createdat ordering builds a single sorted chain, self-points the oldest root and chooses the last Version as newest, using exact normalized timestamp fractions and ID ties. Direct tests assert out-of-order creation and equivalent zero-fraction ties; mode-specific deletion and lower/high ID tie matrices remain unasserted.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.versionmode`

requirements.text: - `modifiedat` - This is the same as the `createdat` algorithm except that the `modifiedat` attribute of each Version MUST be used instead of the `createdat` attribute.

review.note: Modifiedat reuses timestamp ordering with the modifiedat field, including repeated repair because ancestry changes themselves touch timestamps. The fixed-point test asserts the exact stable chain after an edit; inherited createdat algorithm obligations such as mode-specific deletion/ties are not all directly tested.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.versionmode`

requirements.text: - `semver` - Newest Version: MUST be the Version with the highest `versionid` value per the [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/) specification's "precedence" ordering rules. - Oldest Version: MUST be the Version with the lowest `versionid` value per the [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/) specification's "precedence" ordering rules. Note that this MUST also be the one and only "root" Version. - Ancestor Processing: The `ancestorid` value of each Version MUST either be its `versionid` value (if it is the oldest Version), or the `versionid` of the next oldest Version per the [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/) specification's "precedence" ordering rules. - Deleted Ancestor: if a Version's ancestor is deleted, then this Version's `ancestorid` value MUST be determined by the "ancestor processing" logic as stated above. - When this `versionmode` is used, the `singleversionroot` aspect MUST be set to `true`.

review.note: SemanticVersion parses exact numeric components, rejects leading-zero numeric prereleases, applies numeric-versus-text prerelease precedence, and ignores build metadata for precedence. Engine ordering builds a single chain. The direct 1.0.0-rc.1/2.0.0 case is not the full precedence, invalid-ID and deletion matrix.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.validatecompatibility`

requirements.text: - Indicates whether the server MUST validate that all Versions of this Resource type adhere to its owning Resource's `meta.compatibility` value.

review.note: RESOLVED MODEL-REV-011: Built-in Resource Meta compatibility mode membership is case-insensitive based on system origin. Mode spelling still flows through the advertised directional/transitive policies; unrelated extension string enums, including same-named fields, remain ordinal.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.validatecompatibility`

requirements.text: - When not specified, the default value MUST be `false`.

review.note: CompileResources uses false for omitted validatecompatibility, and the runtime respects the compiled flag. There is no direct assertion of the omitted compiled value paired with a configured validator that must not run compatibility checks.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.validatecompatibility`

requirements.text: - A value of `true` indicates that the server MUST generate an error ([compatibility_violation](spec.md#compatibility_violation)) if any Version of a Resource instance of this Resource type does not adhere to the rules of the `meta.compatibility` value for that Resource's `format` value. See [`strictvalidation`](#groupsstringresourcesstringstrictvalidation) for exceptions to this requirement.

review.note: Established incompatibility yields compatibility_violation even when strictvalidation is false; it is not converted into compatibilityvalidated:false. The direct Avro test asserts rejected publication, retained default Version and unchanged Version count, while unsupported policies take the separate unchecked path.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.validatecompatibility`

requirements.text: - When a Version does not have a `format` value then compatibility verification MUST NOT be done.

review.note: The engine requests compatibility only when format is present; the built-in adapter returns NotRequested for a missing format. The separate policy test directly asserts absent format causes both flags to remain null, but no direct server response/callback-count test isolates this condition.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.validatecompatibility`

requirements.text: - When this model attribute is `true` then its sibling `validateformat` attribute MUST also be `true`.

review.note: CompileResources rejects validatecompatibility:true when validateformat is not true. The exact inconsistent-control case omits validateformat and expects model_error at validatecompatibility; the valid all-enabled case observes both flags true.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.validatecompatibility`

requirements.text: - A value of `false` indicates that the server MUST NOT perform any `compatibility` checking for instances of this Resource type.

review.note: The adapter avoids compatibility checks when ValidateCompatibility is false, and ApplyValidation removes unrequested compatibility flags. No direct engine test with validateformat:true, validatecompatibility:false and a counting compatibility validator proves this prohibition independently.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.validatecompatibility`

requirements.text: - In cases where this attribute is `false`, but there is a desire to advertise the external entity that has performed the validation, a `label` MAY be added to the Resource's model or to the Resource instance itself with this information.

review.note: Advertising an external validator through a label is a permitted convention, not a mandate to run verification or set success flags. Model labels and instance labels provide storage surfaces, but their presence cannot prove external validation occurred; no automatic certification is claimed.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.strictvalidation`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL

review.note: Strictvalidation is optional. The engine test uses an omitted aspect to return explicit unchecked false results and an explicit true variant to reject an unsupported format. It does not promote an unknown validator outcome to validated:true.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.strictvalidation`

requirements.text: - When not specified, the default value MUST be `false`.

review.note: StrictValidation's false default is observed at the engine seam: an unknown format under a model with no strictvalidation field is accepted only as unchecked false with a reason; changing just the field to true rejects it.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.strictvalidation`

requirements.text: - The `format` validation logic MUST generate an error ([format_violation](spec.md#format_violation)) if the Version's `format` is an unsupported value.

review.note: Strict unsupported format rejects publication, but the engine and tests use format_unknown, whereas this model paragraph names format_violation. Core's formatvalidated definition expressly requires format_unknown/format_external. This is an uncorrected source conflict, not evidence that rejection is missing.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.strictvalidation`

requirements.text: - The `compatibility` validation logic MUST generate an error ([compatibility_violation](spec.md#compatibility_violation)) if the Resource's `meta.compatibility` value is an unsupported value.

review.note: Strict unsupported compatibility is rejected as compatibility_unknown, directly asserted for unsupported non-Avro evolution. This model clause instead names compatibility_violation, while Core's compatibilityvalidated definition requires compatibility_unknown. Established incompatibility remains a distinct violation error.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.strictvalidation`

requirements.text: - If the Version's `format` value is absent, then format and compatibility validation logic MUST NOT be performed for that Version.

review.note: Absent format disables both checks before strictness matters. The standalone policy test uses invalid document bytes with missing format and still obtains accepted with null flags; the engine gates match this source logic, but its corresponding response/callback assertion is absent.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.strictvalidation`

requirements.text: - If the Version's `format` value is not supported, then the `format` validation logic MUST NOT generate an error. Instead, the Version's `formatvalidated` and `compatibilityvalidated` attributes MUST be set to `false`.

review.note: Nonstrict unsupported format returns false for requested format and compatibility validation, with nonempty reasons, rather than rejection or a success claim. The engine test directly asserts both flags for an unknown format and requested backward compatibility.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.strictvalidation`

requirements.text: - If the Resource's `meta.compatibility` value is unsupported, then the Version's `compatibilityvalidated` attribute MUST be set to `false`.

review.note: Unsupported nonstrict compatibility produces compatibilityvalidated:false while a successful syntax check stays true. The direct non-Avro changed-bytes test observes both flags and the explicit compatibility.policy reason, distinguishing unsupported proof from actual incompatibility.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.strictvalidation`

requirements.text: - Regardless of the value of this aspect, if the Version's `format` value is absent, then format and compatibility validation logic MUST NOT be performed for that Version.

review.note: Regardless of strictness, missing format makes both checks unrequested. The independent policy assertion uses strict:true and verifies neither flag is invented. The engine's hasFormat guards were inspected, but a direct engine test of this unconditional exemption is not present.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.typemap`

requirements.text: - Type: Map where the keys and values MUST be non-empty strings.

review.note: TypeMap requires nonempty keys and string values, and its value switch rejects empty/unsupported strings. The direct invalid map tests cover repeated wildcards and yaml, but not empty key/value or non-string value; those are present source checks with incomplete direct evidence.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.typemap`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

review.note: Typemap is optional and supplies implicit defaults when omitted. Its complete surrounding description distinguishes JSON, string and exact binary representations; raw/inline tests assert those shapes. Empty Documents correctly use base64:"" under Core's explicit rule, not string:"" merely because a mapping is string.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.typemap`

requirements.text: Since the `contenttype` value is a "media-type" per [RFC9110](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9110#media.type), for purposes of looking it up in the `typemap`, just the `type/subtype` portion of the value (case-insensitively) MUST be used. Meaning, any `parameters` MUST be excluded.

review.note: ResolveDocumentFormat removes everything from the semicolon, trims the type/subtype and matches case-insensitively. The direct APPLICATION/JSON; charset=utf-8 assertion selects Json; the parameter is not part of the lookup key.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.typemap`

requirements.text: If more than one entry in the `typemap` matches the `contenttype`, but they all have the same value, then that value MUST be used. If they are not all the same, then `binary` MUST be used.

review.note: Lookup examines every matching entry: equal results are retained and any conflicting result becomes Binary, without most-specific-pattern precedence. The direct text/plain case has agreeing implicit/wildcard matches; text/mine has conflicting string/json matches and resolves Binary.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.typemap`

requirements.text: - The key MAY include at most one `*` to act as a wildcard to mean zero or more instances of any character at that position in the string - similar to a `.*` in a regular expression. The key MUST be a case-insensitive string.

review.note: The compiler rejects more than one star; lookup implements prefix/suffix matching with zero-or-more middle characters and ordinal-ignore-case comparisons. Direct repeated-star rejection and ordinary wildcard/case matches exist, but no direct zero-character wildcard match is asserted.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.typemap`

requirements.text: Implementations MAY define additional values.

review.note: Additional typemap result values are permitted but not mandatory. This implementation deliberately limits the set to binary, json and string. The preceding value definitions were read; declining to add yaml or another extension is not missing required behavior.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.typemap`

requirements.text: A value of `json` indicates that the Resource's document is JSON and MUST be serialized under the `<RESOURCE>` attribute if it is valid JSON. Note that if there is a syntax error in the JSON then the server MUST treat the document as `binary` to avoid sending invalid JSON to the client. The server MAY choose to modify the formatting of the document (e.g. to "pretty-print" it).

review.note: InlineDocument parses json-mapped bytes into the Resource attribute and falls back to exact base64 for invalid_json, invalid_utf8 or duplicate_member. Tests assert valid JSON structure and invalid UTF-8 fallback. A genuine malformed JSON-text case and other strict parser rejection categories are not directly asserted.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.typemap`

requirements.text: Specifying an unknown (or unsupported) value MUST generate an error ([model_error](./spec.md#model_error)) during the update of the xRegistry model.

review.note: Unknown typemap values fail compilation through the supported-value switch. The direct yaml input expects model_error at its typemap entry, rather than silently defaulting an unsupported requested mapping to binary.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.typemap`

requirements.text: By default, the following [RFC9110](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9110#media.type) `typemap` keys MUST be implicitly defined as follows, unless overridden by an explicit `typemap` entry:

review.note: The implicit application/json, *+json and text/plain mappings are installed before explicit entries. Direct tests observe all three and an explicit case-insensitive Application/JSON override to binary; no absent mapping is treated as JSON by guesswork.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.attributes`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

review.note: Version extension attributes are optional; omitted lists are populated with the Version system baseline and conditional Document fields. The minimal model directly observes required versionid, and hasdocument:false tests confirm Document definitions are absent rather than merely hidden in output.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.attributes`

requirements.text: - Extension attribute names at this level MUST NOT overlap with extension attributes defined at the `groups.resources.resourceattributes` level. The only duplicate names allowed are specification-defined attributes such as `self` and `xid`, and the Version-specific values MUST be overridden by the Resource-level values when serialized.

review.note: The compiler-owned named-extension uniqueness gap is resolved: conditional Version siblings are recursively checked against Resource projection reservations, with independent nested object/item scopes preserved. Normal Resource projection and Server serialization remain separate obligations whose qualification is not inferred from these Core runs.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.resourceattributes`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

review.note: Resourceattributes is optional because the compiler supplies Resource navigation fields separately from Version attributes and Meta attributes. Runtime alias projection asserts Resource self/ID while preserving target Version metadata, but no direct complete effective ResourceAttributes enumeration exists.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.resourceattributes`

requirements.text: - These attributes are reserved for system-managed attributes, such as `metaurl`, that exist to help in the navigation of the entities. Users MUST NOT define additional attributes for this list. Extension Resource-level attributes would appear in the `metaattributes` list, while Version-level extensions would appear in the `attributes` list.

review.note: CompileResources rejects user-supplied Resource projection names that are absent from Resource's system baseline, routing extensions to Version attributes or Meta instead. The direct custom resourceattributes case expects model_error; this is not a prohibition on Meta extensions.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.resourceattributes`

requirements.text: - While it is NOT RECOMMENDED, implementations MAY add additional attributes to this list if they are necessary to help with model traversal. Otherwise the other 2 attribute lists SHOULD be used. The goal is to make the Resource entity look as much like the `default` Version as possible; adding additional attributes at the Resource level violates that goal.

review.note: Implementations may add necessary navigation attributes but are discouraged from making Resource projections noisy. This implementation reserves the plane for its system navigation set and exposes no arbitrary user extension hook there; the permission does not require such a hook.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.metaattributes`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

review.note: Metaattributes is an optional, independently compiled plane, populated with Meta defaults and allowing extensions without polluting the Version projection. The minimal model asserts defaultversionsticky:false, but no direct custom Meta-extension versus Version-extension serialization test covers the complete explanatory subsection.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Retrieving the Registry Model

requirements.text: The full "model" view can be thought of as a full schema definition of what the message exchanges with the server might look like. As such, it MUST include:

review.note: The full surrounding list requires Registry, Group, Resource, Meta and Version collection/navigation definitions, not only an object named model. SystemAttributes/ModelWriter provide these planes and remove Document definitions for hasdocument:false. Representative tests do not enumerate all full-model definitions/aspects against the specification.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Retrieving the Registry Model

requirements.text: - Registry top-level and Group `<COLLECTION>*` attributes. While the `model` and `modelsource` attributes MUST appear, their definitions MAY be shallow - meaning, they can be defined as just `object` with one attribute (`*`) of type "any".

review.note: Registry and Group collection maps/counts/URLs are added from effective types. Model and modelsource use explicitly permitted shallow object definitions containing *:any. This is a permitted schema simplification, not missing deep model-language support; direct assertions for both shallow definitions are absent.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Retrieving the Registry Model

requirements.text: The "modelsource" view of the model is just what was provided by the user when the model was defined, or last edited. It is expected that this view of the model is much smaller than the full model and only includes domain-specific information. While specification-defined attributes MAY appear in this document, they are NOT RECOMMENDED since the server will automatically add them so users do not need to concern themselves with those details.

review.note: Modelsource retains user-specified omissions/nulls/directives rather than synthesizing the system baseline. Source system attributes are allowed but unnecessary; actual overlay tests exercise this allowance. This is semantic source preservation, not a claim that response whitespace matches the original bytes.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Retrieving the Registry Model

requirements.text: When retrieving the `modelsource`, the response MUST only include what was specified in the request to define the model - it MUST NOT include any auto-added specification defined metadata that will appear under `model`.

review.note: RegistryModel.Source and the engine's separately persisted source are distinct from EffectiveModel/frozen compiledsource. Tests assert omitted plural remains omitted, explicit default:null remains null, include directives remain in source, and restart retrieves the directive without refetching it.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model

requirements.text: A server MAY support updating the model of a Registry via:

review.note: This server elects to support both direct modelsource replacement and modelsource inside Registry updates, subject to authorization/availability. Direct replacement persists across restart; the root modelsource:null test exercises the embedded update path and resets to an empty source model.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model

requirements.text: - Changes to specification-defined attributes MAY be included in the model but MUST NOT change them such that they become incompatible with the specification. For example, changes to further constrain the allowable values of an attribute are typically allowed, but changing its `type` from `string` to `integer` is not.

review.note: RESOLVED MODEL-REV-011: Built-in Resource Meta compatibility mode membership is case-insensitive based on system origin. Mode spelling still flows through the advertised directional/transitive policies; unrelated extension string enums, including same-named fields, remain ordinal. RESOLVED MODEL-REV-012: Cross-Version matching checks actual derived default membership after final ordering/retention rather than stored false placeholders. A single retained Version remains valid; model updates introducing an inconsistent equality rule reject as model_compliance_error. The compound clause remains pending its other direct-evidence obligations.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model

requirements.text: - Specification-defined attributes that are `required` MUST NOT have this aspect changed to `false`.

review.note: A baseline Required=true cannot be explicitly changed to false; omitted values inherit the baseline. The direct specversion required:false model case asserts model_error.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model

requirements.text: - Specification-defined attributes that are `readonly` MUST NOT have this aspect changed to `false`.

review.note: A specification baseline ReadOnly=true cannot be weakened. The self readonly:false case directly fails compilation, while omission retains the readonly baseline for runtime ignore processing.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model

requirements.text: - Specification-defined attributes that define a `default` value MUST always include a `default` value in their definitions.

review.note: Omitted system defaults are inherited; an explicit null cannot remove a non-null baseline default. The direct specversion default:null case is rejected, and the minimal model confirms the inherited 1.0-rc4 default exists.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model

requirements.text: Any specification attributes not included in a request to define, or update, a model MUST be included in the resulting full model. In other words, the full Registry's model consists of the specification-defined attributes overlaid with the attributes that are explicitly-defined as part of a `modelsource` update request.

review.note: MODEL-REV-005 is resolved: Group attribute overlays compile after all local and imported Resource collection baselines are available. A valid imported rsurl immutable overlay retains its system origin, immutable/read-only/required flags and annotation, while aliases preserve the actual shared Resource definition. Ordinary extension immutable and weakened system constraints still reject. The obsolete Server immutable-stripping workaround was removed after a direct red/green persisted-overlay assertion; actual restart retains immutable and shared imported type identity.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model

requirements.text: Registries MAY support extension attributes to the model language (meaning, new attributes within the model definitions themselves), but only if the server supports them. Servers MUST generate an error ([model_error](./spec.md#model_error)) if a model definition includes unknown model language attributes.

review.note: CheckMembers allows only explicitly implemented model-language fields at each scope and rejects future with model_error, including root and attribute scopes. The supported source shorthand and root $schema are deliberate understood forms, not silent acceptance of arbitrary extension language.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model

requirements.text: Once a Registry has been created, changes to the model MAY be supported by server implementations. This specification makes no statement as to what types of changes are allowed beyond the following requirements:

review.note: Post-creation updates are an optional server feature; this engine implements authorized whole-model candidate replacement. The direct test proves a rejected incompatible removal and an accepted additive update surviving restart. This does not mean every conceivable model change is supported or safe.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model

requirements.text: - Any model change MUST result in a specification compliant model definition.

review.note: This recovery verifies the compiler fixes for conditional Resource-name overlap, annotation URI syntax and imported system-baseline ordering (MODEL-REV-002/004/005). Candidate replacement, singular-identity rules and full model compliance remain broader parent-owned obligations; managed Core compilation success is not complete model or Server qualification. RESOLVED MODEL-REV-006: Model replacement compares retained Group/Resource plural identities and rejects changes to their immutable singular names even when no instances exist. Rejection preserves the prior model and persistence generation. The compound clause remains pending its other direct-evidence obligations. The obsolete Server immutable-stripping workaround was removed after a direct red/green persisted-overlay assertion; actual restart retains immutable and shared imported type identity.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model

requirements.text: - Servers MUST ensure that the representation of all entities within the Registry adheres to the new model prior to completing the model update request.

review.note: RESOLVED MODEL-REV-003: The final-candidate xref constraint gate now applies the shared pure enum/equals checker to every retained target Version and reverse target/Group/model updates. It uses bounded indexed collection traversal, honors one-hop/dangling behavior, applies no referring defaults, checks forward read authorization before values and avoids disclosing private alias identities in reverse diagnostics. RESOLVED MODEL-REV-012: Cross-Version matching checks actual derived default membership after final ordering/retention rather than stored false placeholders. A single retained Version remains valid; model updates introducing an inconsistent equality rule reject as model_compliance_error. The compound clause remains pending its other direct-evidence obligations.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model

requirements.text: Any request to update the model that does not adhere to those requirements MUST generate an error ([model_compliance_error](./spec.md#model_compliance_error)).

review.note: RESOLVED MODEL-REV-008: Existing Version enum/required failures and late cross-Version equality failures during model replacement now use model_compliance_error and preserve prior data/model. Ordinary non-model mutations retain their specific metadata/matchversions errors. This does not by itself establish every error path in the broader update contract. The compound clause remains pending its other direct-evidence obligations.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model

requirements.text: How the server guarantees that all entities in the Registry are compliant with the model is an implementation detail. For example, while it is NOT RECOMMENDED, it is valid for an implementation to modify (or even delete) existing entities to ensure model compliance. Instead, it is RECOMMENDED that the model update requests generate an error ([model_compliance_error](./spec.md#model_compliance_error)) if existing entities are not compliant.

review.note: The recommended policy is rejecting incompatible existing state rather than silently deleting it. The engine rejects missing live types and stages all changes atomically; the direct test verifies existing metadata survives. Default population and normative retention pruning can still modify state, which this paragraph explicitly permits when compliant.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model

requirements.text: For the purposes of validating that the existing entities in the Registry are compliant with the model, the mechanisms used to define the model (e.g. `$include` vs `ximportresources` vs defined locally) MUST NOT impact that analysis. In other words, model updates that have no semantic changes but rather switch between one of those 3 mechanisms MUST NOT invalidate any existing entities in the Registry.

review.note: The imported-system-overlay ordering defect no longer prevents valid modelsource or frozen-source compilation, and imported aliases preserve shared Resource identity. This does not prove an existing-data model update that switches local/include/import mechanisms while preserving metadata and all applicable constraints. The obsolete Server immutable-stripping workaround was removed after a direct red/green persisted-overlay assertion; actual restart retains immutable and shared imported type identity.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model

requirements.text: Additionally, it is STRONGLY RECOMMENDED that model updates be limited to backwards compatible changes.

review.note: Backward-compatible changes are strongly recommended, but the engine's gate is current-state compliance, not compatibility with all previously valid client inputs. An additive update is directly tested; no explicit backward-compatibility policy or complete narrowing/removal classification is implemented at this seam.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model

requirements.text: Implementations MAY choose to limit the types of changes made to the model, or not support model updates at all.

review.note: Servers may restrict model changes or disable updates entirely. Authorization, capability availability and readonly persistence are legitimate host controls; the existence of a mutable engine API does not mandate all deployments enable it. This permission does not waive correctness for updates that are accepted.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model / Reuse of Resource Definitions

requirements.text: When a Resource type definition is to be shared between Groups, rather than creating a duplicate Resource definition, the `ximportresources` mechanism MAY be used instead. The `ximportresources` attribute on a Group definition allows for a list of `<XIDTYPE>` references to other Resource types to be included within this Group.

review.note: Resource reuse is implemented as shared immutable RegistryResourceDefinition identity, not a structural copy. Tests verify transitive imported definitions and ReferenceEquals across reciprocal imports of different local types; the server test confirms identity survives persistence and rejects independent lookalikes for xref.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model / Reuse of Resource Definitions

requirements.text: - Each array value MUST be an `<XIDTYPE>` reference to another Group/Resource combination defined within the same Registry. It MUST NOT reference the same Group under which the `ximportresources` resides.

review.note: Import references must parse as local Group/Resource type pairs, with no Version suffix or owning-Group self-reference, and resolve within the current Group dictionary. Direct tests reject self, missing target and non-string references; external acquisition is not part of ximportresources.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model / Reuse of Resource Definitions

requirements.text: - An empty array MAY be specified, implying no Resources are imported.

review.note: An explicit empty imports array produces no import entries and leaves local Resources unchanged; source retains the empty directive while full model omits it. No direct empty-array equivalence/source-preservation test was found, so ordinary absent-import tests are not substituted.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model / Reuse of Resource Definitions

requirements.text: - The definition of a Group MAY include an `ximportresources` directive that references a Resource from another Group that itself is defined via an `ximportresources`. However, transitive definitions of Resources MUST NOT result in a circular import chain.

review.note: Imports resolve transitively with a cache and active (Group,Resource) pairs; circular Resource definitions fail, while reciprocal imports of distinct local types are valid. The independent import-depth budget is directly tested at two versus one, not confused with include depth.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model / Reuse of Resource Definitions

requirements.text: Locally defined Resources MAY be defined within a Group that uses the `ximportresources` feature; however, Resource `plural` and `singular` values MUST be unique across all imported and locally defined Resources.

review.note: Local Resource definitions may coexist with imports. The resolved peer-name set checks both plural and singular; tests reject a local/imported plural collision and equal singular names, and accept two distinct local/imported Resources in each of two Groups.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model / Reuse of Resource Definitions

requirements.text: This attribute, while listed in the schema definition of `model`, and `modelsource` for ease of reading the specification, is only available for `modelsource`. Similar to the `$include` directive, servers MUST process any `ximportresources` found in the `modelsource` data and the results MUST be reflected in the `model`, but the `ximportresources` directive MUST NOT appear in the `model` serialization.

review.note: Ordinary imports remain in Source and are absent from EffectiveModel; imported definitions retain actual shared identity. The valid imported immutable collection-overlay form now compiles, including a frozen-source form with imports restored. Server persistence/restart qualifications are not inferred from these Core tests. The obsolete Server immutable-stripping workaround was removed after a direct red/green persisted-overlay assertion; actual restart retains immutable and shared imported type identity.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model / Includes in the xRegistry Model Data

requirements.text: There might be times when it is necessary for an xRegistry model to reuse portions of another xRegistry model defined elsewhere. Rather than forcing the duplication of the model definitions, an "include" type of JSON directive MAY be used.

review.note: The optional include facility is implemented before structural compilation, using a caller-supplied resolver for external documents and no resolver for in-document pointers. Tests exercise both forms and inspect the resulting actual attribute/Resource definitions.

requirements.text: These directives MAY be used in any JSON Object or Map entity in an xRegistry model definition. The following rules apply to how the include directive is processed:

review.note: ExpandValue recursively processes directives in object/map positions before model validation, rather than hardcoding only the root. Tests cover root, attributes map and nested Resource-definition includes, including an in-document pointer with no external resolver.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model / Includes in the xRegistry Model Data

requirements.text: - The include path reference value MUST be compatible with the environment in which the `include` is being evaluated. For example, in an xRegistry server it would most likely always be a URL. However, in an external tool the reference might be to a local file on disk or a URL.

review.note: The acquisition environment is explicit: SourceUri supplies the base and IRegistryModelResolver handles authorized document URIs. Core does no network/filesystem fetch itself. Direct tests reject an external reference without a resolver and a relative reference without a base; an injected resolver supports valid references.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model / Includes in the xRegistry Model Data

requirements.text: - The include MUST reference a JSON Object or Map that is consistent with the model definition of where the include appears, and the target attributes, or keys, are processed in place of the `$include` attribute.

review.note: Selected include values must be JSON objects/maps, whose members replace the directive before contextual model compilation. The direct description-string target is rejected, and positive map/Resource imports are compiled into their expected definitions rather than leaving unresolved directives.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model / Includes in the xRegistry Model Data

requirements.text: - Any attributes already present (as siblings to the include) MUST take precedence over an included attribute - matching is done via comparing the `name` of the attributes.

review.note: Local object members are installed before include members, whose TryAdd cannot replace them. Valid model attribute names equal their map keys, so ordinal member matching respects this precedence. The direct test keeps local:string rather than included local:boolean.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model / Includes in the xRegistry Model Data

requirements.text: - When `$includes` is used, the references MUST be processed in order and earlier attributes included take precedence over subsequently included attributes.

review.note: Includes are processed in array order, and earlier members win via TryAdd. The direct test asserts a remains the first document's integer with description first wins despite the later string definition, while later nonconflicting b is still included.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model / Includes in the xRegistry Model Data

requirements.text: - Both `$include` and `$includes` MUST NOT be present at the same time at the same level in the model.

review.note: ExpandValue checks directive presence before expanding and rejects coexisting $include/$includes at the same object level. The direct root case expects model_error; separate objects can still use their own chosen form.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model / Includes in the xRegistry Model Data

requirements.text: - Included model definitions MAY use `include` directives, but MUST NOT result in a circular include chain.

review.note: Nested include chains are supported and tracked by document URI plus decoded fragment; active repeats fail as model_include_cycle. Direct tests cover a root self-reference, a two-document cycle, and a successful nested chain with independent depth/document/node limits.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model / Includes in the xRegistry Model Data

requirements.text: - Resolution of the include path MUST follow standard path resolution. Meaning, relative paths are relative to the document with the include directive.

review.note: Each expanded document becomes the origin for its nested references; relative paths are not resolved against the initial Registry URL or process working directory. The direct parts/first.json -> ../common.json test can only succeed with the expected document-relative URI.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model / Includes in the xRegistry Model Data

requirements.text: - If present, the fragment (`#...`) part of the reference MUST adhere to the [JSON Pointer](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6901) specification.

review.note: Fragments are percent-decoded with strict UTF-8, must be empty or start with slash, decode ~0/~1, and support canonical nonnegative array indices. Tests cover escaped object keys, invalid tilde/UTF-8, missing targets and a non-pointer fragment; direct array-index/leading-zero and non-ASCII success cases remain missing.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model / Includes in the xRegistry Model Data

requirements.text: When the directives are used in a request to update the model, the server MUST resolve all includes prior to updating the model. The original (source) model definition, with any "include" directives, MUST be available via the `modelsource` attribute/entity. The expanded model (after the resolution of any includes, and after all specification-defined attributes have been added), MUST be available via the `model` attribute/entity. The directives MUST only be processed during the initial update of the model. In order to have them re-evaluated, a subsequent model update request (with those directives) MUST be sent.

review.note: MODEL-BUDGET-002 is resolved for expanded and effective serialization. RegistryJson.Create commits through bounded storage before output growth/copying, uses separate reusable writer reservation scratch, and caps retained capacity at MaxBytes. Exact encoded lengths are admitted and one-extra-byte outputs reject. This does not close the independent Server include re-resolution-on-update evidence gap.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model / Includes in the xRegistry Model Data

requirements.text: When there is tooling used outside of the server, e.g. in an xRegistry client, if that tooling resolves the "include" directives prior to sending the model to the server, then the directives will not appear in the `modelsource` view of the model. Ideally, tooling SHOULD allow users to choose whether the resolution of the directives is done locally or by the server.

review.note: The low-level client sends caller-supplied bytes without automatically expanding includes, and Core offers explicit compilation/resolution. There is no direct client test or dedicated include-only preprocessing choice proving both workflows preserve source semantics. Sending EffectiveModel is not transparently equivalent when source import aliases carry shared-type identity.

source.section: xRegistry Events / Abstract

requirements.text: This specification defines the events that an xRegistry server MAY generate.

review.note: Abstract identifying the optional event specification; executable generation policy is reviewed below. This is semantic/managed evidence, not all-platform release qualification.

source.section: xRegistry Events / Overview

requirements.text: As updates are made to entities within an xRegistry instance, events SHOULD be generated to notify interested parties of those changes. This specification defines the metadata associated with each event as [CloudEvent](https://cloudevents.io) context attributes. Whether CloudEvents are used in the generation/serialization of the events is OPTIONAL, but it is RECOMMENDED.

review.note: Chosen SHOULD policy: committed mutations generate structured CloudEvents in the atomic outbox; no standardized subscription/watch transport is claimed. This is semantic/managed evidence, not all-platform release qualification.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Overview / Endpoints

requirements.text: - `producer`: A producer endpoint is made available by a consumer or intermediary (like an application or a queue) to a producer, so that the producer can send events/messages to the endpoint. Those events/messages MUST conform to the declared constraints. If the endpoint is associated with at least one message group, only messages/events that match one of the declared message definitions can be sent. If the message definition references a data schema, the message payload MUST match that schema.

review.note: The Endpoint API now constructs the bounded permitted Message set, rejects incomplete/ambiguous lookup and exposes the selected metadata. Local schema Resource type/self identity and imported Message contracts are implemented. This compound row also requires an actual produced message and payload to match those constraints. The metadata APIs do not send or validate an application's actual wire payload, so that runtime obligation is not promoted to implemented. Implementation scope: runtime-message-contract. Explicit qualifications: external-runtime-message-and-payload-validation. Current bounded Models/Server regression evidence; no broker/runtime-message execution or unexecuted native-platform qualification is inferred.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Overview / Endpoints

requirements.text: - `subscriber`: A subscriber endpoint is made available to consumers for the purpose of setting up their own consumer endpoint. The [CloudEvents Subscriptions API](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/subscriptions/spec.md) specification enumerates the subscription mechanisms intended for these endpoints. As subscription mechanisms can vary substantially across products that implement the same protocol, it is RECOMMENDED to use the `label` mechanism to identify the specific product that provides the endpoint.

review.note: Product labels are recommended publishing metadata, not a mandatory broker discovery or subscription implementation. The source deliberately leaves product-specific subscription mechanisms outside a universal adapter contract. No automatic product-label-to-subscription-adapter behavior is claimed, and omission is not made a server rejection. Implementation scope: product-specific-authoring-policy. Explicit qualifications: undefined-product-selection-policy. Current bounded Models/Server regression evidence; no broker/runtime-message execution or unexecuted native-platform qualification is inferred.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Overview / Endpoints

requirements.text: Each endpoint definition defines a `protocol` selector by which the specific network application protocol is chosen to communicate with the endpoint. If a networked entity supports multiple protocols, each protocol endpoint MUST be declared separately, even if those are multiplexed over the same port. For instance, if you have an MQTT broker that can dynamically select between MQTT 3.1.1 and MQTT 5.0, those endpoints are to be declared separately as the capabilities differ substantially.

review.note: Each Endpoint is a separately identified Group with one string protocol selector. The six binding branches and distinct MQTT versions/options are exercised, and aliases retain their specified default version. This supports separate declarations even for one physical host/port; a passive registry cannot discover undeclared remote protocol capabilities. Implementation scope: metadata-declaration. Current bounded Models/Server regression evidence; no broker/runtime-message execution or unexecuted native-platform qualification is inferred.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Overview / Endpoints

requirements.text: Each endpoint MAY also define an `envelope` selector which allows for defining particular `envelopeoptions` at the endpoint level. For CloudEvents, this permits the definition of the serialization mode (binary or structured) and the event format for structured mode.

review.note: Envelope omission remains legal. CloudEvents binary/structured modes and format declarations are preserved and checked without making CloudEvents mandatory or starting a transport. Implementation scope: metadata-declaration. Current bounded Models/Server regression evidence; no broker/runtime-message execution or unexecuted native-platform qualification is inferred.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Overview / Message Groups

requirements.text: The Endpoint is an xRegistry group-level construct that is conceptually an extension of the [message definition group](../message/spec.md), meaning there are no “groups of endpoints”. An endpoint MAY contain directly embedded message definitions. In the simplest case, an endpoint MAY embed its message definitions locally which in turn MAY embed their data schema definitions locally, all in one compact construct.

review.note: The active Endpoint model imports the actual Message Resource under Endpoint Groups and includes Message Groups for shared definitions. Endpoint-kind server cases store schema-bearing unbound Message children. The corrected messagegroups target names Groups, not Message Resources. Schema type/self-URI checks reuse the Message domain identity helper; inheritance itself remains the separate completed Message materializer's seam. Implementation scope: metadata-hierarchy-and-identity. Current bounded Models/Server regression evidence; no broker/runtime-message execution or unexecuted native-platform qualification is inferred.

requirements.text: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in [RFC 2119](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2119).

review.note: RFC2119 keyword interpretation defines the strength of subsequent rows; it is not an executable feature or an unimplemented local obligation. Implementation scope: notation. source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Notations and Terminology / Notational Conventions

requirements.text: For clarity, OPTIONAL attributes (specification-defined and extensions) are OPTIONAL for clients to use, but the servers' responsibility will vary. Server-unknown extension attributes MUST be silently stored in the backing datastore. Specification-defined attributes and server-known extension attributes MUST generate an error if the corresponding feature is not supported or enabled. However, as with all attributes, if accepting the attribute results in a bad state (such as exceeding a size limit or resulting in a security issue), then the server MAY choose to reject the request.

review.note: The explicit Endpoint authoring model admits its known metadata and opaque extension values; authored known-kind/template errors and finite-budget failures are explicit. Unmarked custom models are not silently opted into domain rules. Unknown protocol/option contracts remain explicit consumer obligations. This row receives domain-admission evidence, not duplicate credit for every Core binding/capability rule. Implementation scope: domain-admission-and-safety-policy. Current bounded Models/Server regression evidence; no broker/runtime-message execution or unexecuted native-platform qualification is inferred.

The presence of the `#` character means the remaining portion of the line is a comment. Whitespace characters in the JSON snippets are used for readability and are not normative.

review.note: Pseudo-JSON optionality/repetition markers and explanatory whitespace are notation, not characters to implement in stored JSON. No runtime or local implementation gap follows. Implementation scope: notation. Explicit qualifications: informative-no-runtime-implementation. source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model

requirements.text: As discussed in the [CloudEvents Registry overview](../cloudevents/spec.md), endpoints are supersets of [message definition groups](../message/spec.md#message-definition-groups) and MAY contain inlined messages. Therefore, the Resources in the meta-model for the Endpoint Registry are likewise `messages` as defined in the [message catalog specification](../message/spec.md).

review.note: Endpoint Groups import the same Message Resource contract, not a distinct untyped endpoint-message surrogate. Inline Message/schema metadata, owning-group selector checks and borrowed-message enforcement are exercised. This does not re-review Message clauses or count broker delivery as registry behavior. Implementation scope: metadata-hierarchy-and-identity. Current bounded Models/Server regression evidence; no broker/runtime-message execution or unexecuted native-platform qualification is inferred.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `envelope`

requirements.text: - If a `<VERSION>` is specified at the Group level, all Resources within that Group MUST have a `<VERSION>` value that is at least as precise as its Group, and MUST NOT expand it. For example, if a Group had a `envelope` value of `myspec`, then Resources within that Group can have `envelope` values of `myspec` or `myspec/1.0`. However, if a Group has a value of `myspec/1.0`, it would be invalid for a Resource to have a value of `myspec/2.0` or just `myspec`. Additionally, if a Group does not have an `envelope` attribute, then there are no constraints on its Resources' `envelope` attributes.

review.note: Owning Endpoint envelope constraints reject omission/broadening and conflicting versions, while an unversioned parent permits a versioned child. Tests distinguish a dot-component refinement from 1.01 and exercise compatible/incompatible server mutations. Borrowed Messages remain subject to the referring Endpoint contract. Implementation scope: metadata-group-contract. Current bounded Models/Server regression evidence; no broker/runtime-message execution or unexecuted native-platform qualification is inferred.

requirements.text: - Description: OPTIONAL authorization configuration details of the endpoint. Each entry describes one authorization option that the endpoint accepts; a client selects one of them. When specified, each entry MUST provide sufficient metadata for clients to select the authorization mechanism and discover where authorization is obtained. Runtime credentials and deployment-specific values are expected to be supplied separately through external configuration. The attribute names below MUST be used as defined. requirements.text: The [endpoint URIs](#protocoloptionsendpoints) for "Kafka" endpoints MUST be valid Kafka bootstrap server addresses. The scheme follows Kafka configuration usage as described in [Apache Kafka], e.g. `SSL://<HOST>:<PORT>` or `PLAINTEXT://<HOST>:<PORT>`.

review.note: Kafka validates nonempty bootstrap arrays and separate host/port values, including IPv6 and the source's listener-style forms. Malformed lists, paths/queries, absent/out-of-range ports fail. Custom listener names carry an explicit security-mapping obligation rather than an invented security protocol. Implementation scope: resolved-kafka-bootstrap-address. Current bounded Models/Server regression evidence; no broker/runtime-message execution or unexecuted native-platform qualification is inferred.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / KAFKA options

requirements.text: - A `subscriber` Kafka Endpoint describes the creation and configuration of a consumer group as an act of registering interest. It MUST NOT declare `consumergroup`, since the group is the resource being established rather than a group to be joined.

review.note: A Kafka subscriber declaration must omit consumergroup; providing one is a consumer-evaluation error. This describes registration intent, not a broker-side consumer-group creation implementation. Implementation scope: kafka-subscriber-metadata. Current bounded Models/Server regression evidence; no broker/runtime-message execution or unexecuted native-platform qualification is inferred.

requirements.text: A `message` definition MAY contain any combination of `envelope`, `protocol`, and data payload declarations. A payload-only declaration can be useful if messages are sent through varying protocols without a fixed envelope model and are distinguished by content-type (including parameters) or even only through whether payload schema definitions match an incoming message.

review.note: Optional definition planes remain independently usable; only selected protocol/envelope/schema declarations trigger their actual dependencies. No broker or schema acquisition is inferred. Exact current source and public assertion evidence; no automatic native-platform or release qualification.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Overview / Reusing Message Definitions

requirements.text: The `basemessage` attribute, a URI-typed reference to another message definition, enables such reuse scenarios. Any message definition MAY refer to another message definition as its base, which effects a copy of the base message’s definitions into the message that defines it. The mechanism is transitive, which means that `basemessage` relationships MUST be resolved recursively as long as they do not result in circular references.

review.note: Explicit callback acquisition follows the base chain once; actual/requested URI cycles fail, deep objects merge and arrays/scalars replace without losing literal null or provenance. Exact current source and public assertion evidence; no automatic native-platform or release qualification.

requirements.text: For clarity, OPTIONAL attributes (specification-defined and extensions) are OPTIONAL for clients to use, but the servers' responsibility will vary. Server-unknown extension attributes MUST be silently stored in the backing datastore. Specification-defined attributes and server-known extension attributes MUST generate an error if the corresponding feature is not supported or enabled. However, as with all attributes, if accepting the attribute results in a bad state (such as exceeding a size limit or resulting in a security issue), then the server MAY choose to reject the request.

review.note: Admitted wildcard/any values are retained and known malformed fields fail. The broad unknown-extension sentence is read with Core model admission; it does not authorize bypassing a closed model. Global Core conformance is not inferred from these domain cases. source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Message Definition Registry Model / Message Definitions (Message Group) / `basemessage`

requirements.text: The process that a client SHOULD follow to materialize the message is to follow the `basemessage` references to the end of the chain of messages, get that message's attributes, and then walk back up the chain performing a "merge" operation of the next message's attributes. Note that if an inherited attribute is a complex type (e.g. map, object) and the overlaying attribute is scalar, then the entire inherited attribute (and nested values) are replaced by that scalar value. For complex types, the merge is "deep", meaning each level of the complex type is merged appropriately rather than it being a complete replacement of the entire complex type.

review.note: Explicit callback acquisition follows the base chain once; actual/requested URI cycles fail, deep objects merge and arrays/scalars replace without losing literal null or provenance. source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Message Definition Registry Model / Metadata Envelopes and Message Protocols / Property Definitions

requirements.text: A header type refines its native protocol value, rather than defining an implicit codec. HTTP, NATS and MQTT values remain strings. The string-valued refinements `string`, `symbol`, `uri`, `uritemplate`, `stringified integer`, `timestamp`, `duration` and `uuid` are permitted; `any` leaves the native string unconstrained. Implementations MUST NOT coerce JSON Boolean, Number, Object or Array values into protocol header strings. Kafka header values may additionally use `binary` with a canonical base64 JSON string, or `any` with literal `null` for Kafka's null byte value. The default `string` represents text, not an implicit base64 decoding. A literal null is otherwise invalid for these header declarations; omission of `value` means that no fixed value is imposed.

review.note: SPEC-019/020 complete common header items with name/type/required/specurl/value, preserve outer map/array rules and duplicate order, and reject implicit wire-kind coercion. source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Message Definition Registry Model / Metadata Envelopes and Message Protocols / Property Definitions / `type`

requirements.text: - The valid types are those defined in the [CloudEvents][CloudEvents Types] core specification, with some additions: - `any`: Any type of value, including `null`. - `binary`: CloudEvents "Binary" type. - `boolean`: CloudEvents "Boolean" type. - `duration`: ISO 8601 duration in the XML Schema duration lexical profile: OPTIONAL leading `-`, `P`, ordered year/month/day components, and OPTIONAL `T` with ordered hour/minute/second components. At least one component is REQUIRED. Fractions are permitted only on seconds; week notation is not part of this profile. Duration validation MUST NOT narrow the value to a host platform's time interval range. - `integer`: CloudEvents "Integer" type (RFC 7159, Section 6). - `number`: IEEE754 Double. - `string`: CloudEvents "String" type. - `symbol`: A `string` that is restricted to alphanumerical characters and underscores. - `stringified integer`: A `string` containing an OPTIONAL leading `-` followed by one or more decimal digits. This refines a string attribute without changing its JSON value kind. - `timestamp`: CloudEvents "Timestamp" type (RFC3339 DateTime) - `uri`: CloudEvents URI type (RFC3986 URI). - `uritemplate`: [RFC6570][RFC6570] Level 1 URI Template.

review.note: Shared declaration validation preserves null presence behind opaque boundaries, checks exact JSON kinds, fixed property types and numeric/Unicode/Base64/URI/duration rules without weakening Core. Expanded output remains byte-bounded. Exact current source and public assertion evidence; no automatic native-platform or release qualification.
