source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.name`

requirements.text: - REQUIRED.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.name`

requirements.text: - The name of the attribute. MUST be the same as its key in the owning `attributes` map. A value of `*` indicates support for undefined extension names at runtime. Absence of a `*` attribute indicates lack of support for undefined extensions the presence of an unknown attribute at runtime MUST generate an ([unknown_attribute](./spec.md#unknown_attribute)) error.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.name`

requirements.text: Often `*` is used with a `type` of `any` to allow for any undefined extension name of any supported data type. By default, the model does not support undefined extensions. Note that undefined extensions, if supported, MUST adhere to the same rules as [defined extensions](./spec.md#attributes-and-extensions).

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.name`

requirements.text: An attribute of `*` MUST NOT use the `ifvalues` feature, but a non-`*` attribute MAY define an `ifvalues` attribute named `*` as long as there isn't already one defined for this level in the entity.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.name`

requirements.text: An extension attribute MUST NOT use a name that conflicts with any specification-defined attribute, sub-object attribute or collection-related attribute names defined at the same level in the hierarchy. For Resource/Version attributes, this applies for both levels - e.g. a Version-level extension MUST NOT use a name that conflicts with its Resource-level attribute names.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.description`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.type`

requirements.text: - REQUIRED.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.type`

requirements.text: - The "TYPE" of the attribute being defined. MUST be one of the data types (in lower case) defined in [Attributes and Extensions](./spec.md#attributes-and-extensions).

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.enum`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.enum`

requirements.text: - A list of possible values for this attribute. Each item in the array MUST be of the type defined by `type`. When not specified, or an empty array, there are no restrictions on the value set of this attribute. This MUST only be used when the `type` is a scalar. See the `strict` attribute below.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.enum`

requirements.text: When specified without `strict` being `true`, this list is just a suggested set of values and the attribute is NOT REQUIRED to use one of them.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.strict`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.strict`

requirements.text: - Indicates whether the attribute restricts its values to just the array of values specified in `enum` or not. A value of `true` means that any values used that are not part of the `enum` set MUST generate an error ([invalid_attribute](./spec.md#invalid_attribute)). This attribute has no impact when `enum` is absent or an empty array.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.strict`

requirements.text: - When not specified, the default value MUST be `true`.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.target`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.target`

requirements.text: - The type of entity that this attribute points to when `type` is set to `url`, `uri` or `xid`. `target` MUST NOT be used for any other type of attribute.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.target`

requirements.text: - The value of this model attribute MUST be an "xid template" of one of the following forms:

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.target`

requirements.text: - `/<GROUPS>` - a plural Group type name. An entity attribute of this type/target MUST reference an instance of this Group type.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.target`

requirements.text: - `/<GROUPS>/<RESOURCES>` - a plural Resource type name. An entity attribute of this type/target MUST reference an instance of this Resource type, not a specific Version of the Resource.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.target`

requirements.text: - `/<GROUPS>/<RESOURCES>[/versions]`. An entity attribute of this type/target MUST reference either an instance of this Resource type or an instance of a Version of this Resource type. Note the `[/versions]` portion of the `target` value is that exact string, including the square brackets.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.target`

requirements.text: - `/GROUPS/<RESOURCES>/versions` - a Version of a Resource type. An entity attribute of this type/target MUST reference an instance of a Version of this Resource type, not the Resource itself.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.target`

requirements.text: - An `xid` entity attribute that includes a `target` value as part of its model definition MUST match the `target` entity type specified. An `xid` attribute that does not include a `target` definition has no such restriction and MAY be any valid `xid` value.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.target`

requirements.text: - A URI/URL entity attribute MAY include `target` as part of its definition. If so, then any runtime value that is a relative URI/URL (begins with `/`) MUST be an `xid` and MUST adhere to the `target` entity type specified, if specified. Absolute URIs/URLs are not constrained by the presence of a `target` value.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.namecharset`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL, and MUST only be used when `type` is `object`.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.namecharset`

requirements.text: - Specifies the name of the character set that defines the allowable characters that can be used for the object's top-level attribute names. Any attempt to define a top-level attribute for this object that does not adhere to the characters defined by the character set name MUST generate an error ([invalid_attribute](./spec.md#invalid_attribute)).

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.namecharset`

requirements.text: - Per the [Attributes and Extensions](./spec.md#attributes-and-extensions) section, attribute names are normally limited to just the set of characters that ensure they can reliably be used in cases such as code variable names without the need for some escaping mechanism. However, there are situations where object-typed attribute names need to support additional characters, such as a dash (`-`), and it is known that they will never be used in those restricted character set situations. By setting the `namecharset` aspect to `extended` the server MUST allow for an extended set of valid characters in attribute names for this object.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.namecharset`

requirements.text: The allowed character set for attribute names within an `object` MUST also apply to the top-level `siblingattributes` of any `ifvalues` defined for those attributes.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.namecharset`

requirements.text: - When not specified, the default value MUST be `strict`.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.namecharset`

requirements.text: - The value of this attribute MUST be case-insensitive.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.namecharset`

requirements.text: - Implementations MAY define additional character sets, however, an attempt to define a model that uses an unknown character set name MUST generate an error ([model_error](./spec.md#model_error)). There is currently no mechanism defined by this specification to discover the list (or definition) of additional `namecharset` values supported by an implementation. Implementations SHOULD use their documentation to advertise this extension.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.matchversions`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.matchversions`

requirements.text: - Indicates whether all Versions of a Resource instance MUST have the same value for this attribute (or MUST be missing from all Versions). If an inconsistency is found then an error ([mismatched_version_attribute](spec.md#mismatched_version_attribute)) MUST be generated.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.matchversions`

requirements.text: - This aspect MUST only be `true` for attribute definitions that:

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.matchversions`

requirements.text: - When not specified, the default value MUST be `false`.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.readonly`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.readonly`

requirements.text: - Indicates whether this attribute is modifiable by a client. Unless otherwise stated, during creation, or update, of an entity if this attribute is specified, then its value MUST be silently ignored by the server even if the value is invalid. Note that there are some readonly attributes that are examined by a server during a write operation (e.g. `epoch` and IDs).

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.readonly`

requirements.text: - When not specified, the default value MUST be `false`.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.readonly`

requirements.text: - When the attribute name is `*` then `readonly` MUST NOT be set to `true`.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.immutable`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.immutable`

requirements.text: - Indicates whether this attribute's value can be changed once it is set. This MUST ONLY be used for server-controlled specification-defined attributes, such as `specversion` and `<SINGULAR>id`, and MUST NOT be used for extension attributes. As such, it is only for informational purposes for clients.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.immutable`

requirements.text: Once set, any attempt to update the value MUST be silently ignored by the server.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.immutable`

requirements.text: - When not specified, the default value MUST be `false`.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.required`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.required`

requirements.text: - Indicates whether this attribute is REQUIRED to have a non-null value.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.required`

requirements.text: - When set to `true`, this specification does not mandate how this attribute's value is populated (i.e. by a client, the server or via a default value), just that by the end of the server's processing of any request it MUST have a non-null value, and generate an error ([invalid_attribute](./spec.md#invalid_attribute)) if not. Note that this implies that a REQUIRED attribute does not mean that clients are mandated to include that attribute in their requests. If the attribute will automatically be populated by the server (e.g. it has a default value defined) the client MAY omit it.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.required`

requirements.text: - A `true` value also implies that this attribute MUST be serialized in any response from the server - with the exception of the optimizations specified for [document view](./spec.md#registry-model).

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.required`

requirements.text: - When not specified the default value MUST be `false`.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.required`

requirements.text: - When the attribute name is `*` then `required` MUST NOT be set to `true`.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.required`

requirements.text: - When a default value (`attributes.<STRING>.default`) is defined, then this aspect MUST be `true`, otherwise an error ([model_required_true](./spec.md#model_required_true)) MUST be generated.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.default`

requirements.text: - Type: MUST be a non-`null` value of the type specified by the `attributes.<STRING>.type` model attribute and MUST only be used for scalar types. Attempts to define a `default` value for a non-scalar type MUST generate an error ([model_scalar_default](./spec.md#model_scalar_default)).

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.default`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.default`

requirements.text: - This value MUST be used to populate this attribute's value if one was not provided by a client. An attribute with a default value does not mean that its owning Object is mandated to be present; rather the attribute would only appear when the owning Object is present. By default, attributes have no default values.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.default`

requirements.text: - When a default value is specified, this attribute MUST be serialized in responses from servers as part of its owning entity, even if it is set to its default value. This means that any attribute that has a default value defined MUST also have its `required` aspect set to `true`.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.default`

requirements.text: - If the default value of an attribute changes over time, all existing instances of that attribute MUST retain their current values and not be automatically changed to the new default value. In other words, a new default value MUST only apply to new or subsequent updates (when set to `null`, which would reset it to the current default value) of existing instances of the attribute.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.default`

requirements.text: - If the attribute is defined to have an `enum` list, and its `strict` aspect is `true`, then if a `default` value is specified it MUST be one of those `enum` values.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.attributes`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.attributes`

requirements.text: - MAY be present when the owning attribute's `type` is `object`, otherwise it MUST NOT be present. It MAY be absent or an empty list if there are no defined attributes for the nested `object`.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.item`

requirements.text: - REQUIRED when owning attribute's `type` is `map` or `array`.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.item`

requirements.text: - Defines the nested entity that this attribute references. This attribute MUST only be used when the owning attribute's `type` value is `map` or `array`.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.item.type`

requirements.text: - REQUIRED.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.item.enum`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL, and MUST only be used when `item.type` is a scalar.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.item.strict`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL, and this attribute has no impact when `item.enum` is absent or an empty array.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.item.target`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL, and MUST only be used when `item.type` is `url`, `uri` or `xid`.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.item.namecharset`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL, and MUST only be used when `item.type` is `object`.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.item.attributes`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL, and MUST ONLY be used when `item.type` is `object`.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.item.item`

requirements.text: - REQUIRED when `item.type` is `map` or `array`.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.ifvalues`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.ifvalues`

requirements.text: - This map can be used to conditionally include additional attribute definitions based on the runtime value of the current attribute. If the string serialization of the runtime value of this attribute matches the `ifvalues` key (case-insensitive), then the `siblingattributes` MUST be included in the model as siblings to this attribute.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.ifvalues`

requirements.text: While maps will automatically prevent two entries with the same key, they will not prevent two entries that only differ in case. Therefore, during a model update, servers MUST ensure that no two entries are the same irrespective of case, otherwise an error ([model_error](./spec.md#model_error)) MUST be generated.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.ifvalues`

requirements.text: If attribute's `enum` aspect is not empty and its `strict` aspect is `true` then this map MUST NOT contain any value that is not specified in the `enum` array.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.ifvalues`

requirements.text: This aspect MUST only be used for scalar attributes.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.ifvalues`

requirements.text: All attributes defined for this `ifvalues` MUST be unique within the scope of this `ifvalues` and MUST NOT match a named attribute defined at this level of the entity. If multiple `ifvalues` sections, at the same entity level, are active at the same time then there MUST NOT be duplicate `ifvalues` attribute names between those `ifvalues` sections and a runtime error ([invalid_attribute](./spec.md#invalid_attribute)) MUST be generated.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.ifvalues`

requirements.text: - `ifvalues` `<STRING>` MUST NOT be an empty string.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.ifvalues`

requirements.text: - `ifvalues` `<STRING>` MUST NOT start with the `^` (caret) character as its presence at the beginning of `<STRING>` is reserved for future use.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `attributes.<STRING>.ifvalues`

requirements.text: - `ifvalues` `siblingattributes` MAY include additional `ifvalues` definitions.

requirements.text: - Type: Map where the key MUST be the plural name (`groups.plural`) of the Group type (`<GROUPS>`) being defined.

requirements.text: - REQUIRED if there are any Group types defined for the Registry.

requirements.text: - REQUIRED.

requirements.text: - MUST be unique across all Group types (plural and singular names) in the Registry.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.plural`

requirements.text: - MUST be non-empty and MUST be a valid attribute name with the exception that it MUST NOT exceed 57 characters (not 63).

requirements.text: - REQUIRED.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.singular`

requirements.text: - MUST be immutable.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.singular`

requirements.text: - MUST be unique across all Group types (plural and singular names) in the Registry.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.singular`

requirements.text: - MUST be non-empty and MUST be a valid attribute name. For clarity, it MUST NOT exceed 61 characters.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.constraints`

requirements.text: These restrictions are designed to only allow subsetting of the constraints specified by the Resource type model. They MUST NOT be used to extend the allowable values of the attributes being constrained.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.constraints`

requirements.text: The format of a constraint map MUST adhere to the following:

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.constraints`

requirements.text: These constraints MUST be applied to all instances of this Group type. Group instances MAY choose to add additional entries, or further restrict the ones defined here, via use of the Group instance's [`constraints` attribute](./spec.md#constraints-attribute).

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.constraints`

requirements.text: The constraints MUST be applied to all Versions of all Resources in the Group instances, and generate an error ([constraint_failure](./spec.md#constraint_failure)) if a violation is detected.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.constraints`

requirements.text: - The `enum` and `equals` constraints, if specified, MUST be adhered to by the Resource. Note that this includes changes to the Resource in its original location that would then violate any of the Groups' constraints that xref that Resource.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.constraints`

requirements.text: - The `default` values specified MUST NOT be applied to the Resource since its presence in the Group is just a "reference" (or "read-only"). Write operations on the Resource need to be done in its original location.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.constraints.<RESOURCES>.<PATH>`

requirements.text: This map key MUST reference the Resource attribute that is to be constrained. It MUST reference a scalar attribute (top-level, or nested within objects) but MUST NOT reference items in arrays or maps. It MUST only reference statically-defined attributes, not ones that are dynamically added via an `ifvalues` clause or via a `*` extension definition.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.constraints.<RESOURCES>.<PATH>`

requirements.text: The `<RESOURCES>` portion of the map key MUST be the plural name of the Resource type being referenced.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.constraints.<RESOURCES>.<PATH>`

requirements.text: The `<PATH>` portion of the map key MUST be a [dot (`.`) notation](spec.md#xregistry-dot--notation) traversal to the Resource attribute being constrained.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.constraints.<RESOURCES>.<PATH>.default`

requirements.text: This aspect defines the default value that MUST be used for the referenced Resource attribute. This Group type value MUST override any default value specified in the model for that attribute.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.constraints.<RESOURCES>.<PATH>.default`

requirements.text: Note, if the constraint does not define a new `enum` set, but a `default` value is defined, then if the referenced attribute has an `enum` set and has its `strict` aspect set to `true` then this `default` value MUST be one of those `enum` values.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.constraints.<RESOURCES>.<PATH>.enum`

requirements.text: This aspect defines the set of values that the referenced Resource attribute MUST be restricted to regardless of whether the Resource's [`strict`](#attributesstringstrict) attribute is set to `true` or not. The list's values MUST be valid per the Resource attribute's model definition (i.e. a proper subset of any `enum` defined if the Resource's `enum` is [`strict`](#attributesstringstrict), and of the same type).

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.constraints.<RESOURCES>.<PATH>.enum`

requirements.text: As with the [`enum` attribute](#attributesstringenum) defined for attributes, an empty `enum` list in a constraint MUST be treated the same as no `enum` aspect at all and no further constraints on the allowable attribute values are applied beyond what the attribute itself defines.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.constraints.<RESOURCES>.<PATH>.enum`

requirements.text: If an `enum` set is defined, but a constraint `default` value is not, then any `default` value specified in the attribute itself MUST be part of the `enum` set.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.constraints.<RESOURCES>.<PATH>.equals`

requirements.text: Use of this aspect within a constraint MAY be used to ensure that the specified attribute in all Versions of all Resources within a Group instance is present with the same value as the specified `equals` attribute in the Group instance.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.constraints.<RESOURCES>.<PATH>.equals`

requirements.text: When specified with an empty string, it MUST be treated as if it were not specified at all.

requirements.text: - Indicates the algorithm that MUST be used when determining how Version's `ancestorid` attribute is managed (or calculated).

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.versionmode`

requirements.text: - Implementations MAY define additional algorithms and MAY define additional aspects that they control, as long as those aspects do not conflict with specification-defined semantics.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.versionmode`

requirements.text: - Regardless of the algorithm used, implementations MUST ensure that the `ancestorid` attribute of all Versions of a Resource accurately represents the relationship of the Versions prior to the completion of any operation that created, modifies or deletes Versions. For example, when the `createdat` algorithm is used and the `createdat` timestamp of a Version is modified, this might cause a reordering of the Versions and the `ancestorid` attributes might need to be changed accordingly. Similarly, the `defaultversionid` of the Resource might change if its `defaultversionsticky` attribute is `false`.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.versionmode`

requirements.text: - When not specified, the default value MUST be `manual`.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.versionmode`

requirements.text: - Implementations MUST support at least `manual`.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.versionmode`

requirements.text: - The value of this attribute MUST be case-insensitive.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.versionmode`

requirements.text: - The "newest" Version MUST be determined by finding all "leaf" Versions (ones that are not referenced as an ancestor of any other Version), and choosing the one with the newest `createdat` timestamp. If there is more than one, then the one with the highest alphabetically case-insensitive `versionid` value MUST be chosen.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.versionmode`

requirements.text: - The "oldest" Version MUST be determined by finding all "root" Versions (ones that have an `ancestorid` value that points to itself), and then choosing the one with the oldest `createdat` timestamp. If there is more than one, then the one with the lowest alphabetically case-insensitive `versionid` value MUST be chosen.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.versionmode`

requirements.text: - `manual` - Ancestor Processing: typically provided by clients. During a "create" operation, all new Versions that do not have an `ancestorid` value provided MUST be sorted/processed by `versionid` (in case-insensitive ascending order) and the `ancestorid` value of each MUST be set to the current "newest Version" per the above semantics. Note that as each new Version is processed, it will likely become the "newest" but it might not if its `createdat` timestamp is in the past. If there is no existing Version then the new Version becomes a root and its `ancestorid` value MUST be its own `versionid` attribute value. - Deleted Ancestor: if a Version's ancestor is deleted, then it MUST become a root, and its `ancestorid` MUST be set to its own `versionid` value. - The name of this versionmode is a bit of a misnomer in that it is not 100% "manual". As stated above, as a convenience, by default new Versions will point to the "newest" Version as their ancestor. If this behavior is not desired, then during the "create" operation, the `ancestorid` can be set to point to itself (or any other Version).

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.versionmode`

requirements.text: - `createdat` - Ancestor Processing: The `ancestorid` value of each Version MUST be determined via examination of the `createdat` timestamp of each Version and the Versions sorted in ascending order, where the first one will be the "root" (oldest) Version and its `ancestorid` value MUST be its `versionid`. If there is more than one Version with the same `createdat` timestamp then those MUST be ordered in ascending case-insensitive order based on their `versionid` values. - When this `versionmode` is used, the `singleversionroot` aspect MUST be set to `true`.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.versionmode`

requirements.text: - `modifiedat` - This is the same as the `createdat` algorithm except that the `modifiedat` attribute of each Version MUST be used instead of the `createdat` attribute.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Registry Model / `groups.<STRING>.resources.<STRING>.versionmode`

requirements.text: - `semver` - Ancestor Processing: The `ancestorid` value of each Version MUST either be its `versionid` value (if it is the oldest Version), or the `versionid` of the next oldest Version per the [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/) specification's "precedence" ordering rules. - When this `versionmode` is used, the `singleversionroot` aspect MUST be set to `true`.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Retrieving the Registry Model

requirements.text: The full "model" view can be thought of as a full schema definition of what the message exchanges with the server might look like. As such, it MUST include:

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Retrieving the Registry Model

requirements.text: - Registry top-level and Group `<COLLECTION>*` attributes. While the `model` and `modelsource` attributes MUST appear, their definitions MAY be shallow - meaning, they can be defined as just `object` with one attribute (`*`) of type "any".

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Retrieving the Registry Model

requirements.text: The "modelsource" view of the model is just what was provided by the user when the model was defined, or last edited. It is expected that this view of the model is much smaller than the full model and only includes domain-specific information. While specification-defined attributes MAY appear in this document, they are NOT RECOMMENDED since the server will automatically add them so users do not need to concern themselves with those details.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Retrieving the Registry Model

requirements.text: When retrieving the `modelsource`, the response MUST only include what was specified in the request to define the model - it MUST NOT include any auto-added specification defined metadata that will appear under `model`.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model

requirements.text: A server MAY support updating the model of a Registry via:

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model

requirements.text: - Changes to specification-defined attributes MAY be included in the model but MUST NOT change them such that they become incompatible with the specification. For example, changes to further constrain the allowable values of an attribute are typically allowed, but changing its `type` from `string` to `integer` is not.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model

requirements.text: - Specification-defined attributes that are `required` MUST NOT have this aspect changed to `false`.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model

requirements.text: - Specification-defined attributes that are `readonly` MUST NOT have this aspect changed to `false`.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model

requirements.text: - Specification-defined attributes that define a `default` value MUST always include a `default` value in their definitions.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model

requirements.text: Any specification attributes not included in a request to define, or update, a model MUST be included in the resulting full model. In other words, the full Registry's model consists of the specification-defined attributes overlaid with the attributes that are explicitly-defined as part of a `modelsource` update request.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model

requirements.text: Registries MAY support extension attributes to the model language (meaning, new attributes within the model definitions themselves), but only if the server supports them. Servers MUST generate an error ([model_error](./spec.md#model_error)) if a model definition includes unknown model language attributes.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model

requirements.text: Once a Registry has been created, changes to the model MAY be supported by server implementations. This specification makes no statement as to what types of changes are allowed beyond the following requirements:

requirements.text: - Any model change MUST result in a specification compliant model definition.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model

requirements.text: - Servers MUST ensure that the representation of all entities within the Registry adheres to the new model prior to completing the model update request.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model

requirements.text: Any request to update the model that does not adhere to those requirements MUST generate an error ([model_compliance_error](./spec.md#model_compliance_error)).

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model

requirements.text: How the server guarantees that all entities in the Registry are compliant with the model is an implementation detail. For example, while it is NOT RECOMMENDED, it is valid for an implementation to modify (or even delete) existing entities to ensure model compliance. Instead, it is RECOMMENDED that the model update requests generate an error ([model_compliance_error](./spec.md#model_compliance_error)) if existing entities are not compliant.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model

requirements.text: For the purposes of validating that the existing entities in the Registry are compliant with the model, the mechanisms used to define the model (e.g. `$include` vs `ximportresources` vs defined locally) MUST NOT impact that analysis. In other words, model updates that have no semantic changes but rather switch between one of those 3 mechanisms MUST NOT invalidate any existing entities in the Registry.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model

requirements.text: Additionally, it is STRONGLY RECOMMENDED that model updates be limited to backwards compatible changes.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model

requirements.text: Implementations MAY choose to limit the types of changes made to the model, or not support model updates at all.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model / Reuse of Resource Definitions

requirements.text: When a Resource type definition is to be shared between Groups, rather than creating a duplicate Resource definition, the `ximportresources` mechanism MAY be used instead. The `ximportresources` attribute on a Group definition allows for a list of `<XIDTYPE>` references to other Resource types to be included within this Group.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model / Reuse of Resource Definitions

requirements.text: - Each array value MUST be an `<XIDTYPE>` reference to another Group/Resource combination defined within the same Registry. It MUST NOT reference the same Group under which the `ximportresources` resides.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model / Reuse of Resource Definitions

requirements.text: - An empty array MAY be specified, implying no Resources are imported.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model / Reuse of Resource Definitions

requirements.text: - The definition of a Group MAY include an `ximportresources` directive that references a Resource from another Group that itself is defined via an `ximportresources`. However, transitive definitions of Resources MUST NOT result in a circular import chain.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model / Reuse of Resource Definitions

requirements.text: Locally defined Resources MAY be defined within a Group that uses the `ximportresources` feature; however, Resource `plural` and `singular` values MUST be unique across all imported and locally defined Resources.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model / Reuse of Resource Definitions

requirements.text: This attribute, while listed in the schema definition of `model`, and `modelsource` for ease of reading the specification, is only available for `modelsource`. Similar to the `$include` directive, servers MUST process any `ximportresources` found in the `modelsource` data and the results MUST be reflected in the `model`, but the `ximportresources` directive MUST NOT appear in the `model` serialization.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model / Includes in the xRegistry Model Data

requirements.text: There might be times when it is necessary for an xRegistry model to reuse portions of another xRegistry model defined elsewhere. Rather than forcing the duplication of the model definitions, an "include" type of JSON directive MAY be used.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model / Includes in the xRegistry Model Data

requirements.text: where the first form specifies a single reference to be included, and the second form specifies multiple. The fragment (`#...`) portion is OPTIONAL.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model / Includes in the xRegistry Model Data

requirements.text: These directives MAY be used in any JSON Object or Map entity in an xRegistry model definition. The following rules apply to how the include directive is processed:

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model / Includes in the xRegistry Model Data

requirements.text: - The include path reference value MUST be compatible with the environment in which the `include` is being evaluated. For example, in an xRegistry server it would most likely always be a URL. However, in an external tool the reference might be to a local file on disk or a URL.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model / Includes in the xRegistry Model Data

requirements.text: - The include MUST reference a JSON Object or Map that is consistent with the model definition of where the include appears, and the target attributes, or keys, are processed in place of the `$include` attribute.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model / Includes in the xRegistry Model Data

requirements.text: - Any attributes already present (as siblings to the include) MUST take precedence over an included attribute - matching is done via comparing the `name` of the attributes.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model / Includes in the xRegistry Model Data

requirements.text: - When `$includes` is used, the references MUST be processed in order and earlier attributes included take precedence over subsequently included attributes.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model / Includes in the xRegistry Model Data

requirements.text: - Both `$include` and `$includes` MUST NOT be present at the same time at the same level in the model.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model / Includes in the xRegistry Model Data

requirements.text: - Included model definitions MAY use `include` directives, but MUST NOT result in a circular include chain.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model / Includes in the xRegistry Model Data

requirements.text: - Resolution of the include path MUST follow standard path resolution. Meaning, relative paths are relative to the document with the include directive.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model / Includes in the xRegistry Model Data

requirements.text: - If present, the fragment (`#...`) part of the reference MUST adhere to the [JSON Pointer](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6901) specification.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model / Includes in the xRegistry Model Data

requirements.text: When the directives are used in a request to update the model, the server MUST resolve all includes prior to updating the model. The original (source) model definition, with any "include" directives, MUST be available via the `modelsource` attribute/entity. The expanded model (after the resolution of any includes, and after all specification-defined attributes have been added), MUST be available via the `model` attribute/entity. The directives MUST only be processed during the initial update of the model. In order to have them re-evaluated, a subsequent model update request (with those directives) MUST be sent.

source.section: xRegistry Service Model - Version 1.0-rc4 / Creating or Updating the Registry Model / Includes in the xRegistry Model Data

requirements.text: When there is tooling used outside of the server, e.g. in an xRegistry client, if that tooling resolves the "include" directives prior to sending the model to the server, then the directives will not appear in the `modelsource` view of the model. Ideally, tooling SHOULD allow users to choose whether the resolution of the directives is done locally or by the server.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Notations and Terminology / Notational Conventions

requirements.text: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in [RFC 2119](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2119).

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Notations and Terminology / Notational Conventions

requirements.text: For clarity, OPTIONAL attributes (specification-defined and extensions) are OPTIONAL for clients to use, but the servers' responsibility will vary. Server-unknown extension attributes MUST be silently stored in the backing datastore. Specification-defined attributes and server-known extension attributes MUST generate an error if the corresponding feature is not supported or enabled. However, as with all attributes, if accepting the attribute results in a bad state (such as exceeding a size limit or resulting in a security issue), then the server MAY choose to reject the request.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Notations and Terminology / Notational Conventions

requirements.text: In the pseudo JSON format snippets `?` means the preceding item is OPTIONAL, `*` means the preceding item MAY appear zero or more times, and `+` means the preceding item MUST appear at least once. The presence of the `#` character means the remaining portion of the line is a comment. Whitespace characters in the JSON snippets are used for readability and are not normative.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Binding Overview / HTTP API Patterns

requirements.text: While these APIs are shown to be at the root path of a host, implementations MAY choose to prefix them as necessary. However, the same prefix MUST be used consistently for all APIs in the same Registry instance.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Binding Overview / HTTP API Patterns

requirements.text: If an OPTIONAL HTTP path is not supported by an implementation, then any use of that API MUST generate an error ([api_not_found](#api_not_found)).

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Binding Overview / HTTP API Patterns

requirements.text: If an HTTP method is not supported for a supported HTTP path, then an error ([action_not_supported](./spec.md#action_not_supported)) MUST be generated.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Binding Overview / HTTP API Patterns

requirements.text: Implementations MAY support extension APIs, however, the following rules apply:

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Binding Overview / HTTP API Patterns

requirements.text: - New HTTP paths that extend non-root paths MUST NOT be defined as they might conflict with URLs of entities within the system.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Binding Overview / HTTP API Patterns

requirements.text: - New root HTTP paths MAY be defined as long as they do not use Registry-level HTTP paths or attribute names. This includes extension and Groups collection attribute names.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Binding Overview / Adherence to HTTP Standards

requirements.text: - A `PUT` or `POST` operation is a full replacement of the entities processed. Any missing attributes MUST be interpreted as a request for them to be deleted. However, attributes that are managed by the server might have specialized processing in those cases, in particular, mandatory attributes, as well as ones that have default values defined, MUST be reset to their default values rather than deleted.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Binding Overview / Adherence to HTTP Standards

requirements.text: - A `PATCH` operation MUST only modify the attributes explicitly mentioned in the request. Any attribute in the request with a value of `null` MUST be interpreted as a request to delete the attribute, and as with `PUT`/`POST`, server-managed attributes might have specialized processing.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Binding Overview / Adherence to HTTP Standards

requirements.text: - `PUT` MUST NOT be targeted at xRegistry collections. A `POST` or `PATCH` MUST be used instead to add entities to the collection, and a `DELETE` MUST then be used to delete unwanted entities.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Binding Overview / Adherence to HTTP Standards

requirements.text: - Unknown query parameters SHOULD be silently ignored by servers. This includes specification-defined but unsupported query parameters.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Binding Overview / No-Code Servers

requirements.text: In the [core specification](./spec.md) there is a discussion about ["no-code servers"](./spec.md#design-no-code-servers). In the case of HTTP, simple file servers SHOULD support exposing Resources where the HTTP body response contains the Resource's domain-specific "document" as well as exposing the serialization of the Resource's xRegistry metadata via the [`$details`](#resource-metadata-vs-resource-document) suffix on the URL path. This can be achieved by creating a secondary, sibling, file on disk with `$details` at the end of its filename.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs

requirements.text: This section mainly focuses on the successful interaction patterns of the APIs. For example, most examples will show an HTTP "200 OK" as the response. Each implementation MAY choose to return a more appropriate response based on the specific situation. For example, in the case of an authentication error the server could return `401 Unauthorized`.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: Creating or updating entities MAY be done using HTTP `PUT`, `PATCH` or `POST` methods:

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: See the [`Request Flags`](#request-flags--query-parameters) section for the list of flags/query parameters that MAY be used for each API.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: The `PUT` variant MUST adhere to the following:

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - The URL MUST be of the form: `<PATH-TO-ENTITY>`.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - The HTTP body MUST contain the full updated serialization of the entity to be processed.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - The entity processed MUST either be created (if it does not already exist), or updated (if it does exist).

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - Any mutable attribute which is either missing or present with a value of `null`, MUST be interpreted as a request to delete the attribute.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - Excluding any Registry collection attributes, all mutable attributes specified MUST be a full serialization of the attribute. Any missing nested attribute MUST be interpreted as a request to delete the attribute.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - After processing the request, if there are any missing REQUIRED attributes then an error ([required_attribute_missing](./spec.md#required_attribute_missing)) MUST be generated.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: The `PATCH` variant when directed at a single entity, MUST adhere to the `PUT` semantics defined above with the following exceptions:

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - Any mutable attribute which is missing MUST be interpreted as a request to leave it unchanged. However, modifying some other attribute (or some other server semantics) MAY modify it. A value of `null` MUST be interpreted as a request to delete the attribute.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - When processing a Resource or Version, whose Resource type has its [`hasdocument`](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringhasdocument) model aspect set to `true`, the URL accessing the entity MUST include the `$details` suffix, and MUST generate an error ([details_required](#details_required)) in the absence of the `$details` suffix. This is because when it is absent, the processing of the HTTP `xRegistry-` headers are already defined with "PATCH" semantics so a normal `PUT` or `POST` can be used instead. Using `PATCH` in this case would mean that the request is trying to "patch" the Resource's "document", which this specification does not support at this time.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - `PATCH` MAY be used to create new entities, but as with any of the create operations, any missing REQUIRED attributes MUST generate an error ([required_attribute_missing](./spec.md#required_attribute_missing)).

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: The `POST` variant when directed at a single entity other than a Resource, MUST adhere to the following:

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - The HTTP body MUST contain only a JSON map where the key MUST be the attribute (collection) name of a nested xRegistry collection. The value of each map entry MUST be a map of nested entities where the key is the entity's `<SINGULAR>id` and the value is a serialization of the entity itself.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - The processing of each top-level map entry MUST follow the same rules as defined for `POST` to the nested xRegistry collection where the map entry's value is the input.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - The root of the JSON object in the HTTP body MUST NOT contain any attributes of the targeted entity other than the nested collections, and none of that entity's attribute are to be updated. This operation allows for an update to multiple nested collections in a single operation without modifying the owning entity.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - The response message MUST be a map of the nested entity types with just the changed entities that were processed. No top-level entity attributes are to appear - similar to the request message.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: The `POST` variant when directed at a Resource entity, MUST adhere to the following:

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - The HTTP body MUST contain the serialization of the single Version to be created, however, it MAY include Resource-level read-only attributes (such as `versionscount`), and if they are present, then they MUST be silently ignored by the server. This is done as a convenience for users who might have obtained the Version's serialization from a query to a Resource (not a specific Version), in which case those extra Resource-level attributes would be included in the serialization.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - The 'PUT' variant rules above MUST apply to the new Version entity.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: The `PATCH` variant when directed at an xRegistry collection, MUST adhere to the following:

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - The HTTP body MUST contain a JSON map where the key MUST be the `<SINGULAR>id` of each entity in the map. Note, that in the case of a map of Versions, the `versionid` is used.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - Each value in the map MUST contain just the attributes that are to be updated for that entity.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - The processing of each individual entity in the map MUST follow the same rules as defined for `PATCH` of a single entity above.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: The `POST` variant when directed at an xRegistry collection MUST adhere to the following:

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - The HTTP body MUST contain a JSON map where the key MUST be the `<SINGULAR>id` of each entity in the map. Note, that in the case of a map of Versions, the `versionid` is used.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - Each value in the map MUST be the full serialization of the entity to be either added or updated. Note that `POST` does not support deleting entities from a collection, so a separate delete operation might be needed if there are entities that need to be removed.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - The processing of each individual entity in the map MUST follow the same rules as defined for `PUT` above.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - In the case of an empty map of Versions and the Resource being referenced does not exist yet, an error ([missing_versions](#missing_versions)) MUST be generated because a Resource can not exist without any Versions. If the intent was to create a Resource with a Version that has just default values, then there are other APIs that can be used that make that intent clear (e.g. `PUT` to the Resource itself).

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - If an entity with the specified `<SINGULAR>id` already exists then it MUST be interpreted as a request to update the existing entity. Otherwise, it MUST be interpreted as a request to create a new entity with that `<SINGULAR>id`.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - Unless otherwise noted, all non-xRegistry collection attributes present MUST be a full representation of their values. This means any complex attributes (e.g. objects, maps), MUST be fully replaced by the incoming value.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - A request to update, or delete, a read-only attribute MUST be silently ignored. However, a request that includes a `<SINGULAR>id` MUST be compared with the entity's current value and if it differs then an error ([mismatched_id](./spec.md#mismatched_id)) MUST be generated. This includes both `<RESOURCE>id` and `versionid` in the case of Resources and Versions. This is to prevent accidentally updating the wrong entity.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - A request to update a mutable attribute with an invalid value MUST generate an error ([invalid_attribute](./spec.md#invalid_attribute)) (this includes deleting a mandatory mutable attribute that has no default value defined).

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - Registry collection attributes MUST be processed per the rules specified in the [Updating Nested Registry Collections](./spec.md#updating-nested-registry-collections) section.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - Write operations that are meant to include xRegistry metadata in the HTTP body MUST NOT be empty, and if detected MUST generate an error ([missing_body](#missing_body)). To denote an empty set of metadata, `{}` MUST be used instead.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - Any error during the processing of an entity, or its nested entities, MUST result in the entire request being rejected and no updates performed.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - When a write operation request includes the Resource/Version's metadata in the HTTP body, then the inclusion of any xRegistry `xRegistry-` HTTP headers MUST generate an error ([extra_xregistry_header](#extra_xregistry_header)).

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - When a write operation request includes a domain-specific document in the HTTP body, and the `<RESOURCE>url` xRegistry HTTP header is present with a non-null value, the HTTP body MUST be empty. If the `<RESOURCE>url` attribute is absent, then the contents of the HTTP body (even if empty) are to be used as the entity's document.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - The `<RESOURCE>` and `<RESOURCEbase64>` attributes MUST never appear as xRegistry HTTP headers, and if present on a write request MUST generate an error ([extra_xregistry_header](#extra_xregistry_header)).

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: A successful response MUST return the same response as a `GET` to the entity (or entities) processed, showing their current representation in the same format (`$details` variant or not) as the request, with the following exceptions:

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - In the `POST` case, or a `PATCH` directed to an xRegistry collection, the result MUST contain only the entities processed, not the entire Registry collection.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - In the `PUT` or `PATCH` cases that are directed to a single entity, for a newly created entity, the HTTP status MUST be `201 Created`, and it MUST include an HTTP `Location` header with a URL to the newly created entity. Note that this URL MUST be the same as the `self` attribute of that entity.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - In the `PUT` or `PATCH` cases directed at a single Resource or Version, if a new Version was created, the response MUST include a `Content-Location` HTTP header to the newly created Version entity, and it MUST be the same as the Version's `self` attribute.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: - The responses MUST NOT include any inlineable attributes (such as `<RESOURCE>`, `<RESOURCE>base64` or nested objects/collections) unless requested.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: Otherwise an HTTP `200 OK` without an HTTP `Location` header MUST be returned.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities

requirements.text: Note that the response MUST be generated applying the semantics of any [request flags](#request-flags--query-parameters) specified in the request URL (e.g. `?inline`).

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Creating or Updating Entities / xRegistry Root HTTP Header

requirements.text: All API responses, including errors, SHOULD include a `Link` HTTP header of the form:

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / HTTP-Specific Attribute Processing Rules / `self` Attribute

requirements.text: - When serializing Resources and Versions, whose Resource type's [`hasdocument`](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringhasdocument) aspect is set to `true`, then this URL MUST include the `$details` suffix appended to its `<SINGULAR>id` if it is serialized in the the HTTP body response. If the aspect is set to `false` then it MUST NOT include it. This rule applies even if the URL used in a request message did include the suffix.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / HTTP-Specific Attribute Processing Rules / `labels` Attribute

requirements.text: - When `labels` is serialized as an HTTP header, see [Serializing Resource Domain-Specific Documents](#serializing-resource-domain-specific-documents), then each map entry MUST appear as a separate HTTP header using a name of `xRegistry-labels.<KEYNAME>`.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / HTTP-Specific Attribute Processing Rules / `contenttype` Attribute

requirements.text: - When this attribute is serialized as an HTTP header, it MUST use the name `Content-Type` and not `xRegistry-contenttype`.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / HTTP-Specific Attribute Processing Rules / `contenttype` Attribute

requirements.text: - On an update request when the xRegistry metadata appears in HTTP headers, unlike other attributes that will remain unchanged when not specified, this attribute MUST be erased if the incoming request does not include the `Content-Type` HTTP header.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / HTTP-Specific Attribute Processing Rules / `<RESOURCE>` Attribute

requirements.text: - When a Resource or Version's attributes are serialized as HTTP headers, this attribute MUST NOT be included in the list.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / HTTP-Specific Attribute Processing Rules / `<RESOURCE>base64` Attribute

requirements.text: - When a Resource or Version's attributes are serialized as HTTP headers, this attribute MUST NOT be included in the list.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Pagination

requirements.text: Since xRegistry collections (i.e. the `<COLLECTION>` attribute) could be too large to retrieve in a single request, when retrieving a collection, the client MAY request a subset by using the [pagination specification](../pagination/spec.md). Likewise, the server MAY choose to return a subset of the collection using the same mechanism defined in that specification even if the request didn't ask for pagination. The pagination specification MUST only be used when the request is directed at a collection, not at its owning entity (such as the root of the Registry, or at an individual Group or Resource).

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Entity Processing Rules / Pagination

requirements.text: In the remainder of this specification, the presence of the `Link` HTTP header indicates that the [pagination specification](../pagination/spec.md) MAY be used for that API.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Resource Entity / Resource Metadata vs Resource Document

requirements.text: The core specification's [Resource Metadata vs Resource Document](./spec.md#resource-metadata-vs-resource-document) section explains how Resource types might be defined to have a domain-specific document associated with them via their [`hasdocument` model aspect](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringhasdocument) being set to `true`. For HTTP, clients indicate whether they want to interact with the Resource's xRegistry metadata or the Resource's domain-specific document by the use of a `$details` suffix on the `<RESOURCE>id` in its URL. Presence of the `$details` suffix MUST be interpreted as a request to interact with the xRegistry metadata of the Resource, while its absence MUST be interpreted as a request to interact with the Resource's domain-specific document.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Resource Entity / Resource Metadata vs Resource Document

requirements.text: Use of `$details` on a non-Resource entity MUST generate an error ([bad_details](./spec.md#bad_details)).

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Resource Entity / Resource Metadata vs Resource Document

requirements.text: If a Resource type does not support domain-specific documents (i.e. [`hasdocument`](./model.md#groupsstringresourcesstringhasdocument) is set to `false`), then use of the `$details` suffix in a request URL MUST be treated the same as if it were absent and any URLs in server response messages referencing that Resource (e.g. `self`) MUST NOT include it.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Resource Entity / Resource Metadata vs Resource Document / Serializing Resource Domain-Specific Documents

requirements.text: When a Resource is serialized as its underlying domain-specific document, in other words `$details` is not appended to its URL path, the HTTP body of requests and responses MUST be the exact bytes of that document. If the document is empty, then the HTTP body MUST be empty (zero length).

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Resource Entity / Resource Metadata vs Resource Document / Serializing Resource Domain-Specific Documents

requirements.text: In this serialization mode, it might be useful for clients to also interact with some of the Resource's xRegistry metadata. To support this, some of the Resource's xRegistry metadata MAY appear as HTTP headers in messages.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Resource Entity / Resource Metadata vs Resource Document / Serializing Resource Domain-Specific Documents

requirements.text: On responses, unless otherwise stated, all top-level scalar attributes of the Resource SHOULD appear as HTTP headers where the header name is the name of the attribute prefixed with `xRegistry-`. Note, the optionality of this requirement is not to allow for servers to decide whether or not to do so, rather it is to allow for [No-Code Servers](#no-code-servers) that might not be able to control the HTTP response headers.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Resource Entity / Resource Metadata vs Resource Document / Serializing Resource Domain-Specific Documents

requirements.text: The `<RESOURCE>` and `<RESOURCEbase64>` attributes MUST NOT be serialized as HTTP headers, even if their values can be considered "scalar", because their values will appear in the HTTP body.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Resource Entity / Resource Metadata vs Resource Document / Serializing Resource Domain-Specific Documents

requirements.text: Top-level map attributes whose values are of scalar types SHOULD also appear as HTTP headers (each key having its own HTTP header) and in those cases the HTTP header names will be of the form: `xRegistry-<MAPNAME>.<KEYNAME>`. Note that map keys MAY contain the `.` character, so any `.` after the `<MAPNAME>.` is part of the key name. See [HTTP Header Processing](#http-header-processing) for additional information and [`labels`](#labels-attribute) for an example of one such attribute.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Resource Entity / Resource Metadata vs Resource Document / Serializing Resource Domain-Specific Documents

requirements.text: Complex top-level attributes (e.g. arrays, objects, non-scalar maps) MUST NOT appear as HTTP headers.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Resource Entity / Resource Metadata vs Resource Document / Serializing Resource Domain-Specific Documents

requirements.text: On update requests, similar serialization rules apply. However, rather than these headers being REQUIRED, the client would only need to include those top-level attributes that they would like to change. But, including unchanged attributes MAY be done. Unless otherwise stated, any attributes not included in request messages MUST be interpreted as a request to leave their values unchanged. Using a value of `null` (case-sensitive) MUST be processed as a request to delete that attribute.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Registry HTTP APIs / Resource Entity / Resource Metadata vs Resource Document / Serializing Resource Domain-Specific Documents

requirements.text: Any top-level map attributes that appear as HTTP headers MUST be included in their entirety and any missing keys MUST be interpreted as a request to delete those keys from the map.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Request Flags / Query Parameters

requirements.text: The [core xRegistry specification](./spec.md) defines a set of [request flags](./spec.md#request-flags) that MAY be used to control the processing of requests as well as influence how response messages are generated. Each flag is mapped to an HTTP query parameter per the following rules:

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Request Flags / Query Parameters

requirements.text: - When the flag is a boolean type of flag then it MUST be serialized as `?FLAG_NAME`, all lower case.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Request Flags / Query Parameters

requirements.text: - When the flag has a single value associated with it, then it MUST be serialized as `?FLAG_NAME=VALUE`, where the `FLAG_NAME` MUST be all lower case. The flag MUST NOT be specified more than once.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Request Flags / Query Parameters

requirements.text: - When the flag allows for multiple values, then each value MUST be serialized as a separate query parameter per the previous bullets.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Request Flags / Query Parameters / `?filter` Flag

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Request Flags / Query Parameters / `?filter` Flag
