source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / Request Flags / Query Parameters / `?filter` Flag

requirements.text: - The `?filter` query parameter MAY appear multiple times and if so MUST be evaluated as a logical `OR` with the other `?filter` query parameters that appear - per the [core specification](./spec.md#filter-flag).

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Header Processing / HTTP Header Names

requirements.text: The allowable characters for HTTP header name differs from that of what xRegistry allows for map-key names. Therefore, any map-key name that appears as an HTTP header MUST have those non-HTTP compliant characters percent encoded.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Header Processing / HTTP Header Values

requirements.text: The following rules MUST be followed when encoding values as HTTP headers:

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Header Processing / HTTP Header Values

requirements.text: - Double-quotes (`"`) around a set of characters MAY be used to denote a "group". Whitespace within groups are excluded from whitespace trimming and commas (`,`), normally interpreted as header value separators, are treated as normal characters.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Header Processing / HTTP Header Values

requirements.text: - Any non-US-ASCII characters, percent (`%`) and double-quotes within values, MUST be percent encoded.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Header Processing / HTTP Header Values

requirements.text: - Header values that support lists MAY be expressed as separate HTTP headers or multiple values MAY be grouped into one HTTP header separated by a an unescaped comma.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Header Processing / HTTP Header Values

requirements.text: The following rules MUST be followed when decoding HTTP header values:

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Header Processing / HTTP Header Values

requirements.text: - Commas that appear outside of groups (non-escaped double-quoted ranges of characters) MUST be treated as separators between a list of values.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Header Processing / HTTP Header Values

requirements.text: - Leading and trailing (non-percent encoded) whitespace around individual values MUST be removed. All non-leading/trailing whitespace MUST remain as-is.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Header Processing / HTTP Header Values

requirements.text: - Group's double-quotes MUST be removed prior to passing the values on to the receiving application.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Header Processing / HTTP Header Values

requirements.text: - Percent decoding MUST be performed on all character ranges, both in and out of groups.

source.section: xRegistry HTTP Binding / HTTP Header Processing / HTTP Header Values

requirements.text: If there is an error during processing of HTTP header values then an error ([header_error](#header_error)) MUST be generated.

source.section: xRegistry Events / Abstract

requirements.text: This specification defines the events that an xRegistry server MAY generate.

source.section: xRegistry Events / Overview

requirements.text: As updates are made to entities within an xRegistry instance, events SHOULD be generated to notify interested parties of those changes. This specification defines the metadata associated with each event as [CloudEvent](https://cloudevents.io) context attributes. Whether CloudEvents are used in the generation/serialization of the events is OPTIONAL, but it is RECOMMENDED.

source.section: xRegistry Events / Notations and Terminology / Notational Conventions

requirements.text: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in [RFC 2119](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2119).

source.section: xRegistry Events / Notations and Terminology / Notational Conventions

requirements.text: In the pseudo JSON format snippets `?` means the preceding item is OPTIONAL, `*` means the preceding item MAY appear zero or more times, and `+` means the preceding item MUST appear at least once. The presence of the `#` character means the remaining portion of the line is a comment. Whitespace characters in the JSON snippets are used for readability and are not normative.

source.section: xRegistry Events / Event Definition

requirements.text: Notification of changes to the entities within an xRegistry instance SHOULD be exposed as events. These changes could be the result of an end-user interaction with the Registry, or due to some other (possibly internal) processing of the Registry data.

source.section: xRegistry Events / Event Definition

requirements.text: A single interaction with the Registry MAY result in multiple events; however, within the scope of one interaction (see [`xregcorrelationid`](#xregcorrelationid-extension-context-attribute)), the following constraints apply:

source.section: xRegistry Events / Event Definition

requirements.text: - Only one `created`, `updated` or `deleted` event MUST be generated per `subject`.

source.section: xRegistry Events / Event Definition

requirements.text: - If the interaction involved more than one of those actions, then the single event generated MUST be chosen in the following order of precedence: `deleted`, `created`, `updated`.

source.section: xRegistry Events / Event Definition

requirements.text: - Only one event with the same `type` and `subject` combination MUST be generated.

source.section: xRegistry Events / Event Definition

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Overview / Endpoints

requirements.text: - `producer`: A producer endpoint is made available by a consumer or intermediary (like an application or a queue) to a producer, so that the producer can send events/messages to the endpoint. Those events/messages MUST conform to the declared constraints. If the endpoint is associated with at least one message group, only messages/events that match one of the declared message definitions can be sent. If the message definition references a data schema, the message payload MUST match that schema.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Overview / Endpoints

requirements.text: - `subscriber`: A subscriber endpoint is made available to consumers for the purpose of setting up their own consumer endpoint. The [CloudEvents Subscriptions API](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/subscriptions/spec.md) specification enumerates the subscription mechanisms intended for these endpoints. As subscription mechanisms can vary substantially across products that implement the same protocol, it is RECOMMENDED to use the `label` mechanism to identify the specific product that provides the endpoint.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Overview / Endpoints

requirements.text: Each endpoint definition defines a `protocol` selector by which the specific network application protocol is chosen to communicate with the endpoint. If a networked entity supports multiple protocols, each protocol endpoint MUST be declared separately, even if those are multiplexed over the same port. For instance, if you have an MQTT broker that can dynamically select between MQTT 3.1.1 and MQTT 5.0, those endpoints are to be declared separately as the capabilities differ substantially.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Overview / Endpoints

requirements.text: Each endpoint MAY also define an `envelope` selector which allows for defining particular `envelopeoptions` at the endpoint level. For CloudEvents, this permits the definition of the serialization mode (binary or structured) and the event format for structured mode.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Overview / Message Groups

requirements.text: The Endpoint is an xRegistry group-level construct that is conceptually an extension of the [message definition group](../message/spec.md), meaning there are no “groups of endpoints”. An endpoint MAY contain directly embedded message definitions. In the simplest case, an endpoint MAY embed its message definitions locally which in turn MAY embed their data schema definitions locally, all in one compact construct.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Notations and Terminology / Notational Conventions

requirements.text: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in [RFC 2119](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2119).

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Notations and Terminology / Notational Conventions

requirements.text: For clarity, OPTIONAL attributes (specification-defined and extensions) are OPTIONAL for clients to use, but the servers' responsibility will vary. Server-unknown extension attributes MUST be silently stored in the backing datastore. Specification-defined attributes and server-known extension attributes MUST generate an error if the corresponding feature is not supported or enabled. However, as with all attributes, if accepting the attribute results in a bad state (such as exceeding a size limit or resulting in a security issue), then the server MAY choose to reject the request.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Notations and Terminology / Notational Conventions

requirements.text: In the pseudo JSON format snippets `?` means the preceding attribute is OPTIONAL, `*` means the preceding attribute MAY appear zero or more times, and `+` means the preceding attribute MUST appear at least once. The presence of the `#` character means the remaining portion of the line is a comment. Whitespace characters in the JSON snippets are used for readability and are not normative.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model

requirements.text: As discussed in the [CloudEvents Registry overview](../cloudevents/spec.md), endpoints are supersets of [message definition groups](../message/spec.md#message-definition-groups) and MAY contain inlined messages. Therefore, the Resources in the meta-model for the Endpoint Registry are likewise `messages` as defined in the [message catalog specification](../message/spec.md).

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `usage`

requirements.text: - REQUIRED.

requirements.text: - MUST contain only the following possible values: - "subscriber" - "consumer" - "producer"

requirements.text: - MAY declare `["subscriber", "consumer"]` only when the protocol is `MQTT/3.1.1`, `MQTT/5.0`, `AMQP/1.0`, or `NATS`. In these protocols a single client connection both establishes subscription interest and receives the resulting messages, so the two roles are served by one protocol interface and one endpoint contract.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `usage`

requirements.text: - MUST NOT declare `["subscriber", "consumer"]` for `HTTP` or `KAFKA` endpoints. In those protocols the two roles are distinct interfaces and MUST be modeled as separate Endpoint resources.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `usage`

requirements.text: - Endpoints that jointly describe more than one role SHOULD be declared separately and correlated with a shared `channel` value.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `channel`

requirements.text: - Description: A string that can be used to correlate Endpoints. Any Endpoints within an instance of an Endpoint Registry that share the same non-empty `channel` value MUST have some relationship. This specification does not define that relationship or the specific values used in this property. However, it is expected that the `usage` value in combination with this `channel` property will provide some information to help determine the relationship.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `channel`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `channel`

requirements.text: - When specified, the value MUST be a non-empty string.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `envelope`

requirements.text: - MUST be a non-empty case-insensitive string of the form `<SPEC>[/<VERSION>]`, where `<SPEC>` is the non-empty string name of the specification that defines the Resource. An OPTIONAL `<VERSION>` value SHOULD be included if there are multiple versions of the specification available.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `envelope`

requirements.text: - If a `<VERSION>` is specified at the Group level, all Resources within that Group MUST have a `<VERSION>` value that is at least as precise as its Group, and MUST NOT expand it. For example, if a Group had a `envelope` value of `myspec`, then Resources within that Group can have `envelope` values of `myspec` or `myspec/1.0`. However, if a Group has a value of `myspec/1.0`, it would be invalid for a Resource to have a value of `myspec/2.0` or just `myspec`. Additionally, if a Group does not have an `envelope` attribute, then there are no constraints on its Resources' `envelope` attributes.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `envelopeoptions`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `envelopeoptions` / `CloudEvents/1.0`

requirements.text: - `mode` : indicates whether the CloudEvent will use `binary` or `structured` [mode](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md#message). When specified, its value MUST be one of: `binary` or `structured`, case sensitive. When not specified, the endpoint is indicating that either mode is acceptable.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `envelopeoptions` / `CloudEvents/1.0`

requirements.text: - `format` : indicates the format of the CloudEvent when sent in `structured` mode. This attribute MUST NOT be specified when `mode` is `binary`. The value used MUST match the expected content type of the message (e.g. for HTTP the `Content-Type` header value).

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `protocol`

requirements.text: - Description: The transport or application protocol used by the endpoint. This specification defines a set of common protocol names that MUST be used for respective protocol endpoints, but implementations MAY define and use additional protocol names.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `protocol`

requirements.text: Predefined protocols SHOULD be referred to by name and version as `<NAME>/<VERSION>`. The version number format is determined by the protocol specification's usage of versions. If the version is not specified, the default version of the protocol is assumed. For AMQP and MQTT, see the list below. For others, refer to the protocol specifications.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `protocol`

requirements.text: - "AMQP/1.0" - Use the [AMQP 1.0][AMQP 1.0] protocol. MAY be shortened to "AMQP". AMQP draft versions before 1.0 (e.g. 0.9) are *not* AMQP.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `protocol`

requirements.text: All messages inside an Endpoint MUST use this same protocol.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `protocol`

requirements.text: - SHOULD follow the naming convention `<NAME>/<VERSION>`, whereby `<NAME>` is the name of the protocol and `<VERSION>` is the version of the protocol.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `protocoloptions`

requirements.text: - Description: Configuration details of the endpoint related to the protocol used to transmit the messages. An endpoint MAY be defined without detailed configuration. In this case, the endpoint is considered to be "abstract". For per-protocol option definitions, see [Protocol Options](#protocol-options).

requirements.text: - Description: An array of objects where each object describes one network address at which clients can communicate with the endpoint. The object MAY contain extension attributes that can be used by clients to determine which address to use, or to configure access to the specific address. Whether the address identifies a network host or links directly to a resource managed by the network host is protocol specific.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `protocoloptions` / `protocoloptions.endpoints`

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `protocoloptions` / `protocoloptions.endpoints`

requirements.text: - Each object MUST carry the endpoint address in the attribute that the endpoint's protocol defines for that purpose. Of the protocols defined in this specification, `HTTP`, `AMQP/1.0`, `MQTT/3.1.1`, `MQTT/5.0`, and `NATS` use a `uri` attribute holding a valid, absolute URI (URL), and `KAFKA` uses a non-empty `bootstrap.servers` attribute. A protocol defined outside of this specification MAY define a different addressing attribute.

Runtime credentials and deployment-specific values are expected to be supplied separately through external configuration. The attribute names below MUST be used as defined. Additional endpoint-specific extension attributes MAY be added.

requirements.text: Endpoints are supersets of [message definition groups](../message/spec.md#message-definition-groups) and MAY contain inlined messages. See [Message Definitions](../message/spec.md#message-definitions).

requirements.text: When this specification, and the [message specification](../message/spec.md), are used with specifications such as [CloudEvents](https://cloudevents.io), where a semantically unique identifier is used in a runtime message (e.g. CloudEvent's `type` attribute), it is STRONGLY RECOMMENDED that the `messageid` values of the message definitions for an Endpoint match that unique identifier and therefore be unique across all messages within the `messages` collection and the messages referenced by the `messagegroups` attribute. This will allow for an easy "lookup" from an incoming runtime message to its related message definition.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / `messages`

requirements.text: Implementations MAY choose to generate an error if they detect duplicate `messageid` values across the `messages` collection message definitions and the `messagegroups` referenced message definitions, if that is the desired constraint for their users.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options

requirements.text: For each protocol specified in the following sections there is a table that describes the set of protocol-specific options and the roles (Producer, Consumer, Subscriber) to which each option applies. All protocol options are OPTIONAL.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options

requirements.text: The role applicability is descriptive: it guides clients on how to interpret metadata. Where a rule below is stated with MUST, MUST NOT, or REQUIRED, it is a conformance requirement of this specification, and a client evaluating the metadata MUST treat a violation as an error. A Registry server is not obligated to check these rules.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options

requirements.text: - `✓`: The option applies to that role. Clients acting in that role SHOULD apply the option semantics.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options

requirements.text: Any string value of any protocol option MAY contain placeholders expressed with the [RFC6570][RFC6570] Level 1 URI Template expression syntax, for example `orders/{tenantid}/events`. This applies to plain string values, to the string items of arrays, and to the keys and values of maps, and it also applies to the `uri` values of [`protocoloptions.endpoints`](#protocoloptionsendpoints). Placeholders are resolved out-of-band by the client; this specification does not define how the values are supplied. When the same placeholder name occurs in more than one value of the same endpoint, all of its occurrences MUST resolve to the same value.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / HTTP options

requirements.text: The [endpoint URIs](#protocoloptionsendpoints) for "HTTP" endpoints MUST be valid HTTP URIs using the "http" or "https" scheme as defined in [HTTP Message Format].

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / HTTP options

requirements.text: - An HTTP Endpoint MUST declare exactly one `usage` value and therefore MUST represent exactly one of the three roles above.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / HTTP options

requirements.text: - An HTTP Endpoint MUST NOT declare `["subscriber", "consumer"]`.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / HTTP options

requirements.text: - A subscription manager, a delivery target, and a pull consumer that belong to the same logical channel MUST be declared as separate Endpoint resources and SHOULD be correlated with a shared `channel` value.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / HTTP options

requirements.text: | `apikeyin` | enum: `header`, `query`, default `header` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | Placement of API key metadata when `authorization.type` is `APIKey`. `header` SHOULD be used; `query` SHOULD only be used when header placement is not possible. |

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / HTTP options

requirements.text: These options only define protocol-level placement and naming metadata. Credential values (API keys, usernames, passwords) MUST NOT be stored in endpoint metadata and MUST be supplied out-of-band.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / AMQP options

requirements.text: The [endpoint URIs](#protocoloptionsendpoints) for "AMQP" endpoints MUST be valid AMQP URIs using the "amqp" or "amqps" scheme. If the path portion of the URI is present, it MUST be a valid AMQP node name according to [AMQP Addressing Version 1.0].

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / AMQP options

requirements.text: An AMQP Endpoint MAY declare `["subscriber", "consumer"]`, because a single AMQP receiving link both establishes interest in the source node and carries the resulting transfers. When it does, the `subscriber` role refers to the establishment of the link with the node as source and the `consumer` role refers to the transfers over that link.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / MQTT options

requirements.text: The [endpoint URIs](#protocoloptionsendpoints) for "MQTT" endpoints MUST be valid MQTT URIs using the (informal) "mqtt" or "mqtts" scheme. If the path portion of the URI is present, it MUST be a valid MQTT topic name as described by [MQTT 3.1.1] and [MQTT 5.0]. The informal schemes "tcp" (plain TCP/1883), "ssl" (TLS TCP/8883), and "wss" (Websockets/443) MAY also be used, but MUST NOT have a path.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / MQTT options

requirements.text: - `topic` MUST be a concrete MQTT topic name. It MUST NOT contain the `+` or `#` wildcard characters, since a wildcard is not a valid publish destination.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / MQTT options

requirements.text: - `topicfilter` MAY contain the `+` and `#` wildcard characters as defined by [MQTT 3.1.1] and [MQTT 5.0].

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / MQTT options

requirements.text: - An MQTT Endpoint MUST NOT declare both `topic` and `topicfilter`.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / MQTT options

requirements.text: - An MQTT Endpoint MAY declare `["subscriber", "consumer"]`, because a single MQTT connection both sends the `SUBSCRIBE` packet and receives the resulting `PUBLISH` packets.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / MQTT options

requirements.text: - `sharedsubscriptiongroup` MUST only be present when `topicfilter` is also present.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / MQTT options

requirements.text: - The value of `sharedsubscriptiongroup` is the bare group name. It MUST NOT include the `$share/` prefix and MUST NOT contain the `/` character.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / MQTT options

requirements.text: - When `sharedsubscriptiongroup` is present, a client MUST send the subscription as the topic filter `$share/{sharedsubscriptiongroup}/{topicfilter}`, where `{sharedsubscriptiongroup}` and `{topicfilter}` are the literal values of those two options.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / KAFKA options

requirements.text: For `KAFKA` endpoints, the [endpoint addresses](#protocoloptionsendpoints) MUST be carried in `bootstrap.servers` as an array of client bootstrap addresses. Each entry MUST use the `host:port` format without a scheme. The listener-style `uri` format is not an alternative addressing field for a `KAFKA` endpoint.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / KAFKA options

requirements.text: - A `subscriber` Kafka Endpoint describes the creation and configuration of a consumer group as an act of registering interest. It MUST NOT declare `consumergroup`, since the group is the resource being established rather than a group to be joined.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / KAFKA options

requirements.text: - A `consumer` Kafka Endpoint describes joining an existing consumer group. It MUST declare `consumergroup` with a non-empty value.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / KAFKA options

requirements.text: - A Kafka Endpoint MUST NOT declare `["subscriber", "consumer"]`. The two roles MUST be declared as separate Endpoint resources and SHOULD be correlated with a shared `channel` value.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / KAFKA options

requirements.text: - `autooffsetreset` and `enableautocommit` describe group-based consumption. They MUST NOT be used on a `producer` or `subscriber` Endpoint.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / KAFKA options

requirements.text: - `autooffsetreset` expresses only the reset behavior when no valid committed offset exists. A concrete starting offset or a starting timestamp is runtime consumer state, not endpoint metadata, and MUST NOT be expressed through this option.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / NATS options

requirements.text: The [endpoint URIs](#protocoloptionsendpoints) for "NATS" endpoints MUST be valid NATS URIs as described by [NATS]. The scheme MUST be "nats" or "tls" or "ws" and the URI MUST include a port number, e.g. `nats://<HOST>:<PORT>` or `tls://<HOST>:<PORT>`.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / NATS options

requirements.text: - `subject` MUST be a concrete NATS subject. It MUST NOT contain the `*` or `>` wildcard tokens, since a wildcard is not a valid publish destination.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / NATS options

requirements.text: - `subjectfilter` MAY contain the `*` and `>` wildcard tokens as defined by [NATS].

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / NATS options

requirements.text: - `queuegroup` MUST only be present when `subjectfilter` is also present.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / NATS options

requirements.text: - A NATS Endpoint MUST NOT declare both `subject` and `subjectfilter`.

source.section: Endpoint Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Endpoint Registry Model / Endpoints Groups / Protocol Options / NATS options

requirements.text: - A NATS Endpoint MAY declare `["subscriber", "consumer"]`, because a single Core NATS connection both registers the subscription interest and receives the resulting messages.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Overview / Message Metadata

requirements.text: A `message` definition MAY contain any combination of `envelope`, `protocol`, and data payload declarations. A payload-only declaration can be useful if messages are sent through varying protocols without a fixed envelope model and are distinguished by content-type (including parameters) or even only through whether payload schema definitions match an incoming message.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Overview / Reusing Message Definitions

requirements.text: The `basemessage` attribute, a URI-typed reference to another message definition, enables such reuse scenarios. Any message definition MAY refer to another message definition as its base, which effects a copy of the base message’s definitions into the message that defines it. The mechanism is transitive, which means that `basemessage` relationships MUST be resolved recursively as long as they do not result in circular references.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Overview / Message Definition Matching

requirements.text: - Use of CloudEvents is RECOMMENDED as it will provide well-defined metadata that will appear in each Message to help differentiate Message definitions.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Overview / Message Definition Matching

requirements.text: - Message definitions SHOULD have a `messageid` value that is the same as the CloudEvents' `type` context attribute defined for that Message. This will allow for an exact mapping from the incoming Message's `type` attribute to its related Message definition.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Overview / Message Definition Matching

requirements.text: - Message Resource types SHOULD be defined with a `maxversions` of `1`. This eliminates the need for each incoming Message to include some unique Version discriminator.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Overview / Message Definition Matching

requirements.text: - Modifications to Message definitions SHOULD NOT result in "on the wire" changes to the resulting messages as that could break existing systems. Rather, new Message definitions SHOULD be created, with new `type` and `messageid` values, and referenced through the use of the `deprecated` attribute.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Overview / Message Definition Matching

requirements.text: Implementations and Registry model authors MAY deviate from these recommendations; however, they are then responsible for defining the mechanisms by which a unique Message definition is matched to incoming messages.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Message Groups

requirements.text: All message definitions MUST be contained in a group. A message group can be formed for many reasons. At a minimum, the group will be an access control boundary in many implementations of this specification even though none is mandated.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Notations and Terminology / Notational Conventions

requirements.text: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in [RFC 2119](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2119).

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Notations and Terminology / Notational Conventions

requirements.text: For clarity, OPTIONAL attributes (specification-defined and extensions) are OPTIONAL for clients to use, but the servers' responsibility will vary. Server-unknown extension attributes MUST be silently stored in the backing datastore. Specification-defined attributes and server-known extension attributes MUST generate an error if the corresponding feature is not supported or enabled. However, as with all attributes, if accepting the attribute results in a bad state (such as exceeding a size limit or resulting in a security issue), then the server MAY choose to reject the request.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Notations and Terminology / Notational Conventions

requirements.text: In the pseudo JSON format snippets `?` means the preceding attribute is OPTIONAL, `*` means the preceding attribute MAY appear zero or more times, and `+` means the preceding attribute MUST appear at least once. The presence of the `#` character means the remaining portion of the line is a comment. Whitespace characters in the JSON snippets are used for readability and are not normative.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Notations and Terminology / Terminology / Envelopes and Protocols

requirements.text: This specification uses **protocol** as a selector into the protocol-specific message metadata that is defined under the `protocol.ifvalues` section of the model. When a known protocol is explicitly specified for a message definition, the `protocoloptions` section MAY contain constraints for the protocol-specific metadata.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Message Definition Registry Model / Message Definition Groups / `envelope` (Message Group)

requirements.text: - Description: Identifies a common, transport protocol-independent message metadata format. Message metadata envelopes are referenced by name and version as `<NAME>/<VERSION>`. This specification defines a set of common [metadata envelope names](#metadata-envelopes) that MUST be used for the given envelopes, but applications MAY define extensions for other envelopes on their own. All messages inside a group MUST use this same envelope.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Message Definition Registry Model / Message Definition Groups / `envelope` (Message Group)

requirements.text: - If present, MUST be a non-empty case-insensitive string.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Message Definition Registry Model / Message Definition Groups / `envelope` (Message Group)

requirements.text: - If present, MUST follow the naming convention `<NAME>/<VERSION>`, whereby `<NAME>` is the name of the metadata envelope and `<VERSION>` is the version of the metadata envelope.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Message Definition Registry Model / Message Definition Groups / `protocol` (Message Group)

requirements.text: - Description: Identifies a transport protocol to be bound to for this Message. Protocols are referenced by name and version as `<NAME>/<VERSION>`. This specification defines a set of common [message protocol names](#message-protocols) that MUST be used for the given protocols, but applications MAY define extensions for other protocols on their own. All messages inside a group MUST use this same protocol.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Message Definition Registry Model / Message Definition Groups / `protocol` (Message Group)

requirements.text: - If present, MUST be a non-empty case-insensitive string.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Message Definition Registry Model / Message Definition Groups / `protocol` (Message Group)

requirements.text: - If present, MUST follow the naming convention `<NAME>` or `<NAME>/<VERSION>`, whereby `<NAME>` is the name of the protocol and `<VERSION>` is the version of protocol. The version is REQUIRED if multiple, mutually incompatible versions of the protocol exist and protocol options differ between versions.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Message Definition Registry Model / Message Definitions (Message Group)

requirements.text: When [CloudEvents](https://cloudevents.io) is used for a particular message, it is RECOMMENDED that the message's `messageid` attribute be the same as the [CloudEvents `type` attribute](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec/blob/main/cloudevents/spec.md#type). Doing so makes for easier management of the meta-model by correlating the look-up value (id) of messages with their related events.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Message Definition Registry Model / Message Definitions (Message Group) / `basemessage`

requirements.text: When the value is a relative reference (begins with `/`), it MUST be a valid XID referencing a Resource, or Version, of type `message` within the same registry. When the value is an absolute URI, it MUST point to a message definition in an external registry, but the server is not mandated to validate or resolve external references.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Message Definition Registry Model / Message Definitions (Message Group) / `basemessage`

requirements.text: Referenced messages MAY themselves have a `basemessage` value; however, the chain of messages MUST NOT be recursive.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Message Definition Registry Model / Message Definitions (Message Group) / `basemessage`

requirements.text: The process that a client SHOULD follow to materialize the message is to follow the `basemessage` references to the end of the chain of messages, get that message's attributes, and then walk back up the chain performing a "merge" operation of the next message's attributes. Note that if an inherited attribute is a complex type (e.g. map, object) and the overlaying attribute is scalar, then the entire inherited attribute (and nested values) are replaced by that scalar value. For complex types, the merge is "deep", meaning each level of the complex type is merged appropriately rather than it being a complete replacement of the entire complex type.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Message Definition Registry Model / Message Definitions (Message Group) / `basemessage`

requirements.text: If the referenced message can not be found, whether due to a dangling reference, an unreachable external registry, or insufficient permissions, an error MUST NOT be generated. Dangling references are permitted.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Message Definition Registry Model / Message Definitions (Message Group) / `basemessage`

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

requirements.text: - If the value is an absolute URI, it MUST point to a message definition but the server MUST NOT validate the target.

The schema format is identified by the `dataschemaformat` attribute. See [Schema Formats](../schema/spec.md#43-schema-formats) for details on how to reference specific schema objects for the message payload. It is not sufficient for the URI to point to a schema document; it MUST resolve to a concrete schema object.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Message Definition Registry Model / Message Definitions (Message Group) / `datacontenttype`

requirements.text: - Description: Content type of the message payload. This attribute MAY be duplicative with some other metadata within the message definition. For example, in the case of using CloudEvents, the `envelopemetadata` attribute might include the `datacontenttype` attribute. This possible duplication of data is expected so as to allow for easy, more consistent discovery of the message's format. This means that if this information does appear in more than one location within the message metadata, all occurrences MUST have the same value.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Message Definition Registry Model / Message Definitions (Message Group) / `datacontenttype`

requirements.text: Note that when an `envelope` is defined for a message and the data of interest is serialized as being nested within the envelope (e.g. CloudEvents "structured" mode), then this attribute MUST be the content type of the message envelope and not of the data nested within the envelope.

source.section: Message Definitions Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / Message Definition Registry Model / Message Definitions (Message Group) / `datacontenttype`

requirements.text: As specified in [RFC 2045](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2045), the media type part of the content type MUST be treated in a case-insensitive manner by consumers, along with the attribute names in parameters. For example, a `datacontenttype` of `text/plain; charset=utf-8` MUST be treated in the same way as `TEXT/Plain; CharSet=utf-8`.

source.section: Schema Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: The schema registry therefore allows managing multiple versions of schemas, declares their lineage, and states their compatibility policy. The compatibility policy is used to determine whether a schema change is compatible with prior versions and whether data that has been serialized based on prior versions can still be deserialized and/or validated using the new schema. This compatibility check is important to ensure that changes to schemas do not inadvertently break the ability to read existing data, and MAY be enforced by implementations of the schema registry. The [xRegistry Core][xRegistry Core] specification defines the versioning and compatibility relationship mechanisms.

Server-unknown extension attributes MUST be silently stored in the backing datastore. Specification-defined and server-known extension attributes MUST generate an error if the corresponding feature is not supported or enabled. However, as with all attributes, if accepting the attribute would result in a bad state (such as exceeding a size limit, or results in a security issue), then the server MAY choose to reject the request.

source.section: Schema Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 2. Notations and Terminology / 2.2. Terminology / 2.2.1. Schema

requirements.text: We use the term **schema** (or schema Resource) in this specification as a logical grouping of **schema Versions**. A **schema Version** is a concrete document. The **schema** Resource is a semantic umbrella formed around one or more concrete schema Version documents that represent iterations of the same logical schema. Per the definition of the [`compatibility`][xRegistry compatibility] attribute, all Versions of a single **schema** MUST adhere to the rules defined by the `compatibility` attribute. Any breaking change MUST result in a new **schema** Resource being created.

source.section: Schema Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 2. Notations and Terminology / 2.2. Terminology / 2.2.1. Schema

requirements.text: In terms of versioning, you can think of a **schema** as a collection of versions that are compatible according to the selected `compatibility` mode. The [`deprecated`][xRegistry deprecated] attribute MAY be used to indicate the appropriate new schema to use following a breaking change.

source.section: Pagination - Version 1.0-rc4 / Client Request

requirements.text: When a client sends a request to a server which is meant to result in a set of records being returned, the client MAY include extra attributes to control how those records are to be returned if the results can not fit within one response message.

source.section: Pagination - Version 1.0-rc4 / Client Request / Client Attributes

requirements.text: The following list of attributes MAY be included in a client's request for a set of records from a server. The client MUST only specify these on the initial request for the set and their presence (and values) in any subsequent request to the server to retrieve additional records for the same pagination sequence is dictated by the server - the client MUST NOT add or modify them.

source.section: Pagination - Version 1.0-rc4 / Client Request / Client Attributes

requirements.text: While this specification defines a mechanism by which clients can initiate the pagination of a result set, servers MAY automatically initiate it themselves, typically if the result set is very large. How the server knows that the client supports pagination, or how clients are made aware of this possibility, is out of scope for this specification.

source.section: Pagination - Version 1.0-rc4 / Client Request / Client Attributes / limit

requirements.text: - Description: Indicates the maximum number of records per message that the client is willing to accept. If the server is unable to meet this criterion then it MUST generate an error.

source.section: Pagination - Version 1.0-rc4 / Client Request / Client Attributes / limit

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

source.section: Pagination - Version 1.0-rc4 / Client Request / Client Attributes / limit

requirements.text: - MUST be an unsigned 64-bit integer with a value greater than 0.

source.section: Pagination - Version 1.0-rc4 / Server Response

requirements.text: When a server returns a subset of records, it MAY include additional attributes to help the client retrieve the additional subsets of records.

source.section: Pagination - Version 1.0-rc4 / Server Response / Server Attributes

requirements.text: The following list of attributes MAY be included in a server's response to a client's request for a set of records. The location and syntax of how these attribute appear in response messages will be defined by the protocol binding being used.

source.section: Pagination - Version 1.0-rc4 / Server Response / Server Attributes / link

requirements.text: - Description: A URI-Reference to another subset of records. The relationship of the subset to the current subset MUST be specified by the [`rel` attribute](#rel). This value is meant to be treated as an opaque value by the client. If a client uses this value in a subsequent request then it MUST use it as it was provided by the server. Any attempt to modify its value, or attributes (such as query parameters), is not defined by this specification and the results from the server are undefined.

source.section: Pagination - Version 1.0-rc4 / Server Response / Server Attributes / link

requirements.text: - REQUIRED if any pagination metadata is included in a response message.

source.section: Pagination - Version 1.0-rc4 / Server Response / Server Attributes / link

requirements.text: - MUST be a URI-Reference as defined in [RFC3986](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3986).

source.section: Pagination - Version 1.0-rc4 / Server Response / Server Attributes / rel

requirements.text: Unless otherwise constrained by a specification leveraging this specification, additional values MAY be defined.

requirements.text: - REQUIRED if the `link` attribute is present.

source.section: Pagination - Version 1.0-rc4 / Server Response / Server Attributes / rel

requirements.text: - If the current subset of records is not the last set of records for the pagination sequence, then a `next` Link attribute MUST be included in the response message.

source.section: Pagination - Version 1.0-rc4 / Server Response / Server Attributes / rel

requirements.text: - A `self` Link attribute is STRONGLY RECOMMENDED to be included in all responses from the server so that clients have a consistent location to find metadata about the current pagination sequence.

source.section: Pagination - Version 1.0-rc4 / Server Response / Server Attributes / rel

requirements.text: - If the size of the entire result set can fit in one response message then the `self` Link attribute SHOULD still be included, however no other Link attribute SHOULD be present.

requirements.text: It is RECOMMENDED that this attribute only be used when the underlying result set is guaranteed to not change before the date specified. For example, it might be used if the result set is cached to ensure that subsequent write operations to the server will not modify the result set.

requirements.text: - OPTIONAL.

source.section: Pagination - Version 1.0-rc4 / Server Response / Server Attributes / offset

requirements.text: - If the current set of records does not contain any records then this attribute MUST NOT be present.

source.section: Pagination - Version 1.0-rc4 / Server Response / Server Attributes / offset

requirements.text: - STRONGLY RECOMMENDED to appear on the `self` Link attribute.

source.section: Pagination - Version 1.0-rc4 / Server Response / Server Attributes / offset

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / Abstract

requirements.text: This specification defines a Registry-of-Registries domain for xRegistry. Its catalog stores versioned descriptions of independently administered Registries and human-facing websites, with OPTIONAL federation advertisements. A Consumer can discover an entry without fetching or copying the contents it describes.

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 1. Overview / 1.1. Scope

requirements.text: The catalog MAY advertise HTTP, OCI, Git, File, OPC UA or extension bindings. [Shared federation][Federation] defines the read operations and Registry context established after selection. A catalog does not have to implement those bindings, serve an HTTP facade for them, proxy their contents or provide a materialized view.

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 1. Overview / 1.1. Scope

requirements.text: A catalog's own `category` Groups and `registry` Resources MAY be federated using the shared federation rules and a compatible catalog model. The resulting view combines catalog descriptions; it does not combine the contents of every Registry they describe. A resolver still needs an initial access context and composition policy for the catalog view. An advertised Registry is not automatically added to that view, nor does its advertisement authorize another traversal. Federation policy and cycle limits continue to apply.

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 2. Notations and Terminology

requirements.text: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in [RFC 2119][RFC2119].

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 3. Registry Model

requirements.text: The authoritative xRegistry extension model in [model.json](model.json) defines the catalog as a compact `modelsource`. An implementation MUST apply both that model and this specification's semantic constraints. Core remains authoritative for entity IDs, navigation, labels, Version management and Meta attributes.

requirements.text: The Group singular name MUST be `category` and its collection name MUST be `categories`. The Resource singular name MUST be `registry` and its collection name MUST be `registries`. Canonical entry XIDs have the form:

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 3. Registry Model / 3.1. Hierarchy

requirements.text: A catalog-description Version appends `/versions/<versionid>`. Its Meta entity appends `/meta` to the entry XID. All identifiers MUST follow [Core ID rules][Core IDs]. IDs MUST be unique case-insensitively within their parent scope, but lookups MUST be case-sensitive. For example, `Catalog` and `catalog` MUST NOT identify different siblings. A lookup using the wrong case MUST be treated as not found, not normalized to an existing ID.

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 3. Registry Model / 3.1. Hierarchy

requirements.text: IDs MUST contain 1 to 128 ASCII characters. The first character MUST be a letter, digit or `_`. Subsequent characters MUST be letters, digits, `_`, `.`, `~`, `:`, `@` or `-`. Storage mappings MUST preserve the original IDs and their scopes without weakening this grammar or introducing case-only duplicate siblings. For example, `schema:main` is a valid Core ID even on a platform that prohibits `:` in a filename: an ID is not a raw filesystem name. Equal IDs in distinct parent or model-type scopes do not imply identity.

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 3. Registry Model / 3.1. Hierarchy

requirements.text: Every catalog entry MUST belong to a Category. Category IDs are open-ended. A producer MUST NOT assume that a Category ID selects a protocol, grants trust or proves a target model. Empty Categories are valid. A catalog MAY host other Group types in addition to this domain.

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 3. Registry Model / 3.1. Hierarchy

requirements.text: Registry Resources MUST have `hasdocument: false`, so their metadata is their document. There is no separate `registry` document, `registrybase64` content or `registryurl` document locator in this domain. The `xregurl` domain attribute does not replace a Core document locator.

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 3. Registry Model / 3.2. Versions and References

requirements.text: Each non-alias entry MUST have at least one catalog-description Version. Core determines its default Version through `meta.defaultversionid`. A consumer MUST NOT select a description by sorting Version IDs, endpoint tags or timestamps instead.

source.section: Registry-of-Registries Service - Version 1.0-rc1 / 3. Registry Model / 3.2. Versions and References

requirements.text: An endpoint, authority, type assertion or relationship is description data. Core permits changing that data by updating a Version or creating another Version. This domain requires neither immutable descriptions nor a target snapshot for every catalog Version. When a consumer needs a stable snapshot, it MUST use the selected binding's revision rules.

The native binding defines supported transport profiles and endpoint discovery, including [advertisement and Registry selection][OPC UA selection] and [structured reference resolution][OPC UA references].
