source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Record and Index Documents

requirements.text: Version indexes MUST include all locally owned Versions. An ordinary Resource MUST have at least one Version. Exactly one MUST have `isdefault: true`, matching its Meta's `defaultversionid`. Ancestors MUST exist in that same index and MUST NOT form cycles other than a root's self-reference. An alias MUST NOT own a Version index, including a fabricated empty index.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Model and Capabilities

requirements.text: The Registry's `entity.modelsource` MUST preserve the captured source, including `ximportresources` provenance. `entity.model`, when supplied, MUST be the actual full Core model, not a compact source relabeled as a full model. It MUST agree with the source, its resolved includes and the captured data.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Model and Capabilities

requirements.text: If the source contains [`$include` or `$includes`](../../core/model.md#includes-in-the-xregistry-model-data), the Registry record MUST also contain `resolvedmodelsource`. That object is the compact source after those includes were evaluated at capture time, but before implicit Core definitions and `ximportresources` expansion.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Model and Capabilities

requirements.text: This object MUST be self-contained and preserve [Resource type sharing](../../core/model.md#reuse-of-resource-definitions). `modelbase` MUST record the absolute base of the original source. Consumers MUST NOT re-fetch mutable includes during a read.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Model and Capabilities

requirements.text: The producer MUST establish equivalence between the captured source, resolved source and full model, when present. The original include directives remain available through [`entity.modelsource`](../../core/spec.md#modelsource-attribute). The resolved copy supplies storage context without establishing a second authoritative domain model.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Model and Capabilities

requirements.text: When includes are absent, `resolvedmodelsource` is OPTIONAL and, if present, MUST equal `entity.modelsource`. Model reads expose the original source, available resolved source and available full model.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Model and Capabilities

requirements.text: When interpreting a compact source, the consumer MUST apply Core defaults. It MUST NOT silently infer type sharing from structural similarity.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Model and Capabilities

requirements.text: Model results MUST preserve `modelbase` when present. Registry metadata envelopes retain `snapshot` and available `source` outside `entity`. These are capture context, not new Core attributes.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Model and Capabilities

requirements.text: `entity.capabilities` MUST describe access to this snapshot, not copy claims of upstream writes or filtering that the selected binding cannot implement. It MUST include Core's `available` map. The bindings are read-only.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Model and Capabilities

requirements.text: Captured source information MAY appear in the Registry record's `source` object with an absolute, credential-free `uri` and OPTIONAL `revision`. This is provenance, not the operation's Git pin, an entity XID, or an implicit base for document links.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Documents

requirements.text: Each Version record MUST have exactly one `document` descriptor:

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Documents

requirements.text: | `document.kind` | REQUIRED fields | Meaning |

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Documents

requirements.text: For a local document, OPTIONAL `base` supplies the base URI used to resolve relative links inside that document. If the file was copied from an external location, OPTIONAL `origin` records that original location. The copied Version no longer has a `<RESOURCE>url`, because its document is now local.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Documents

requirements.text: Both `base` and `origin`, when present, MUST be absolute URIs without embedded credentials.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Documents

requirements.text: For `external`, `uri` MUST equal the Version's `<RESOURCE>url` exactly. A relative URI MUST have an explicit absolute `base` on this descriptor. Neither the containing file, catalog URL, Git repository URL nor `source.uri` is an implicit base.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Documents

requirements.text: Known integrity is recorded in OPTIONAL paired `size` and `sha256` fields. If those fields are present and a consumer retrieves the content, it MUST check both. An external locator does not create a metadata alias.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Documents

requirements.text: A Version referencing a document MUST identify either local bytes or an explicit external location. A missing referenced local file is an `invalid_package` error, not an empty document.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Documents

requirements.text: A zero-byte local document MUST reference an actual zero-byte file, with `size: 0` and SHA-256 `e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855`.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Documents

requirements.text: Consumers MUST NOT decode, reserialize, newline-convert or replace binary and JSON bytes with an empty JSON wrapper. The Version's `contenttype`, if present, describes the bytes independently of the file's extension.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Documents

requirements.text: For `hasdocument: false`, `document.kind` MUST be `none`. The Core document attributes do not apply. Consumers MUST preserve and validate ordinary model-admitted metadata named `<RESOURCE>`, `<RESOURCE>base64` or `<RESOURCE>url` as metadata. Consumers MUST NOT decode or dereference it as document content.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Documents

requirements.text: A document request for such a Resource MUST produce `unsupported_operation`. A present zero-byte document is a different case.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Reads and Core Document View

requirements.text: An exact read starts at the Registry record and follows the necessary typed collection indexes and selected child records. A Version read MUST NOT require unrelated domain bytes. A consumer MAY scan a collection index in memory; the format defines one complete index per collection, without pagination. Inline objects require no read beyond their containing file. Each followed external reference requires one read of its file.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Reads and Core Document View

requirements.text: If a configured limit prevents a consumer from reading the complete index or the records needed for its request, the consumer MUST return `limit_exceeded`. It MUST NOT return the subset already read as a complete collection or use that subset to claim a unique match. The inline nesting depth within one file and the cumulative number of decoded metadata objects are such limits, in addition to file count and byte limits.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Reads and Core Document View

requirements.text: Every materialized entity's `self` MUST be a JSON Pointer fragment locating that entity in the returned envelope. For example, a standalone Version has `self: "#/entity"`. Collection members begin at `#/entities/<ID>`. JSON Pointer tokens MUST escape `~` as `~0` and `/` as `~1`. URI-fragment encoding also applies. XIDs are not rewritten.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Reads and Core Document View

requirements.text: Navigation MUST use a `#` JSON Pointer if and only if the referenced entity or collection is included in the output. A pointer into another record file is not document-local navigation.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Reads and Core Document View

requirements.text: Registry and Group results inline all child metadata. Ordinary Resource results inline `meta` and all Version metadata. `metaurl`, `versionsurl`, and the Meta's `defaultversionurl` MUST point at those actual objects. Collection URLs and counts, when included, MUST describe the materialized maps, including empty maps. A producer MUST NOT also copy Default-Version attributes onto the Resource. No response in this format invents an API `self`.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Reads and Core Document View

requirements.text: A standalone ordinary Meta result includes its selected default Version metadata in an envelope sibling, `related.defaultversion`. Its `defaultversionurl` MUST be `#/related/defaultversion`, and that Version's `self` MUST locate the same object. This explicit navigation closure avoids an absolute URL to an undefined native API or a dangling local pointer. An alias Meta has no such sibling and no default-Version attributes.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Reads and Core Document View

requirements.text: Core [`xref`](../../core/spec.md#cross-referencing-resources) remains one-hop, same-Registry and same-Resource-model-type. Document-view Resource and Meta reads MUST leave aliases unexpanded, including dangling aliases and aliases whose targets are themselves aliases. Document-view alias Versions and alias Version collections MUST produce `unsupported_operation`, retaining Core's `cannot_doc_xref` diagnostic. No materialized target metadata can replace the source IDs.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Reads and Core Document View

requirements.text: A logical document request to an alias MAY read the one-hop target's selected document, independently of document-view metadata. It MUST NOT follow a second alias. If no one-hop target document exists, the document request returns `not_found`. That does not make the source's minimal metadata invalid.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Reads and Core Document View

requirements.text: Resource document requests use `meta.defaultversionid`. Explicit Version requests use exactly the requested Version ID. A snapshot revision, index position or highest Version string MUST NOT override the Core default.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Reads and Core Document View

requirements.text: Resource label selection uses effective default-Version metadata, applying one-hop alias semantics where applicable. It does not inspect only the reduced storage Resource object. Selection MUST use the common literal comparator and complete collection, and return `not_found` or `ambiguous` as appropriate. The selected metadata result still obeys document-view alias suppression.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Completeness and Integrity

requirements.text: The root's `snapshot` object MUST contain `scope: "/"` and `completeness`, either `linked` or `offline-complete`. Both classes MUST contain the complete internal record/index/document graph. An `offline-complete` snapshot MUST NOT contain external-only domain documents. Captured resolved model material MUST permit offline interpretation in both classes.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Completeness and Integrity

requirements.text: A full-graph validator is OPTIONAL and checks every referenced object. A selective read validates only its visited path and MUST NOT claim an independent audit of unvisited graph closure.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Completeness and Integrity

requirements.text: Consumers MUST verify length and SHA-256 before parsing or returning each internally referenced file. An inline object has no separate size or digest. The bytes of its containing file cover it. Root bytes are captured once per operation. Their SHA-256 identifies that root serialization, not universal semantic identity or publisher authenticity.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Completeness and Integrity

requirements.text: Every external descendant is pinned transitively by its parent's reference, and every inline descendant by its containing file. Newly published states MUST be complete without replaying a prior snapshot. Shared content reuse does not relax closure.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Completeness and Integrity

requirements.text: Missing indexed objects, invalid kinds, invalid model types and inconsistent defaults are `invalid_package`. A requested absent XID is `not_found`. Descriptor mismatch is `integrity_error`. Observed mutation during a File read or loss of already selected Git objects is `inconsistent_snapshot`. Consumers MUST NOT return empty collections or retry another profile to hide these failures.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Security and Conformance

requirements.text: Producers MUST use regular files and real directories. They MUST NOT use symlinks, reparse points, parent paths, device names, alternate data streams or OS aliases.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Security and Conformance

requirements.text: Consumers MUST enforce selected-root containment before reading bytes.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Security and Conformance

requirements.text: Bindings define access to the selected root and race protection. Consumers MUST impose explicit file, byte and traversal limits. Traversal limits cover inline nesting depth, counted within each containing file, and the cumulative number of decoded metadata objects. Integrity checks do not ensure authorized filesystem access or establish publisher trust. Before retrieving an external URI, the consumer MUST check that destination against its access policy and use only credentials authorized for that destination.

source.section: xRegistry Directory Mapping Format / Executable Example

requirements.text: [`mapping_examples.py`](tools/mapping_examples.py) provides offline parsing, schema/semantic validation, selective reads, document-view assembly and an OPTIONAL local Git object-store reader. It uses the common `FederationError`, XID validation, label selection and Resource type helper. It does not fetch repositories or external documents.

source.section: xRegistry File Federation Binding / Scope and Conventions

requirements.text: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in [RFC2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119).

source.section: xRegistry File Federation Binding / Advertisement and File URI

requirements.text: `binding` MUST be `file`. The `endpoint` MUST be an absolute [RFC8089](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8089) file URI identifying the selected directory. It MUST NOT contain credentials, a query or fragment. An absent authority or `localhost` means local access. Other authorities, including UNC (Universal Naming Convention) servers, MUST produce `policy_denied` in this binding. A separately named extension can define a remote filesystem access policy. An implementation MUST NOT infer such a policy from this profile.

source.section: xRegistry File Federation Binding / Advertisement and File URI

requirements.text: | `layout` | REQUIRED, exactly `document-tree` or `oci-layout`. |

source.section: xRegistry File Federation Binding / Advertisement and File URI

requirements.text: | `reference` | REQUIRED for `oci-layout`, forbidden for `document-tree`. An OCI tag or `sha256` digest under the OCI binding. |

source.section: xRegistry File Federation Binding / Advertisement and File URI

requirements.text: An unknown selected parameter MUST produce `unsupported_operation`. The resolver MUST NOT infer a layout from the directory's files or switch layouts after a failure. When an OCI layout contains several snapshots, `reference` selects the root; directory-entry order does not.

source.section: xRegistry File Federation Binding / Advertisement and File URI

requirements.text: The first example selects an absolute Windows drive path; the second selects an absolute POSIX path. If a host cannot interpret the selected native path, it MUST report `unsupported_operation` rather than reinterpret the path as a different filesystem root. Windows drive-relative paths and older `C|` spellings are not accepted.

source.section: xRegistry File Federation Binding / Advertisement and File URI

requirements.text: URI parsing MUST:

source.section: xRegistry File Federation Binding / Advertisement and File URI

requirements.text: After decoding, URI parsing MUST reject:

source.section: xRegistry File Federation Binding / Advertisement and File URI

requirements.text: These rejections apply where applicable. A single terminal slash is permitted for a directory URI. Decoding a second time MUST NOT turn a literal percent sequence into traversal.

source.section: xRegistry File Federation Binding / Layout Selection and Reads

requirements.text: For `document-tree`, the selected directory MUST contain `registry.json`. The [directory mapping format](mapping.md#record-and-index-documents) defines the record and index schemas and exact-byte representation. It also defines model and capabilities reads, label selection, Core document view, defaults and `xref`. Every internal `href` is [relative to this directory](mapping.md#root-and-storage-paths), including references in nested records. There is no implicit `xregistry` directory.

source.section: xRegistry File Federation Binding / Layout Selection and Reads

requirements.text: Both layout modes carry the selected Registry's [resolution-owner capability](../federation/spec.md#signaling-who-performs-resolution). A consumer MUST NOT repeat catalog resolution for a `producer` view. Absence of the signal retains the default consumer-side process.

source.section: xRegistry File Federation Binding / Layout Selection and Reads

requirements.text: For `oci-layout`, consumers MUST use the [OCI binding's image-layout selection](oci.md#22-image-layout-selection) and [descriptor-graph rules](oci.md#4-containment-and-range-shards).

source.section: xRegistry File Federation Binding / Layout Selection and Reads

requirements.text: External domain-document links remain explicit. Retrieving one requires separate caller authorization, URI-base handling and integrity checking. Relative links MUST NOT silently become paths outside the selected root.

source.section: xRegistry File Federation Binding / Containment and Concurrent Changes

requirements.text: The caller MUST authorize a filesystem boundary before the resolver opens the selected directory. The resolver MUST verify that the directory is within that boundary, then constrain all internal reads to that selected root. A mere string prefix test is insufficient: `root-other` is not inside `root`.

source.section: xRegistry File Federation Binding / Containment and Concurrent Changes

requirements.text: The resolver MUST check every directory component, including components of the selected root, for symlinks and Windows reparse points. Internal objects MUST be regular files. Consumers MUST NOT follow symlinks, junctions, mount-point reparse records or other path redirections. Consumers MUST NOT read device files, pipes, sockets and alternate data streams as snapshot content. Case folding, short-name aliases and reserved OS names MUST NOT select a different internal object. Git/File storage portability does not permit case-insensitive Core XID lookup.

source.section: xRegistry File Federation Binding / Containment and Concurrent Changes

requirements.text: Before interpreting bytes, consumers MUST establish that the actual opened objects are contained within the selected root. When a hostile process can change paths concurrently, containment requires directory/handle-relative no-follow access, equivalent platform protection, or a private immutable copy made before resolution. Checking `realpath` before opening a mutable pathname is insufficient. Hard links also provide no immutability guarantee: a writer outside the directory can still change shared content.

source.section: xRegistry File Federation Binding / Containment and Concurrent Changes

requirements.text: For document-tree reads, consumers MUST capture the root record once and retain its exact-byte SHA-256. Descendant references pin every consumed external record, index and document. The bytes of the containing file pin each inline record and index. For OCI reads, consumers MUST pin the selected root digest and verify every descriptor under the OCI binding.

source.section: xRegistry File Federation Binding / Containment and Concurrent Changes

requirements.text: Consumers MUST detect changes during open/read operations, short reads and changes to already captured selection state. An observed change MUST produce `inconsistent_snapshot`. A stable descriptor mismatch is `integrity_error`.

source.section: xRegistry File Federation Binding / Containment and Concurrent Changes

requirements.text: If the environment cannot guarantee a coherent read, the consumer MUST either capture a private stable snapshot or explicitly report the lack of an immutable filesystem pin. Consistent file timestamps alone are insufficient: the consumer MUST NOT use them to advertise an atomic capture of a live upstream Registry.

source.section: xRegistry File Federation Binding / Containment and Concurrent Changes

requirements.text: A producer SHOULD construct a complete snapshot separately and then make it available atomically using platform-appropriate synchronization. Updating files in place while readers traverse them does not establish completeness. Retaining immutable old files can allow readers with an older pinned root to complete without mixing revisions.

source.section: xRegistry File Federation Binding / Containment and Concurrent Changes

requirements.text: Origin MUST identify the file URI, layout and selected root hash/digest, plus the presence or absence of an immutable filesystem snapshot guarantee. It MUST NOT replace entity XIDs, Resource Version IDs or Core navigation.

source.section: xRegistry File Federation Binding / Errors and Conformance

requirements.text: A producer MUST provide a complete snapshot in one explicitly declared layout. A consumer MUST implement that layout's metadata/document semantics and all applicable containment and consistency rules. A consumer MUST identify which layouts it implements. Support for one does not imply the other. An offline-complete claim additionally requires the selected layout's offline content closure.

source.section: xRegistry Git Federation Binding / Scope and Conventions

requirements.text: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in [RFC2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119).

source.section: xRegistry Git Federation Binding / Advertisement

requirements.text: `binding` MUST be `git`. `endpoint` MUST be an absolute HTTPS repository URL with a host, and MUST NOT contain credentials, a query or fragment. Native Git, SSH, `file:`, `git+https:` and remote-helper transports are not part of this binding. A web page URL is not implicitly a repository.

source.section: xRegistry Git Federation Binding / Advertisement

requirements.text: | `revision` | REQUIRED string: full Git ref or complete SHA-1/SHA-256 object ID. |

source.section: xRegistry Git Federation Binding / Advertisement

requirements.text: | `path` | OPTIONAL portable relative directory. Default `xregistry`. `""` selects the repository tree root. |

source.section: xRegistry Git Federation Binding / Advertisement

requirements.text: A full ref MUST begin with `refs/` and pass Git's [`check-ref-format`](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-check-ref-format) rules. For example, `refs/heads/main` and `refs/tags/release-1` are valid. The resolver MUST NOT accept:

source.section: xRegistry Git Federation Binding / Advertisement

requirements.text: A nonempty `path` MUST use `/`-separated portable directory components. Components MUST be 1 to 64 ASCII letters, digits, `_`, `-` or `.`, begin with a letter, digit or `_`, and MUST NOT end in `.`. A component MUST NOT have a case-insensitive Windows device name (`CON`, `PRN`, `AUX`, `NUL`, `COM1` through `COM9`, or `LPT1` through `LPT9`, including before an extension). Leading/trailing separators, empty components, `.` and `..`, backslashes, colon/drive names, URI escapes and OS aliases are forbidden. This constraint applies to the storage root locator, not to Core entity IDs.

source.section: xRegistry Git Federation Binding / Advertisement

requirements.text: An unknown selected parameter MUST produce `unsupported_operation`. Authentication and endpoint authorization are supplied by caller policy, never by embedded metadata credentials.

source.section: xRegistry Git Federation Binding / Revision and Object Selection

requirements.text: The resolver MUST establish one repository context using the selected HTTPS endpoint and the caller's access policy. It can fetch into an isolated object store, but MUST NOT create or execute a working tree. Any acquisition MUST be explicit, bounded and complete for the requested operation.

source.section: xRegistry Git Federation Binding / Revision and Object Selection

requirements.text: The resolver MUST resolve `revision` once. Lightweight tags and branches select their referenced object. The resolver MUST peel annotated tags to a commit. An object that cannot resolve to a commit is invalid selection input.

source.section: xRegistry Git Federation Binding / Revision and Object Selection

requirements.text: The resolver MUST record the resulting complete commit OID and retain that pin for the entire operation, including model, label and document reads. If the original ref moves, that movement MUST NOT change the pin or trigger a second resolution. Consumers MUST NOT substitute a currently reachable or newer commit when the selected commit is inaccessible.

source.section: xRegistry Git Federation Binding / Revision and Object Selection

requirements.text: Starting at the pinned commit's tree, the resolver MUST walk `path` with case-sensitive Git tree-name comparison. Every component MUST be a tree. The selected tree MUST contain the format root `registry.json`. Every format `href` is resolved inside that same selected tree.

source.section: xRegistry Git Federation Binding / Revision and Object Selection

requirements.text: Consumers MUST read `registry.json`, external records and indexes, and documents as blob payloads. An inline record or index is read as part of its containing file's blob. Consumers MUST NOT use checkout bytes, text conversion, clean/smudge filters or attributes. They MUST NOT use LFS downloads, hooks, external diff commands, build steps or repository code. Blob modes `100644` and `100755` both denote data; executable permission does not authorize execution. Consumers MUST verify Git object type and identity as well as the format's descriptor size and SHA-256.

source.section: xRegistry Git Federation Binding / Revision and Object Selection

requirements.text: A Git OID hashes the typed Git object representation, rather than the raw document bytes. It is distinct from a document SHA-256 and a Core `versionid`. The result origin MUST distinguish the repository endpoint, selected root path, requested revision and resolved commit. These values neither become `self` nor modify the selected entity XID.

source.section: xRegistry Git Federation Binding / Read Operations

requirements.text: Explicit XID traversal MUST NOT retrieve unrelated domain documents. Collection selection MUST apply the common literal label comparison and inspect the complete necessary index/member metadata before asserting uniqueness. Neither tree ordering nor a Git tag determines the default Resource Version, whose choice follows [Core default selection](../../core/spec.md#default-version-of-a-resource).

source.section: xRegistry Git Federation Binding / Read Operations

requirements.text: Both linked and offline-complete snapshots MUST contain every internal graph object in the selected commit. Linked external document locators require a separate caller-authorized retrieval, not an implicit Git fetch. Relative domain links use the format's explicit document base, not the repository URL. Core [`xref`](../../core/spec.md#cross-referencing-resources) is resolved only inside this captured Registry and remains one-hop. It is not a link to another repository.

source.section: xRegistry Git Federation Binding / Unsupported Indirections

requirements.text: | Git object or indirection | REQUIRED outcome |

source.section: xRegistry Git Federation Binding / Errors and Security

requirements.text: Resolvers MUST enforce HTTPS authentication, certificate, redirect and credential-scoping policy during acquisition. They MUST disable unsupported protocols, repository-controlled execution and implicit lazy fetching.

source.section: xRegistry Git Federation Binding / Errors and Security

requirements.text: Local object-store alternates, replacement objects, grafts, untrusted configuration includes and filesystem indirections MUST NOT silently change the selected object graph or bypass the permitted storage boundary.

source.section: xRegistry Git Federation Binding / Errors and Security

requirements.text: Readers using Git subprocesses MUST pass validated arguments directly without shell evaluation, and MUST isolate unsafe configuration/environment settings.

source.section: xRegistry Git Federation Binding / Errors and Security

requirements.text: The resolver MUST apply explicit resource limits to acquisition, tag peeling, tree traversal and object reads. It MUST NOT report an exhausted limit or incomplete acquisition as a successful empty result, or use either condition to justify fallback to another profile.

source.section: xRegistry Git Federation Binding / Conformance

requirements.text: A producer MUST publish a complete document-tree mapping at the advertised path in one commit. A native resolver MUST implement locator validation, commit pinning, object-only reads, the common operations and the rejection rules above. An offline-complete snapshot additionally contains all declared document bytes locally.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / Abstract

requirements.text: One OCI image index identifies the selected complete Registry snapshot. Nested standard image indexes describe its Registry, Group, Resource and collection containment. Image manifests reference portable metadata configs and independently addressable Version document blobs. Ordinary OCI descriptor edges reach all REQUIRED content.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 1. Scope and Notation

requirements.text: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" are to be interpreted as described in [RFC 2119][rfc2119].

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 1. Scope and Notation

requirements.text: This profile uses OCI Image Specification **v1.1.1** and Distribution Specification **v1.1.1**. The Image Specification states that implementations SHOULD support nested indexes. Within this profile, producers, resolvers and copy tools **MUST** support them. This requirement does not imply support for the format in every OCI client or container runtime.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 1. Scope and Notation

requirements.text: Consuming a Package is read-only. Constructing and publishing a Package are separate operations. This binding does not define write-through, replication, synchronization, delta replay, arbitrary domain-document dependency discovery or conflict resolution. An xRegistry HTTP facade is OPTIONAL and MUST separately conform to [the HTTP binding](../../core/http.md).

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 2. Advertisement and Root Selection

requirements.text: `endpoint` MUST contain an OCI host, an OPTIONAL port, and a nonempty repository name. The repository MUST obey the Distribution repository grammar. The endpoint MUST NOT contain credentials, a tag, an `@digest`, a query, or a fragment.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 2. Advertisement and Root Selection

requirements.text: `parameters.reference` is REQUIRED and MUST be either a Distribution tag (at most 128 characters) or `sha256:` followed by exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 2. Advertisement and Root Selection / 2.1. Distribution selection

requirements.text: The resolver MUST request the selected reference at `/v2/<repository>/manifests/<reference>`. The returned object MUST be a Registry index as defined below, not a flat inventory, Version manifest, layout index, or collection index.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 2. Advertisement and Root Selection / 2.1. Distribution selection

requirements.text: The resolver MUST compute SHA-256 over the exact returned bytes. If the reference is a digest, the resolver MUST compare the computed digest with it. If the reference is a tag, the resolver MUST retain the computed digest as the snapshot pin before traversing any child.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 2. Advertisement and Root Selection / 2.1. Distribution selection

requirements.text: All subsequent requests in the operation MUST use descriptor digests without resolving the tag again. The selected state remains unchanged if the tag moves. A missing descendant MUST NOT trigger a retry at a newer root.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 2. Advertisement and Root Selection / 2.1. Distribution selection

requirements.text: If the response includes a SHA-256 `Docker-Content-Digest` header, its value MUST agree with the bytes. The resolver still computes the digest itself; the header does not replace that check. An absent header is not an error. A different supported digest algorithm in the header is verified independently and does not replace the profile's SHA-256 pin.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 2. Advertisement and Root Selection / 2.2. Image layout selection

requirements.text: A local layout uses OCI's `oci-layout`, `index.json` and `blobs/sha256/<hex>` paths. `imageLayoutVersion` MUST be `1.0.0`. The layout's `index.json` provides an entry point rather than the Registry snapshot itself. It MAY list several roots and unrelated OCI artifacts. Every index, including this entry point, MUST satisfy the bounds in Section 4. The entry point need not list every blob stored in the layout.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 2. Advertisement and Root Selection / 2.2. Image layout selection

requirements.text: A snapshot entry descriptor MUST use the standard index media type and `artifactType: application/vnd.xregistry.registry.v1+json`. Its OPTIONAL `org.opencontainers.image.ref.name` annotation supplies its tag. This annotation MUST NOT be used as Version identity or on internal edges. Profile-specific edge annotations are not REQUIRED on layout entries.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 2. Advertisement and Root Selection / 2.2. Image layout selection

requirements.text: If an interactive tool offers unqualified selection, it MUST select only when exactly one distinct eligible Registry root digest is advertised. Zero is `not_found`, and more than one is `ambiguous`. Advertisements themselves always have an explicit reference.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 2. Advertisement and Root Selection / 2.2. Image layout selection

requirements.text: After selection, the resolver MUST verify the root and retain its digest. It MUST NOT merge different roots. Extra blobs and other roots are outside the selected root's closure. These rules also govern the File binding's `layout: oci-layout` mode.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 3. Media Types and Descriptor Rules

requirements.text: All indexes and manifests MUST set `schemaVersion: 2`, the indicated `mediaType`, and the indicated `artifactType`. Their annotations MUST include `io.xregistry.oci.version: "1"`, `io.xregistry.oci.kind`, and `io.xregistry.oci.xid`. The kind is `registry`, `group`, `resource`, `collections`, `collection`, `meta`, or `version`, as appropriate. Metadata manifests use the kind of the entity they describe.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 3. Media Types and Descriptor Rules

requirements.text: Every internal descriptor MUST contain `mediaType`, `digest`, `size`, and string-valued annotations `io.xregistry.oci.role` and `io.xregistry.oci.xid`. The XID is the target entity or collection path. For collection directories it is the owning entity's XID. A shard retains its routing index's XID. A config, document or empty layer descriptor retains its owning entity's XID.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 3. Media Types and Descriptor Rules

requirements.text: Internal descriptors MUST use SHA-256 and the exact byte length, including JSON whitespace and any final newline. They MUST NOT use `urls`, `data`, or `platform`. Blobs MUST actually be available in the same repository or layout, even for tiny placeholders. An OPTIONAL descriptor `artifactType` MUST agree with the referenced index or manifest. Consumers MUST verify both size and digest before interpreting content.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 3. Media Types and Descriptor Rules

requirements.text: `root` is reserved for fixture-tool output and MAY annotate a layout entry. It is not an internal containment role. A descriptor's role, media type, XID and target kind MUST agree. Unknown REQUIRED roles are not silently ignored.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 3. Media Types and Descriptor Rules

requirements.text: Only the seven annotation suffixes `version`, `kind`, `xid`, `role`, `mode`, `lower`, and `upper` are defined in `io.xregistry.oci.`. A consumer MUST reject unknown keys in that namespace in version 1.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 3. Media Types and Descriptor Rules

requirements.text: Other OCI annotations MAY be included but MUST NOT carry REQUIRED containment, model, labels or other authoritative entity metadata. Configs store the full metadata; stringified JSON annotation values do not replace them. Annotation keys and string values also follow OCI's annotation rules.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 3. Media Types and Descriptor Rules

requirements.text: `subject` MUST NOT be used in the REQUIRED snapshot graph. OPTIONAL provenance and signatures can be separate artifacts associated with the root through `subject` and referrers. They are not prerequisites for enumerating or reading the snapshot and are not automatically copied with ordinary containment.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 4. Containment and Range Shards

requirements.text: Each arrow represents a standard OCI `manifests[]`, `config` or `layers[]` descriptor edge. Storing a digest in a custom JSON field does not create such an edge. A manifest MUST NOT hide child manifests inside its data layers.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 4. Containment and Range Shards

requirements.text: A Registry or Group index MUST contain, in order, exactly one `metadata` descriptor and one `collections` descriptor. A Resource index MUST contain, in order, `metadata`, `meta`, and `collections`. Thus entity indexes remain constant-sized even when the model defines many child collection types. All their metadata is detached into configs.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 4. Containment and Range Shards

requirements.text: A collection has kind `collection`. Its leaf entries use role `entity`. All are immediate children of that collection's typed path. For example, `/dirs/main/files` contains Resource indexes, while `/dirs/main/files/report/versions` contains Version manifests. There MUST be exactly one entry per entity. Paths retain type names as well as IDs. Neither ID-only keys nor case-folded keys are sufficient.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 4. Containment and Range Shards / 4.1. Bounds and ordering

requirements.text: **Every index MUST have at most 256 `manifests` descriptors and at most 1,048,576 encoded JSON bytes. Both limits apply independently.** The descriptor count includes metadata and control descriptors as well as entity entries. Both limits apply to routing indexes and the layout entry-point index. The byte limit applies to the exact UTF-8 representation used for the digest, including whitespace, annotations and any final newline. A character count or reserialized estimate cannot replace that measurement.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 4. Containment and Range Shards / 4.1. Bounds and ordering

requirements.text: A producer MUST split a routing index before exceeding either limit. It MAY also shard smaller indexes. If an individual entry or fixed entity index cannot fit, the outcome is `limit_exceeded`; data cannot be silently dropped. The 256-descriptor limit does not cap collection size. Additional routing levels support arbitrarily large finite collections. A consumer MAY impose separately reported depth, total-byte or object-count policy limits.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 4. Containment and Range Shards / 4.1. Bounds and ordering

requirements.text: Before this byte comparison, the serialized keys MUST use the following canonical URI-component encoding. Validate percent escapes and decode each component exactly once as strict UTF-8, then validate the decoded Core type, identifier and hierarchy.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 4. Containment and Range Shards / 4.1. Bounds and ordering

requirements.text: Emit ASCII unreserved characters literally and percent-encode every other allowed component character using uppercase hexadecimal. Under the current Core ID grammar, `:` is therefore `%3A` and `@` is `%40`. Type names and the fixed `meta` and `versions` components are emitted literally. Case-sensitive entity identity MUST be preserved. No case folding, second decoding pass or Unicode normalization is permitted.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 4. Containment and Range Shards / 4.1. Bounds and ordering

requirements.text: This encoding is REQUIRED for every `io.xregistry.oci.xid` on an internal descriptor, index or manifest, and every finite `lower` or `upper` boundary. A consumer MUST reject a consumed noncanonical annotation as `invalid_package`, not probe alternative serialized spellings or rewrite the verified object.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 4. Containment and Range Shards / 4.1. Bounds and ordering

requirements.text: A caller's XID selector MUST be validated and canonicalized once before routing, retaining the original requested identity separately from the selected config's serialization. URI-equivalent selectors then follow the same one-interval-per-level lookup.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 4. Containment and Range Shards / 4.1. Bounds and ordering

requirements.text: Portable config `entity.xid` and Meta `xref` MAY retain another valid, URI-equivalent spelling. Their decoded, case-sensitive identity MUST agree with their canonical descriptor identity. Their original bytes still determine the config digest. Producers MUST NOT rewrite those bytes during a read.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 4. Containment and Range Shards / 4.1. Bounds and ordering

requirements.text: JSON map keys and document-local pointers use decoded IDs. Producers MUST reject duplicate decoded sibling identities, including Core's case-insensitive sibling collisions. Domain URLs, document base/origin and domain-document bytes are not subject to this routing-key encoding.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 4. Containment and Range Shards / 4.1. Bounds and ordering

requirements.text: A layout containing noncanonical graph annotations requires explicit migration or regeneration, with new digests propagated to its root. A producer MUST NOT relabel it as conforming. The original layout can be retained as migration evidence. The encoding does not prescribe a canonical JSON serialization or a unique placement of shard boundaries.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 4. Containment and Range Shards / 4.2. Exact range representation

requirements.text: Every directory, collection and shard MUST carry these annotations:

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 4. Containment and Range Shards / 4.2. Exact range representation

requirements.text: The top directory or collection has range `["", "")`, meaning the whole key space in this notation, not an empty interval. Other nonempty bounds MUST themselves be valid keys in the routing scope. A finite lower bound MUST be strictly less than a finite upper bound.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 4. Containment and Range Shards / 4.2. Exact range representation

requirements.text: A **leaf** has only the appropriate `collection` or `entity` descriptors, strictly sorted by XID. Each key MUST be at least the lower bound and strictly below the upper bound. Duplicates are invalid even when their descriptors are identical. An empty collection or directory MUST be an unsharded leaf with zero descriptors and the whole-space range.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 4. Containment and Range Shards / 4.2. Exact range representation

requirements.text: A **branch** has at least two `shard` descriptors. Every shard descriptor MUST have `lower` and `upper` annotations equal to those on its target index. Target kind and XID MUST equal the parent's.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 4. Containment and Range Shards / 4.2. Exact range representation

requirements.text: The first lower bound MUST equal the parent's lower bound. The last upper bound MUST equal the parent's upper bound. Every intervening upper bound MUST equal the next lower bound, and MUST be finite. The descriptors MUST be ordered by these bounds.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 4. Containment and Range Shards / 4.2. Exact range representation

requirements.text: All shards MUST contain at least one eventual entry. Branch and leaf entry roles MUST NOT be mixed.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 4. Containment and Range Shards / 4.2. Exact range representation

requirements.text: This illustrates the annotation values. A boundary MAY fall between existing entity IDs. Gaps in the set of entity IDs are ordinary. Gaps or overlaps in routing intervals are invalid. A producer can choose each split boundary as the first key in the right-hand shard. Split choice is not globally canonical.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 4. Containment and Range Shards / 4.2. Exact range representation

requirements.text: A full validator MUST verify the complete partition and closure, rather than only one successful lookup path. A selective reader validates the path it consumes and cannot establish that unvisited shards are well formed or that their objects exist and are consistent. A complete conformance or absence claim covering all serialized representations requires full validation. A selective `not_found` result covers only the canonical routed lookup.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 5. Metadata and Documents / 5.1. Portable entity configs

requirements.text: The `kind` MUST agree with the containing manifest and structural path. `entity` MUST preserve Core attributes and model-defined extensions, including nested extension values, timestamps, epochs, label maps, IDs, Version ancestry and explicitly selected defaults.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 5. Metadata and Documents / 5.1. Portable entity configs

requirements.text: The following storage decomposition is REQUIRED:

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 5. Metadata and Documents / 5.1. Portable entity configs

requirements.text: - `formatvalidated` and `compatibilityvalidated` are absent, as in Core document view. For Resource types with `hasdocument: true`, domain Documents are detached and MUST NOT be duplicated in the `<RESOURCE>` or `<RESOURCE>base64` fields of configs.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 5. Metadata and Documents / 5.1. Portable entity configs

requirements.text: For Resource types with `hasdocument: false`, model-admitted attributes with these spellings, or `<RESOURCE>url`, are ordinary metadata. Consumers MUST preserve and validate them according to their model definitions. Consumers MUST NOT drop them or interpret them as Document content or locators.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 5. Metadata and Documents / 5.2. Model preservation

requirements.text: The Registry config additionally MUST contain `snapshot` with value `linked` or `offline-complete`, and `modelresolved`. Its `entity` MUST include `specversion`, `registryid`, `model`, `modelsource` and `capabilities`.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 5. Metadata and Documents / 5.2. Model preservation

requirements.text: Capabilities MUST describe access to this read-only snapshot, not advertise the source server's write operations or unsupported HTTP flags as native OCI features. Other Registry metadata preserves the captured identity and state. Capability mapping does not change its XIDs.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 5. Metadata and Documents / 5.2. Model preservation

requirements.text: `entity.model` contains the full resolved Core model, including Core attributes. `entity.modelsource` preserves the original model-source value. The separate `modelresolved` value captures the source after [Core `$include`/`$includes` processing](../../core/model.md#includes-in-the-xregistry-model-data) but **before** expansion of `ximportresources` or addition of implicit Core aspects. This value uses the existing Core model-source language and MUST retain Resource type-sharing provenance.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 5. Metadata and Documents / 5.2. Model preservation

requirements.text: `modelresolved` MUST NOT contain unresolved include directives. The full model MUST reflect the same resolved definitions and imports. A consumer can therefore interpret the snapshot without fetching a mutable remote model, while the original source remains available for inspection.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 5. Metadata and Documents / 5.3. Version documents and placeholders

requirements.text: A Version config MUST have a `document` object containing `mode`:

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 5. Metadata and Documents / 5.3. Version documents and placeholders

requirements.text: An external URL MUST be absolute and credential-free. A consumer MUST resolve a relative domain-document locator against its original retrieval base before capture, never against an OCI repository, XID, or config blob path.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 5. Metadata and Documents / 5.3. Version documents and placeholders

requirements.text: A captured copy of an externally stored document uses `embedded`. Its original locator MAY be retained as `document.origin`, not as a misleading Core `<RESOURCE>url`.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 5. Metadata and Documents / 5.3. Version documents and placeholders

requirements.text: Embedded content MAY also retain an absolute `document.base` for resolving relative references inside the domain document. A resolver MUST preserve this base when returning the bytes. It MUST NOT substitute the OCI repository or config path.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 5. Metadata and Documents / 5.3. Version documents and placeholders

requirements.text: Both OPTIONAL fields MUST be credential-free absolute URIs and MUST appear only in `embedded` mode. Reads obtain the pinned bytes from the selected snapshot rather than fetching the original locator again.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 5. Metadata and Documents / 5.3. Version documents and placeholders

requirements.text: `metadata-only` MUST agree with `hasdocument: false`. Such Versions MUST NOT carry a domain Document or a Document locator. Ordinary model-admitted metadata attributes named `<RESOURCE>`, `<RESOURCE>base64` or `<RESOURCE>url` do not constitute Document content or a locator. Consumers MUST NOT decode, fetch, drop or reject them merely because of their names.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 5. Metadata and Documents / 5.3. Version documents and placeholders

requirements.text: All metadata manifests and non-embedded Version manifests MUST have one `empty` layer. Its media type is `application/vnd.oci.empty.v1+json`, its content is exactly the two bytes `{}`, its size is 2, and its digest is `sha256:44136fa355b3678a1146ad16f7e8649e94fb4fc21fe77e8310c060f61caaff8a`. This follows OCI's portability guidance for an unused layer. It is not a domain document.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 5. Metadata and Documents / 5.3. Version documents and placeholders

requirements.text: An actual empty domain document has size 0 and digest `sha256:e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855`. Consumers MUST NOT replace one with the other.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 5. Metadata and Documents / 5.4. Snapshot completeness

requirements.text: Both snapshot classes MUST contain the complete internal descriptor closure: all structural indexes, metadata manifests, configs, embedded documents and placeholders. OCI layout's general allowance for missing blobs does not relax this profile.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 5. Metadata and Documents / 5.4. Snapshot completeness

requirements.text: A `linked` snapshot MAY have `external` documents. An `offline-complete` snapshot MUST NOT: every document declared to exist in its captured scope has embedded bytes. `metadata-only` explicitly declares no domain document and does not invalidate offline completeness. An offline-complete claim does not guarantee availability of a domain document for every possible document request.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 5. Metadata and Documents / 5.5. Core document-view results and local references

requirements.text: A config record stores metadata but is not itself an API entity. A native metadata operation MUST assemble a [Core document-view result](../../core/spec.md#doc-flag) from the records. The baseline view inlines the requested metadata subtree, including Meta and Version metadata, recreates collection counts and navigation fields, and excludes domain-document bytes.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 5. Metadata and Documents / 5.5. Core document-view results and local references

requirements.text: `self` and navigation URLs MUST be valid `#`-prefixed JSON Pointers into that returned document. `#` denotes the empty pointer to the document root. Transport endpoint and snapshot pin are separate result context.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 5. Metadata and Documents / 5.5. Core document-view results and local references

requirements.text: An implementation offering a different partial view MUST provide actual retrievable, Core-conforming absolute URLs for non-inlined navigation, or report `unsupported_operation`. A resolver MUST NOT present an arbitrary implementation-defined `oci:` URI as a conforming `self` URL.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 5. Metadata and Documents / 5.5. Core document-view results and local references

requirements.text: A domain-document operation is not the Core `doc` metadata flag. It MAY resolve the source Resource's default, or an explicit Version's bytes, through one local `xref` hop.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 5. Metadata and Documents / 5.5. Core document-view results and local references

requirements.text: A resolver supporting this operation MUST verify same-Registry and same Resource model type. It MUST NOT chase a second hop. It MUST retain source target identity separately from the resolved Version XID. A dangling or alias target has no retrievable document. Absolute remote `xref` values or wrong Resource model types are invalid.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 6. Native Read Operations

requirements.text: Indexes and manifests use `GET /v2/<repository>/manifests/<digest>`. Config, document and placeholder blobs use `GET /v2/<repository>/blobs/<digest>`. Clients MUST NOT use the blob endpoint for an index merely because a local layout stores all objects below `blobs`. Nor is the document layer's XID a Distribution URL.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 6. Native Read Operations

requirements.text: Manifest requests MUST advertise both standard index and image-manifest media types in `Accept`. The response's media type, ignoring HTTP parameters, MUST agree with the descriptor and JSON `mediaType`. `HEAD` MAY be used for existence checks but does not replace byte verification. Unsupported REQUIRED artifact kinds or format versions are reported explicitly rather than mistaken for empty collections.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 6. Native Read Operations

requirements.text: A direct Version lookup reads the routing path, the selected Version manifest and its config. It reads the payload only for a document operation and MUST NOT require unrelated Version documents or the whole Registry's metadata. It can read model and capabilities bootstrap data and the Resource Meta needed to check default consistency.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 6. Native Read Operations

requirements.text: The resolver MUST examine every necessary shard before asserting uniqueness. Zero matches are `not_found`. Multiple matches are `ambiguous`, including a match on a later page. OPTIONAL acceleration MUST NOT alter this result or hide missing content. Version documents need not be fetched to select by label.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 7. Production and Publication

requirements.text: A producer MUST capture a coherent Registry state, including its model, capabilities, defaults and Version metadata. If changes to the source prevent a coherent capture, the producer MUST report `inconsistent_snapshot` and MUST NOT publish that capture as a complete snapshot.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 7. Production and Publication

requirements.text: A publisher SHOULD use the Distribution existence and blob-mount mechanisms to reuse content where supported. Reusing an unchanged subtree's digest avoids rewriting its descendants. Each newly published root still denotes a complete graph. Reading it MUST NOT require an old snapshot, parent root, delta chain or replay log.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 7. Production and Publication

requirements.text: JSON serialization and shard grouping determine the bytes and therefore affect digests. A producer MAY make its own output reproducible, but the profile defines no globally canonical semantic digest. A digest verifies exact bytes without establishing common authority or semantic equality.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 7. Production and Publication

requirements.text: Copying MUST preserve the selected root and all standard containment descendants. A compatible artifact copier MUST support nested indexes, typed artifact configs, opaque layers and zero-byte document blobs. Normal containment copy does not require a referrers operation. ORAS's `--recursive` option concerns referrer artifacts. It is not the definition of nested-index containment traversal.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 8. Errors and Security

requirements.text: Consumers MUST reject duplicate JSON keys, invalid UTF-8 and non-JSON numbers.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 8. Errors and Security

requirements.text: Consumers MUST detect cycles and impose finite resource budgets. Exhausting a budget causes failure, not successful enumeration of a truncated result. Verifying the selected path does not establish that unvisited shards are well formed.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 8. Errors and Security

requirements.text: Use authenticated HTTPS and repository-scoped credentials under caller policy. OCI metadata MUST NOT contain credentials. Redirect destinations, external document URLs and filesystem roots require independent policy checks. A layout reader MUST NOT forward Authorization headers indiscriminately.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 8. Errors and Security

requirements.text: A layout reader MUST prevent path traversal and symlink or reparse-point escape. A blob name is derived from a validated digest, never from an ID.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 8. Errors and Security

requirements.text: Untrusted document blobs are data, not executable code. Consumers MUST NOT execute hooks or start containers. They MUST NOT extract archives or interpret domain links merely to traverse this profile.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 8. Errors and Security

requirements.text: Integrity checks do not authorize a publisher. Trust decisions and OPTIONAL signature checks are separate from format validation. Integrity and policy errors MUST NOT silently trigger fallback to another [advertisement](#2-advertisement-and-root-selection). See the [Federation binding-selection rules](../federation/spec.md#discovery-and-binding-selection).

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 9. Conformance and Executable Examples

requirements.text: A **producer** implements Sections 2 through 5 and 7. A **native resolver** implements root pinning, metadata/document operations, range traversal, shared selection, Core view semantics and integrity/error rules. A **linked snapshot** and an **offline-complete snapshot** satisfy their respective Section 5.4 requirements. A **compatible copier** preserves the selected descriptor closure. Claims MUST state which roles apply.

source.section: xRegistry OCI Binding - Working Draft / 9. Conformance and Executable Examples / Verify a Copy

requirements.text: A copy exercise MUST execute the tool and verify the copied root and all REQUIRED descendants. Merely parsing JSON or quoting tool help is not interoperability evidence. Offline layout copying does not establish a Distribution round trip, and a round trip against one configured service does not establish support in every registry or client. The integration test requires a configured test registry and ORAS. It runs separately from the offline suite:

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Scope

requirements.text: These file roles apply to locally stored, document-backed Resources. The companion's OPTIONAL `MetadataResourceType` is instead a `BaseObjectType` subtype for a metadata-only Resource with `hasdocument: false` and `maxversions: 1`. It has no domain file interface. An unresolved local `xref` or an unmaterialized remote proxy does not require local Version Objects. Sections 5.10 and 10 describe these cases.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Scope

requirements.text: This binding is independent of any domain registry. Domain companion specifications define subtypes of `RegistryType`, `GroupType` and `ResourceType` and constrain Group and Resource names. They MAY add domain Properties or Methods. These specializations do not change the OPC UA API patterns defined here.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 2. Normative references

requirements.text: - [xRegistry Publication](../publication/spec.md) — OPTIONAL retained-publication behavior used by §10.4.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 3. Terms and conventions

requirements.text: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in [RFC 2119](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2119).

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. The OPC UA API access model / 4.1. AddressSpace root and service model

requirements.text: A server MAY expose multiple Registries. Before applying this API, a client selects a Registry root by NodeId, BrowsePath, discovery metadata or domain convention. A federation advertisement supplies the portable `registryroot` NodeId specified in §10.1. Selecting an endpoint alone does not select a Registry.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. The OPC UA API access model / 4.1. AddressSpace root and service model

requirements.text: All operations that create, modify or delete registry content or metadata MUST use a SecureChannel with `MessageSecurityMode` `SignAndEncrypt`. This includes get-or-create Calls, file write Opens, Writes and committing Closes, label and native-document mutations, deletion and domain Methods that change registry state. Roles and Permissions apply independently. Reads SHOULD use a secured channel. Deployment policy MAY permit read-only operations and event subscriptions over `None`, but clients MUST NOT infer authenticity, integrity or confidentiality from such a connection.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. The OPC UA API access model / 4.1. AddressSpace root and service model

requirements.text: If an xRegistry function is not supported for an otherwise supported node, the server MUST return `Bad_NotSupported`, `Bad_UserAccessDenied`, `Bad_NotWritable`, `Bad_MethodInvalid` or `Bad_InvalidArgument` as appropriate. If the requested node or Property cannot be resolved, the server MUST return an appropriate StatusCode such as `Bad_NodeIdUnknown`, `Bad_BrowseNameInvalid` or `Bad_NotFound` where available.

requirements.text: - Each logical Resource and exact Version MUST be a `ResourceType` or the same domain subtype when it uses the document-backed contract.
