requirements.text: 5. Before reading the target as a Registry entity, verify its Registry root, model, Core version, NodeClass, TypeDefinition ancestry, structural role and origin-relative XID. A logical `ExternalReference` MUST identify the remote logical Resource Object of FileType or a subtype, not a folder, exact Version or content-digest Variable. Exact Version selection uses that Resource's verified `Versions` hierarchy or an explicitly exact-Version reference. A same-application target still needs the correct Registry-root check. Read file bytes with a new target-local handle under §5.13.1 only after these checks succeed.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 10. Federation / 10.2. Structured reference resolution

requirements.text: A table index has meaning only in its captured context. The resolver remaps indexes after reconnecting or selecting another Server. A missing namespace produces a specific failure, never a substitution of namespace zero. For storage without table context, Part 6 provides `nsu=` and, for an application-specific reference, `svu=`. The `svu=` value is an Application URI, not a connectable endpoint. Namespace and Application URIs MUST be compared as exact opaque strings, without URL normalization.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 10. Federation / 10.2. Structured reference resolution

requirements.text: For de-duplication, the source key MUST contain the trusted origin, concrete origin-relative XID and logical/exact role. The application/root form uses both values, not Application URI alone. Equal XIDs or document bytes from independent origins remain separate. An authorized locator change or table reordering MUST NOT change the pinned origin, XID, role or remote Node identity. A changed origin, including a switch between authoritative forms, is a different source, not a reconnect.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 10. Federation / 10.3. Three distinct reference mechanisms

requirements.text: A local `xref` MUST remain the case-sensitive XID of a same-typed Resource in the same Registry, represented by `MetaXref`. It MUST NOT be an absolute URI or remote-node locator. Structurally identical Resource definitions do not establish a shared type. Imported/shared types follow Core [`ximportresources`](https://github.com/xregistry/spec/blob/v1.0-rc4/core/model.md#reuse-of-resource-definitions). When the target is accessible, the Server exposes the Core-derived target view under the source Resource's identity while retaining the source `ResourceId`, `Xid`, self reference and `MetaXref`. It MUST NOT follow a target `xref` transitively. When the target is inaccessible or dangling, the source identity and `MetaXref` remain readable; the Server is not REQUIRED to detect the condition or provide local Version storage. The source's minimal serialization remains valid. `ExternalReference` MUST NOT substitute for `MetaXref`.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 10. Federation / 10.3. Three distinct reference mechanisms

requirements.text: A Resource describing remote bytes retains local metadata. Remote `Xid`, `ResourceId`, `VersionId`, labels or Meta values MUST NOT silently overwrite that local describing entity. To read the remote Registry intentionally, the caller establishes a separate context. A domain can explicitly define logical-identity relationships; equal XIDs in unrelated Registries do not establish one.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 10. Federation / 10.3. Three distinct reference mechanisms

requirements.text: An unsupported retrieval scheme or undocumented convention MUST fail explicitly. Implementations MUST NOT assume `ResourceUrl` and `ExternalReference` are interchangeable spellings of one target. If both are present, a declared mapping and policy determine their relationship and selection. Arbitrary precedence does not resolve conflicting or ambiguous targets.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 10. Federation / 10.3. Three distinct reference mechanisms

requirements.text: `XREG-GroupFederation` is a separate OPTIONAL facet. A Group reference owns read-only `OriginRegistry`, `ExternalReference` and `GroupUrl` Properties. Its source key includes the trusted origin, collection-qualified Group XID and Group role. Selection MUST verify the remote `GroupType` ancestry, REQUIRED domain subtype, XID and Registry ownership. A Resource, Version or Registry root MUST NOT substitute for that Group. `GroupUrl` is only an authorized locator. The referencing server maps the verified remote Application URI through its own `ServerArray`; setting `ServerIndex` to zero does not make a remote target local. A native Group metadata identity claim MUST agree with the independent Group observation. Epoch rollback, or different metadata at an already observed epoch, MUST fail without replacing the last verified observation.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 10. Federation / 10.4. Trust and live consistency

requirements.text: Catalog metadata, discovered endpoints and remote references supply untrusted locators, not trust decisions. The resolver checks destination, transport, application certificate and authorization at every hop. Credentials, user identity tokens and file handles MUST NOT be forwarded to a remote Server by implication. After a policy, integrity or version failure, the resolver MUST NOT weaken security or silently try another advertisement.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 10. Federation / 10.4. Trust and live consistency

requirements.text: The server MUST persist immutable origin selection and portable remote identity with the owning logical Resource's federation record. Restore MUST validate the exclusive origin form, agreement with its trusted binding, XID, target role and portable Node identities. It MUST NOT silently repair contradictory records, persist Session-local indexes as identity pins or reinterpret an origin change as relocation. Restoring pins does not authenticate a peer; fresh provider and Session checks precede use. Group federation records follow the same origin and portable-identity rules.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 10. Federation / 10.4. Trust and live consistency

requirements.text: A live Browse/Read/FileTransfer capture MUST retain its scope and observations and disclose that it has no cross-node atomic snapshot guarantee. A pinned native document view guarantees only the selected document and authorization view under §4.5, not a transaction over remote providers or separately opened domain files. If a consistent capture is requested, changed membership, default selection, table mapping, metadata or file contents during capture MUST produce `inconsistent_snapshot`. Per-node timestamps alone cannot establish cross-node atomicity.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 10. Federation / 10.4. Trust and live consistency

requirements.text: The OPTIONAL [publication extension](../publication/spec.md) provides retained exact Version documents rather than inferring a snapshot from these live indicators. Its descriptors select Registry access with `binding: "opcua"`, the endpoint and the parameters in §10.1, followed by an exact Version XID. Resolve that Version under the selected Registry root using §4.2, then read its raw document bytes using §5.13.1. This applies to the manifest and captured Registry JSON as well as domain documents. A captured Registry JSON Version is not the live multi-read export in §5.3. No HTTP facade, HTTP GET or standard UA context node is needed.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 10. Federation / 10.4. Trust and live consistency

requirements.text: To open a channel, obtain a coherent `scope`, complete `head` and `MetaEpoch` from its Resource Meta. Return the checked publication open record as caller-visible context and retain it across reads. If the adapter cannot represent the Meta extensions or obtain a coherent head, it MUST report the operation as unsupported or inconsistent instead of substituting the default Version or a live view.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 10. Federation / 10.4. Trust and live consistency

requirements.text: Native write support is a separate capability. `head` is a structured Meta extension, not a string label, so `MetaLabels.AddAttribute` cannot replace it. An adapter can use a supported native `ApplyChanges` targeting the Meta entity, or a documented domain operation, only if it atomically replaces the complete head against the expected `MetaEpoch` and enforces publication validation, scope, immutability and retention. Ordinary native-write support alone does not establish those publication guarantees. A successful multi-Property Write or a client-side read/write sequence does not prove atomic head replacement. An adapter without that guarantee MUST NOT advertise writable publication support. This extension assigns no new standard Method, Property or NodeId to the Version 0.11.0 Draft companion model.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 10. Federation / 10.5. Namespace export is separate

requirements.text: [NamespaceMetadataType][ua-namespace] describes a namespace through, among other members, an OPTIONAL `NamespaceFile` component of type [AddressSpaceFileType][ua-address-file]. It does not discover arbitrary Registries, enumerate the catalog domain or resolve an xRegistry XID.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 10. Federation / 10.5. Namespace export is separate

requirements.text: If the OPTIONAL, parameterless `ExportNamespace` Method is available and permitted, calling it updates the XML file represented by `NamespaceFile`. The client then uses the inherited FileType Open/Read/Close lifecycle:

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 10. Federation / 10.5. Namespace export is separate

requirements.text: The client explicitly requests `ExportNamespace` to refresh the file, separately from ordinary read-only Registry discovery. If the Method is unavailable, the client can read only an exposed existing file and MUST NOT claim a refresh. This type defines neither a standard direct-return `Export` Method nor a standard `Import` Method. Part 5 describes vendor-specific import mechanisms. The example introduces no new domain or gateway.

requirements.text: These are unadopted working drafts. Native-document and snapshot capabilities remain OPTIONAL unless their respective conformance units are claimed.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 10. Federation / 10.6. Companion model alignment

requirements.text: A server MAY expose local proxy or mirror Resources. Their local NodeIds, `Xid`, `ResourceId` and any local `VersionId` remain local identities. The remote XID and logical/exact role belong to the origin-scoped federation record; they MUST NOT overwrite local identity to impersonate the origin. A mirror with locally hosted Versions preserves the distinct local hierarchy. A proxy that does not materialize Versions omits its local `Versions` folder, and the client browses at the verified remote logical target. It MUST NOT fabricate local Version Objects implying locally authoritative remote state.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 11. Error handling

requirements.text: The server reports OPC UA errors as StatusCodes on Service, Operation or Method Call results, or as individual input/output argument diagnostics. If an xRegistry error includes structured details, the server SHOULD include additional information in OPC UA DiagnosticInfo or an available domain-specific error payload.

For a batch implemented as multiple OPC UA Service calls, the failing call's StatusCode and diagnostics identify it. For a domain batch Method, each entity result SHOULD carry its own StatusCode, and the Method result MUST indicate whether partial effects occurred.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 11. Error handling

requirements.text: Authorization failures MUST use `Bad_UserAccessDenied` or `Bad_SecurityChecksFailed`. Authentication and secure-channel failures are governed by OPC 10000-4 and are not redefined by this binding.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 11. Error handling / 11.1. Federation resolver outcomes

requirements.text: The table maps native observations to common resolver outcomes; it defines no new OPC UA StatusCodes. The resolver MUST retain the original Service/operation/Method StatusCode, argument diagnostics and any cleanup failure. A successful Service result does not override a failed node read or Method result.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 11. Error handling / 11.1. Federation resolver outcomes

requirements.text: For an unknown bad or uncertain status, the resolver MUST report failure with the original diagnostic. It MUST NOT treat that status as Good. A normal dangling local `xref` retains Core serialization; it does not mean the source Resource is missing. An explicitly requested early stop or an expired continuation point cannot prove that a label selector has no match.

requirements.text: For document-bearing Resources, read-only conformance also requires `Open`/`Read`/`Close` sufficient to retrieve the declared documents. Document-backed servers MUST NOT expose group-level exact-Version aliases. A metadata-only domain instead declares its applicable units and uses `MetadataResourceType`, collection-qualified identity, coherent metadata reads and any REQUIRED native-access facets. It need not expose the document-backed Resource/Version file hierarchy or fabricate domain bytes.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 12. Conformance

requirements.text: `Name`, `Description`, `Documentation` and `Labels` remain OPTIONAL in these units. `XREG-Identity` does not make `Name` mandatory. A metadata-only catalog Resource MUST NOT claim `XREG-Resource` without its document-backed contract. If it claims `XREG-MetadataResource`, it MUST meet that unit's requirements. A binding-conformance claim does not weaken the requirements of any companion unit it claims.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 12. Conformance

requirements.text: Logical and exact Version opens MUST share exact-Version writer reservations and incarnation safeguards, and logical handles MUST remain pinned to the Version selected at `Open`.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 12. Conformance

requirements.text: All mutating capabilities MUST enforce the `SignAndEncrypt` and authorization rules in §4.1.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 12. Conformance

requirements.text: A server claims `XREG-Events` for event-capable OPC UA xRegistry API conformance. It MUST expose `EventSourceUrl`, the notifier hierarchy and `GeneratesEvent` declarations. For every supported mutation, it MUST generate every event that the xRegistry Events specification, with the §9.1 binding corrections, says MUST be generated. It MUST support standard OPC UA event subscription and delivery under §9.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 12. Conformance

requirements.text: The specification's SHOULD events retain that strength, including Registry lifecycle events and descendants on whole-Registry deletion. REQUIRED descendants of recursive Group and Resource deletion remain MUST events. `XREG-Events` is OPTIONAL, not REQUIRED for read-only, writable or export-capable conformance.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 12. Conformance

requirements.text: A client MUST follow the advertised document-backed, metadata-only or proxy mapping. A missing `Versions` folder alone does not identify another layout.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 12. Conformance

requirements.text: Event-capable client conformance is OPTIONAL and is not REQUIRED for baseline client conformance.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 12. Conformance

requirements.text: A federation client MUST additionally implement the portable root and reference resolution in §10, literal selectors, necessary Browse continuation sequences, FileTransfer cleanup and explicit resolver errors. It MUST distinguish Application URI, endpoint, namespace URI, Session-local NodeId, Registry-root selection and Core XID. It MUST reject unsupported Core versions and disclose incomplete or non-atomic live captures.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 12. Conformance

requirements.text: A conforming implementation MUST NOT assume additional node or Method names. The members it needs MUST come from the Version 0.11.0 Draft companion model, the normative OPC UA Parts in §2, or an explicitly documented domain mapping. The standard Server and namespace tables come from Part 5. Federation introduces no ReferenceType or Registry-discovery Method.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 12. Conformance

requirements.text: A conforming implementation MUST NOT require a node or Method name absent from *OPC UA — xRegistry*, OPC 10000-20 or its own domain companion specification.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Notations and Terminology

requirements.text: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in [RFC2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119).

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Notations and Terminology

requirements.text: The catalog's `registryid`, its entry's `registryid` and the described Registry root's `registryid` have different scopes. Their values need not match. A catalog-description `versionid`, target Resource `versionid`, OCI digest, Git commit and endpoint address MUST NOT be treated as interchangeable.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Design: Hosting Models / API Server Resolution

requirements.text: A conforming server-hosted resolver MUST expose a Core-conforming Registry through each consumer-facing binding that it implements. Its model MUST describe the resulting view. Responses, including source-derived data, MUST use the consumer-facing Registry's identity and navigation according to that binding. Source provenance and revision information remain separate.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Design: Hosting Models / API Server Resolution

requirements.text: The server MUST apply the source-selection, shadowing, error and completeness rules below. It MUST NOT expose unrelated source identities as though their XIDs were globally interchangeable. The server's advertised capabilities describe what it can provide, not the union of features advertised by sources.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Design: Hosting Models / API Server Resolution

requirements.text: The server MUST signal `producer` resolution for this consumer-facing view as specified below. Its clients read the server's results directly instead of repeating the server's catalog traversal.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Design: Hosting Models / No-Code and Stored Views

requirements.text: The producer MUST signal `producer` resolution in the stored view's capabilities. Storing files alone does not imply that federation has been performed. A stored Registry intended for consumer-side composition retains the default `consumer` behavior.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Design: Hosting Models / No-Code and Stored Views

requirements.text: Core single-document exports and multiple-document views remain available. The [directory mapping](../bindings/mapping.md) and [OCI](../bindings/oci.md) bindings additionally define storage formats with explicit content and integrity references. Their [snapshot completeness](#snapshots-and-completeness) rules identify which content has been captured. A live resolver MAY consume these stored snapshots as source Registries.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Design: Hosting Models / Signaling Who Performs Resolution

requirements.text: The Registry's enabled [Core capabilities](../../core/spec.md#registry-capabilities) can contain an OPTIONAL `federation` extension identifying who performs resolution for the selected view. This extension belongs to the enabled capabilities, not to a catalog attribute, an `xref` value or the `flags` array.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Design: Hosting Models / Signaling Who Performs Resolution

requirements.text: The extension is an object containing the REQUIRED string field `resolution`. Its values are case-sensitive:

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Design: Hosting Models / Signaling Who Performs Resolution

requirements.text: If the `federation` capability is absent, the consumer MUST use `consumer`, preserving the default behavior for existing Registries. If the capability is present, `resolution` MUST be present and MUST be a string. Malformed data produces `invalid_package`. An unknown owner value or unsupported field produces `unsupported_operation`. In these cases the consumer MUST NOT silently fall back to consumer-side resolution.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Design: Hosting Models / Signaling Who Performs Resolution

requirements.text: Before traversing a view's catalog, a federation-aware consumer MUST inspect the resolution-owner signal. It obtains the enabled capabilities through the selected binding's capability read or an equivalent inlined representation, rather than using an offered capability as the enabled value. A failed metadata read does not establish that the signal is absent. The consumer MUST handle that failure according to the binding's error rules.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Design: Hosting Models / Signaling Who Performs Resolution

requirements.text: With `producer`, the consumer MUST NOT repeat composition for the same request through the view's catalog. This rule applies to entity reads, collection enumeration, label selection and default or explicit Version reads. A `not_found` or other failure returned by the producer MUST NOT trigger fallback through that producer's catalog. The producer therefore advertises this value only when it handles resolution for the whole exposed view, rather than returning a partially combined result that its consumer has to finish.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Design: Hosting Models / Signaling Who Performs Resolution

requirements.text: The value applies to the selected Registry root, access context and revision. A capture MUST retain the value appropriate to its resulting view rather than copy `producer` from an upstream view whose composition it has not preserved. Consumers MUST retain that choice throughout the operation. If the value changes during a consistent multi-read capture, the outcome is `inconsistent_snapshot`.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Design: Resolving a Consumer Request / Local Resources and Ordered Sources

requirements.text: The federating Registry MUST use an explicit composition policy identifying the eligible catalog entries, their order and the Resource paths they can supply. That ordered list is configuration, not JSON object-map order or Category enumeration order. This specification does not define a catalog attribute for that list. A caller MAY choose one source explicitly instead.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Design: Resolving a Consumer Request / Local Resources and Ordered Sources

requirements.text: When source order is complete, precedence determines which origin supplies a Resource path that appears in several sources. These copies are not ambiguous. An unordered set of potentially competing origins cannot determine that result and MUST produce `ambiguous` when disambiguation is needed. A selector can still match several distinct visible Resources after shadowing; source precedence does not choose between those Resources. See [Select After Applying Shadows](#example-select-after-applying-shadows).

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Design: Resolving a Consumer Request / Local Resources and Ordered Sources

requirements.text: 1. Check the requested Resource path in the local Registry view. A present local Resource wins, including a local alias. A resolver MUST NOT fill its missing Version or unavailable document from another Registry.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Design: Resolving a Consumer Request / Local Resources and Ordered Sources

requirements.text: 3. Resolve the same typed Resource XID in the selected source context. A policy that projects a different source path MUST define that mapping explicitly. The source's model and data MUST be compatible with the consumer-visible model for that path.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Design: Resolving a Consumer Request / Local Resources and Ordered Sources

requirements.text: 5. Stop at the first found Resource. Select its requested Version, or its Core default Version, and obtain the requested representation. All Meta, Version and document reads for this Resource MUST use that selected origin and revision. Do not merge Version sets across origins.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Design: Resolving a Consumer Request / Local Resources and Ordered Sources

requirements.text: 6. A source Resource result of `not_found` permits trying the next configured source entry. Exhausting the list yields `not_found`. The resolver MUST report other failures, including authorization denial, unsupported binding/version, malformed data and integrity failure, rather than treat them as absence.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Design: Resolving a Consumer Request / Collections and Selection

requirements.text: A federating server exposing a combined Group or Resource collection MUST enumerate all eligible source collections needed for that view and apply the same Resource-level precedence before returning members. A shadowed source Resource contributes no additional Versions or alternate label values. Configured source type mappings MUST account for the collection's model.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Design: Resolving a Consumer Request / Collections and Selection

requirements.text: The resolver then evaluates a label selector against the visible collection. One match in an early source does not establish uniqueness. The resolver MUST consider all necessary collection pages and unshadowed sources. It MUST NOT present errors or incomplete traversal as a complete result. Counts, continuation links and model/capability reads MUST describe the consumer-visible Registry rather than the first source to respond.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Discovery and Binding Selection

requirements.text: A resolver MUST select a catalog-description Version before interpreting its advertisements. In the absence of an explicit description Version, it MUST use the catalog Resource's Core [default Version](../../core/spec.md#default-version-of-a-resource). A resolver MUST NOT infer an API from `weburl`, a label, a category name or a descriptive relationship. A website-only entry is a valid catalog entry, but is not resolvable.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Discovery and Binding Selection

requirements.text: The domain's `federationprofiles` array contains advertisements with `binding`, `endpoint`, OPTIONAL `priority` and OPTIONAL `parameters`. `binding` values are case-sensitive. The values defined by this family are:

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Discovery and Binding Selection

requirements.text: | `opcua` | Native UA endpoint URL | `registryroot`: portable NodeId. OPTIONAL `applicationuri` and `transportprofileuri`. |

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Discovery and Binding Selection

requirements.text: The bindings define parameter grammars and their supported transports. Endpoints MUST be absolute URIs and MUST NOT embed credentials. A selected built-in advertisement with an unknown parameter MUST produce `unsupported_operation`. Silently ignoring a parameter could select a different Registry or revision. An unknown `binding` value remains valid catalog metadata, but MUST NOT be executed as a known profile.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Discovery and Binding Selection

requirements.text: An absent `priority` means zero. Lower unsigned integer values are preferred. An absent `parameters` means an empty object. Selection MUST proceed as follows:

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Discovery and Binding Selection

requirements.text: A present `xregurl` contributes an implicit HTTP advertisement of priority zero, after explicit advertisements for tie-breaking. This applies even if an explicit advertisement names the same endpoint at another priority. If explicit HTTP advertisements exist, at least one endpoint MUST equal `xregurl` exactly. This exact comparison is a consistency rule, not a definition of URI identity.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Discovery and Binding Selection

requirements.text: If no candidate remains, the outcome is `unsupported_binding`. If the caller rejects access, the outcome is `policy_denied`. After an integrity error, version mismatch, policy rejection, ambiguous selection or inconsistent snapshot, a resolver MUST NOT silently fail over from the attempted binding. The caller MAY inspect the failure and initiate another operation with an explicitly different advertisement. A producer's endpoints describe the same logical Registry, but need not expose the same instantaneous state. Credentials and trust are established independently.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Read Operations

requirements.text: A Resource document request selects its Core [default Version](../../core/spec.md#default-version-of-a-resource). An explicit Version request selects exactly that Version, case-sensitively. Neither operation selects the greatest Version string, latest OCI tag, newest Git commit or most recently modified file. Metadata-only Resources have no domain document. Requesting one MUST produce `unsupported_operation`.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Read Operations

requirements.text: For each operation a resolver MUST:

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Read Operations

requirements.text: Origin information MUST identify the chosen advertisement, catalog-description Version when applicable, target XID and revision pin or the absence of an immutable pin. It MUST be returned separately from Core identity attributes.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Read Operations

requirements.text: A library can return origin information alongside the value. A producer-resolved service MUST document how an authorized consumer obtains the result's context through a binding extension or associated metadata interface. An internal server log alone does not provide that context to the consumer.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Read Operations

requirements.text: The OPTIONAL [publication extension](../publication/spec.md) defines a concrete open-context record and HTTP discovery link for views associated with an immutable publication. Implementations claiming that extension MUST return its checked context. This does not impose a publication write API on ordinary federation sources or change the resolution-owner signal.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Read Operations

requirements.text: A resolver MAY bypass catalog discovery when the caller supplies a standalone endpoint, but MUST still establish all other context.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Read Operations

requirements.text: If a model is captured, the package MUST preserve enough model source to retain Resource type sharing. An expanded model alone can obscure [`ximportresources`](../../core/model.md#reuse-of-resource-definitions) provenance. [Included model documents](../../core/model.md#includes-in-the-xregistry-model-data) MUST be resolved within the captured scope, or supplied with immutable checked references. Offline-complete interpretation MUST NOT fetch mutable external includes. A consumer MUST NOT accept unknown Core versions merely because a document parses.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Identity and References

requirements.text: An [XID](../../core/spec.md#xid-attribute) identifies an entity within one Registry. Resolvers MUST preserve both its Registry context and typed collection path. The same XID in unrelated Registries does not establish that the entities or their bytes are identical. Core [IDs](../../core/spec.md#singularid-id-attribute) are unique case-insensitively within their parent, but are looked up case-sensitively. Storage bindings MUST NOT weaken either rule.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Identity and References / Local Cross-References

requirements.text: Core [`meta.xref`](../../core/spec.md#cross-referencing-resources) remains an intra-Registry Resource XID. Federation chooses a source Registry through the catalog and composition policy, rather than adding a remote meaning to this Core attribute. Its source and target MUST have the same Resource model type. Structurally identical independent definitions are insufficient. Sharing between Group types uses [`ximportresources`](../../core/model.md#reuse-of-resource-definitions).

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Identity and References / Local Cross-References

requirements.text: An alias in `/mirrors/local/assets/copy` can then carry `meta.xref: "/documents/main/assets/item"`. When Core calls for inherited target metadata, source IDs and navigation MUST remain source-relative. If the target is itself an alias, a resolver MUST NOT follow another `xref`. If the target is unavailable, Core's minimal ID-like alias serialization applies. This is not automatically `not_found` for the source.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Identity and References / Local Cross-References

requirements.text: Core's malformed-reference rules distinguish a malformed XID or nonexistent model type from a dangling entity instance. Document view MUST NOT expand the target. A document-view request for an alias's Versions or an individual Version MUST retain Core's `cannot_doc_xref` behavior. This specification does not add remote writes to aliases.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Identity and References / Remote References and Composition

requirements.text: A Version's `<RESOURCE>url` references a domain document. A consumer MUST NOT interpret it as remote Resource metadata or as a request to import Versions. Reading its bytes does not change the identity of the describing Version.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Identity and References / Remote References and Composition

requirements.text: A projected Registry MAY expose locally modeled Resources representing external content. Any `xref` it exposes MUST satisfy Core within that Registry. A projection MUST NOT treat Resources as identical solely because their XIDs collide. Competing origins require explicit selection or `ambiguous`, rather than an undocumented choice of origin. A domain can define a shared logical-identity policy without altering XID scope.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Identity and References / Reference Bases

requirements.text: A resolver MUST NOT substitute one of these bases for another. Some bindings cannot preserve or supply the base needed to interpret a relative document URI. Such a binding MUST report `invalid_package` or `unsupported_operation` rather than guess.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Selectors

requirements.text: The `label` names a map key. `value` is a literal string. Labels MAY be absent, and an empty string value is valid. An absent key does not match an empty value. Comparison MUST follow Core's case-insensitive string filtering. En-US Unicode collation is STRONGLY RECOMMENDED by Core. This specification adds neither mandatory language keys nor NFC normalization. Map-key selection remains exact. Comparison applies to the selected value.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Selectors

requirements.text: A resolver using a transport filter MUST escape its literal value and attribute path under that binding. `*`, `\`, `.` or an operator in a selector MUST NOT accidentally become a wildcard or another expression. Implementations MAY instead enumerate and compare locally. An optimization MUST NOT change the matching or ambiguity outcome.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Selectors

requirements.text: With no matches, the outcome is `not_found`; with exactly one complete match, the result is the selected entity. Multiple matches produce `ambiguous`. Before claiming uniqueness, a resolver MUST inspect all necessary continuation pages. It MAY report ambiguity after the second match without reading further pages. A resolver MUST NOT report a request limit, incomplete page chain or unstable collection as a unique selection. Resource selectors examine the effective metadata of their default Versions as defined by Core, not only the reduced Resource object in document view.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Representations

requirements.text: Metadata and domain documents are distinct results, even when both are JSON. `self`, `metaurl` and `defaultversionurl` locate metadata under the relevant Core binding. A consumer MUST NOT automatically treat them as raw-byte locations.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Representations

requirements.text: Native access to a [snapshot](#snapshots-and-completeness) uses Core [document view](../../core/spec.md#doc-flag), with storage descriptors and transport context outside the Core entity. This requires removing duplicated default-Version attributes, Version validation-result attributes and `shortself`, and suppressing alias-target expansion. Links to entities included in the returned document MUST use document-local JSON Pointers. Links to entities not included MUST NOT be rewritten to nonexistent local pointers. Reassembling records into a larger document requires rebasing their pointers to that document. Concatenating records whose pointers are relative to each individual record does not preserve those targets.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Representations

requirements.text: Native bindings MUST distinguish these document-view serializations from the logical operation that retrieves an alias's target document under Core. A resolver MUST report an unsupported view or alias-Version document view, and MUST NOT silently convert it to a different view.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Representations

requirements.text: A binding offering API-view results MUST define actually retrievable Core-conforming `self` and navigation URLs. An implementation-defined URI with no retrieval contract is insufficient. An OPTIONAL HTTP facade MUST conform separately to [Core HTTP](../../core/http.md). Neither `oci://` locators nor UA NodeIds become Core XIDs.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Representations

requirements.text: Formats MUST preserve extension attributes and domain bytes. A zero-byte document is present content and MUST NOT be replaced by `{}`, `null` or a missing document. Binary documents MUST NOT pass through text conversion.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Snapshots and Completeness

requirements.text: Every snapshot MUST have a complete internal containment graph. The completeness class determines how it handles external content:

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Snapshots and Completeness

requirements.text: - A linked snapshot MAY retain explicit external document references.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Snapshots and Completeness

requirements.text: - An offline-complete snapshot MUST also contain the declared xRegistry document content in its selected scope and the model material needed to interpret that content.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Snapshots and Completeness

requirements.text: The producer MUST identify the scope and completeness class. Missing internally referenced data is an invalid package in either class.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Snapshots and Completeness

requirements.text: Offline completeness does not mean copying all cataloged Registries or discovering arbitrary links inside every domain document. External reference bases and known content integrity descriptors MUST survive packaging. Materializing external content requires preserving its actual bytes.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Snapshots and Completeness

requirements.text: An immutable revision MUST remain pinned throughout an operation. A moving tag, branch or mutable directory name is not a revision pin. A resolver MUST report a live HTTP or UA endpoint without a snapshot guarantee as live, not as an atomic snapshot. Revision identifiers MUST NOT be substituted for Resource Version IDs.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Snapshots and Completeness

requirements.text: Digests identify exact bytes; they do not establish semantic equality. Equivalent publications can therefore have different digests. New snapshots MAY reuse unchanged content and subtrees, but MUST be readable without replaying older snapshots.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Snapshots and Completeness

requirements.text: The [publication extension](../publication/spec.md) adds named channels over these snapshots. A resolver selects a moving channel once per operation and retains the selected immutable context across collection pages, entity reads and document retrieval. Missing data in that context MUST NOT trigger a refresh or lookup against another channel head. Opening the channel again is a separately identified operation.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Errors

requirements.text: When an underlying Core error or transport diagnostic is available, the resolver error MUST retain it without exposing credentials. A resolver MUST NOT return an incomplete retrieval as a successful empty collection. Core's dangling-alias exception still applies.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Security Considerations

requirements.text: Catalog data and package contents are untrusted input. Discovery is not an authorization grant. A resolver MUST apply caller policy before contacting endpoints, following redirects, reading local paths or retrieving external documents. A resolver MUST scope credentials to the authenticated destination, and MUST NOT forward them merely because a catalog entry or redirect names it.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Security Considerations

requirements.text: Resolvers MUST bound traversal depth, request count and aggregate bytes, detect discovery/redirect cycles, and report when a bound is exhausted. SHA-256 integrity does not authenticate a publisher. Signature and provenance policies are separate from containment completeness. Git readers MUST NOT execute repository content. Filesystem readers MUST enforce containment, including symlinks and reparse points.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Conformance

requirements.text: A federation resolver MUST implement the resolution-owner signaling, selection, context, Core semantics, representations and failures defined above and identify each binding it implements. Conformance to one binding does not imply support for another.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Conformance

requirements.text: A snapshot producer MUST identify its format, scope and linked or offline-complete class and produce a complete internal graph. An OPTIONAL API facade requires separate protocol-binding conformance.

source.section: xRegistry Federation / Conformance

requirements.text: Tests MUST distinguish full graph validation from selective lookup. A validator walking everything does not demonstrate efficient selective resolution. Run the shared and binding suites from the repository root:

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.1. Thing Descriptions and Thing Models

requirements.text: A Thing Model (TM) is a JSON-LD 1.1 document conforming to [WoT-TM 1.1][WoT-TM-1.1]. It describes an abstract class of Things and typically omits `href` values from its forms. Thing Models are reusable: a concrete Thing Description MAY extend or compose one or more Thing Models through WoT `tm:extends` and `tm:ref` mechanisms or JSON-LD `@type` declarations.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.1. Thing Descriptions and Thing Models

requirements.text: Although both document classes use JSON-LD and share part of its vocabulary, a WoT Registry MUST treat them as distinct Resource types. Their intended use, validation rules and lifecycles differ.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.2. Relationship to Other xRegistry Specs

requirements.text: - A Thing Description's `forms` array describes protocol bindings that MAY also be represented as `endpoint` Resources. See [Section 6.3](#63-thing-description-to-endpoint-registry).

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.2. Relationship to Other xRegistry Specs

requirements.text: - A Thing Description's property/action/event data schemas (declared inline via WoT data-schema vocabulary) MAY reference external schemas managed by the xRegistry Schema Registry. See [Section 6.4](#64-thing-description-to-schema-registry).

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.2. Relationship to Other xRegistry Specs

requirements.text: - A Thing Description MAY reference one or more Thing Models from which it is derived. See [Section 6.1](#61-thing-description-to-thing-model).

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.2. Relationship to Other xRegistry Specs

requirements.text: This specification does not require the Registry to resolve or validate these cross-references. An implementation MAY check that a referent exists, but it still stores and serves the document when a referent is absent. A Consumer composing a TD from Thing Models or binding an affordance to an endpoint depends on those references independently of the Registry's checks.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: Each Version of a `thingdescription` or `thingmodel` Resource holds a complete WoT document, stored without rewriting its bytes. A Resource's `wotid` and registry Resource id are stable across compatible revisions. `wotid` is declared with [`matchversions`][xRegistry matchversions]. A registry MUST reject a Version that supplies a different `wotid`. A Thing Model's major version MUST be part of its `wotid`. A breaking change MUST use a new `wotid` and a new Resource ([Section 5.1.1](#511-breaking-changes-and-successor-identifiers)).

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: Thing Model Resources and Thing Description Resources MUST use Core [`versionmode`][Core versionmode] `semver` and [`singleversionroot`][Core singleversionroot] `true`. Core orders each Resource's [`ancestorid`][Core ancestorid] lineage by SemVer precedence and forbids multiple roots with these aspects. The assignment rules for the corresponding authored fields are:

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: | TM | `version.model` | `versionid` MUST equal the authored value verbatim. | The registry MUST assign `0.0.0-N`. |

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: | TD | `version.instance` | `versionid` MUST equal the authored value verbatim. | The registry MUST assign `0.0.0-N`. |

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: For either Resource type, the registry MUST inspect the authored field without modifying the stored document. The original authored field MUST NOT be rewritten, including when absent or non-SemVer.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: A valid authored value is SemVer 2.0.0 without build metadata and fits Core's 128-character [id constraint][Core id constraints]. SemVer build metadata (`+build`) MUST be rejected as `invalid-version`, since `+` is not allowed by Core's id constraints. An authored SemVer value that exceeds Core's 128-character id limit MUST also be rejected under those constraints.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: `N` is the lowest positive integer whose complete id is not already used in the Resource. The registry MUST assign an omitted `versionid`. A supplied `versionid` MUST equal the authored or generated assignment, or the registry MUST reject it as `version-mismatch`. A supplied id that violates Core's id grammar MUST be rejected as `invalid-version` before this comparison. Core requires an immutable, unique [`versionid`][Core versionid]. This extension defines the assignment in place of its default [Version ID algorithm][Core Version IDs].

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: The Registry MUST perform assignment and creation atomically with respect to concurrent writes, so two writes cannot claim the same generated id.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: Each Thing Model Version and each Thing Description Version MUST have a server-set, read-only `versionorigin`. Its value MUST be `authored` when the Version's id comes from a SemVer authored field, and `generated` otherwise.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: Client-supplied `versionorigin` MUST be ignored under Core's [read-only attribute rules][Core read-only rules]. The model initializes the attribute to `authored`. When the registry assigns a generated id, it MUST replace that initial value with `generated`. The model default does not replace the assignment rules above.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: Generated ids are prereleases. They MUST NOT be used as minimum-version floors, even when the target Version is absent.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: For Thing Models, the Resource-level [`compatibility`][Core compatibility] attribute in `meta` MUST default to `backward`. A backward-compatible TM revision MUST NOT remove or narrow an affordance, a data schema or an `@type`, and MUST NOT introduce a new mandatory member. Narrowing includes reducing the accepted values or operations of an existing member. These constraints apply to every earlier Version in the Resource's Core [`ancestorid`][Core ancestorid] lineage.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: A Registry MAY validate this domain-specific compatibility rule through Core's [`validatecompatibility`][Core validatecompatibility] capability. Core's [`strictvalidation`][Core strictvalidation] rules still apply. Absence of a domain validator does not permit a Producer to publish an incompatible revision under the same `wotid`.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: When [`defaultversionsticky`][Core defaultversionsticky] is false, Core's SemVer [`versionmode`][Core versionmode] orders the default. A late `1.0.1` after `1.1.0` MUST NOT replace `1.1.0` as the default. A sticky default MUST be honoured.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: For migration, an operator SHOULD inventory every Version and root of a legacy Resource before enabling this model. Compatible TM roots SHOULD be imported into one SemVer-ordered lineage with ids assigned by the rules above. Incompatible roots MUST be placed in distinct Resources with distinct major-version `wotid`s.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: The operator SHOULD inventory legacy TD Resources with manually assigned `versionid`s and re-import them with ids assigned from `version.instance` or generated by these rules.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: Where changing an old immutable id or authored document would be necessary, the operator SHOULD preserve the legacy Resource outside the conforming collection and import a copy under a new registry Resource id.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.3. Versioning

requirements.text: The operator MUST preserve authored bytes, record old-to-new registry paths for callers holding pins, and establish a valid default before enabling `singleversionroot`. An operator MUST NOT claim that an unresolved multiple-root Resource conforms to this model.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 1. Overview / 1.4. Document Store

requirements.text: An xRegistry-unaware WoT consumer MAY use a Version's `self` URL with the `$details` suffix removed, or its `shortself` URL, as a regular WoT TD or TM URL. The unchanged `self` URL returns xRegistry metadata rather than the document. The metadata and document URLs are not interchangeable.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 2. Notations and Terminology / 2.1. Notational Conventions

requirements.text: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in [RFC 2119](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2119).

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 2. Notations and Terminology / 2.1. Notational Conventions

requirements.text: For clarity, OPTIONAL attributes (specification-defined and extensions) are OPTIONAL for clients to use, but the servers' responsibility will vary. Server-unknown extension attributes MUST be silently stored in the backing datastore. Specification-defined, and server-known extension, attributes MUST generate an error if the corresponding feature is not supported or enabled.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 2. Notations and Terminology / 2.1. Notational Conventions

requirements.text: However, as with all attributes, if accepting the attribute results in a bad state (such as exceeding a size limit or resulting in a security issue), then the server MAY choose to reject the request.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 2. Notations and Terminology / 2.1. Notational Conventions

requirements.text: In the pseudo JSON format snippets `?` means the preceding attribute is OPTIONAL, `*` means the preceding attribute MAY appear zero or more times, and `+` means the preceding attribute MUST appear at least once. The presence of the `#` character means the remaining portion of the line is a comment. Whitespace characters in the JSON snippets are used for readability and are not normative.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 2. Notations and Terminology / 2.2. Terminology / 2.2.1. Thing Description

requirements.text: The TD's `version.instance` carries its revision, including breaking major revisions. A major revision remains under the same `id`, `wotid`, and Resource. If a Resource declares the [`compatibility`][xRegistry compatibility] attribute, all its Versions MUST adhere to that policy. A TD that identifies a different Thing MUST use that Thing's `id` and a corresponding Resource. See [Section 1.3](#13-versioning).

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 2. Notations and Terminology / 2.2. Terminology / 2.2.3. WoT Identifier

requirements.text: A WoT identifier is held in the `wotid` attribute. It is distinct from the xRegistry `thingdescriptionid`/`thingmodelid`, which identifies the Resource within a Registry. The two MAY hold the same string when the authored identifier satisfies xRegistry's id grammar. Most do not: a URL such as `https://fabrikam.example/things/lamp-42` is not a legal xRegistry id. The model therefore keeps them as separate attributes rather than reusing the Resource id. [Section 5.1](#51-wot-identifiers-and-registry-ids) defines how the two relate.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry

requirements.text: Implementations of this specification MAY include additional extension attributes, including the `*` attribute of type `any`.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.1. Thing Description Groups

requirements.text: Every Thing Description (the `thingdescription` Resource) MUST reside inside a Thing Description Group.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.2. Thing Description Resources

requirements.text: Thing Description Resources MUST use Core [`versionmode`][Core versionmode] value `semver` and [`singleversionroot`][Core singleversionroot] value `true`, as specified in [Section 1.3](#13-versioning). Core derives `ancestorid` by SemVer precedence and enforces one root ([`ancestorid`][Core ancestorid]).

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.2. Thing Description Resources

requirements.text: The Version-level `versionorigin` attribute is REQUIRED, read-only, and uses the strict enumeration `authored` or `generated`. The `versionid` is assigned from `version.instance` when that member is SemVer without build metadata. Otherwise it is the lowest free `0.0.0-N` id. The original document bytes, including `version.instance`, are not rewritten.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.2. Thing Description Resources

requirements.text: The `format` attribute of a `thingdescription` Resource Version MUST be `"JSON-LD/1.1"`. [model.json](model.json) declares the `format` enumeration as `strict`, so a registry rejects any other value rather than merely discouraging it.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.2. Thing Description Resources

requirements.text: The `contenttype` of a `thingdescription` document MUST be `application/td+json` per [WoT-TD 1.1 §12.1][WoT-TD-1.1], or another media type the deployment has explicitly registered for WoT documents.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.2. Thing Description Resources

requirements.text: `contenttype` is client-supplied and determines the media type used to serve the stored bytes through the document view ([Section 1.4](#14-document-store)). A Registry MUST NOT serve a stored document under a client-supplied media type that would interpret it as active content, such as `text/html`, `image/svg+xml` or `application/xhtml+xml`. A Registry MUST either reject such a write or serve the document under the media type this section requires.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.2. Thing Description Resources

requirements.text: WoT tooling dereferences a Version's document-view URL directly. For documents it did not author, a Registry SHOULD additionally return `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` or serve them from an origin separate from any Registry user interface. See [Section 7](#7-security).

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.2. Thing Description Resources

requirements.text: The `wotid` attribute is REQUIRED and holds the document's authored WoT identifier, distinct from the `thingdescriptionid`. See [Section 5.1](#51-wot-identifiers-and-registry-ids). The OPTIONAL `derivedfrom` attribute lists the `wotid`s of the Thing Models this Thing Description extends or composes. It is a producer-supplied index rather than an authority over the document's own references, as [Section 5.2](#52-preserving-customer-documents) describes.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.2. Thing Description Resources

requirements.text: All Versions of a single Thing Description Resource MUST adhere to the semantic rules of the Thing Description's [`compatibility`][Core compatibility] attribute, if specified.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.2. Thing Description Resources

requirements.text: Implementations of this specification SHOULD use the xRegistry default algorithm for generating new `versionid` values.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.2. Thing Description Resources

requirements.text: The default Version is the one served when no Version is named. It MUST be determined by the xRegistry Core rules, including the Resource's [`defaultversionsticky`][Core defaultversionsticky] setting. A deployment MAY use that setting to pin the default to a Version other than the newest. This specification does not redefine default-Version selection. See [Version IDs][xRegistry version-ids] for more information.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.3. Thing Model Groups

requirements.text: Every Thing Model (i.e. the `thingmodel` Resource) MUST reside inside a Thing Model Group.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.4. Thing Model Resources

requirements.text: The `format` attribute of a `thingmodel` Resource Version MUST be `"JSON-LD/1.1"`, enforced by the same `strict` enumeration used for `thingdescription`. The `contenttype` MUST be `application/tm+json` per [WoT-TM 1.1 §12.2][WoT-TM-1.1], or another media type the deployment has explicitly registered for WoT documents, and the same constraint on serving stored bytes as active content applies as in [Section 4.2](#42-thing-description-resources).

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.4. Thing Model Resources

requirements.text: The `compatibility`, `versionid`, `versionorigin` and [`ancestorid`][Core ancestorid] rules for Thing Models are defined in [Section 1.3](#13-versioning), subject to Core's [`compatibility`][Core compatibility] and [`versionid`][Core versionid] semantics. The Version-level `versionorigin` is a REQUIRED string with the strict enumeration `authored` or `generated`, and is read-only. The model declares `compatibility` under `metaattributes`, with `required: true` and `default: backward`, as Core requires for an attribute with a default.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.4. Thing Model Resources

requirements.text: The `wotid` attribute is REQUIRED on a `thingmodel` and holds the document's authored WoT identifier, which is distinct from the `thingmodelid`. Where a Thing Model extends another via a `tm:extends` link relation, or references one via `tm:ref`, or composes one via `tm:submodel`, the referenced Thing Models' `wotid`s SHOULD be listed in `derivedfrom`.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.5. Formats / 4.5.1. WoT Thing Description

requirements.text: - The document's `@context` MUST include `https://www.w3.org/2022/wot/td/v1.1`.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.5. Formats / 4.5.1. WoT Thing Description

requirements.text: - A URI-reference pointing to a TD MAY use a JSON-Pointer ([RFC 6901](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6901)) fragment to deep-link into a particular property, action, or event affordance, e.g. `…/thingdescriptions/lamp-42#/properties/status`.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.5. Formats / 4.5.2. WoT Thing Model

requirements.text: - The document's `@context` MUST include `https://www.w3.org/2022/wot/td/v1.1` and the document's top-level `@type` MUST include `tm:ThingModel`.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.6. Provenance and Selection Metadata

requirements.text: Tools and autonomous agents need explicit metadata to choose among documents describing similar Things rather than inferring their provenance from titles or naming conventions. Both `thingdescription` and `thingmodel` Resources carry the following OPTIONAL attributes:

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.6. Provenance and Selection Metadata

requirements.text: A Consumer choosing between candidate Thing Models SHOULD prefer, in order:

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.6. Provenance and Selection Metadata

requirements.text: If the choice remains open, the Consumer SHOULD prefer the document whose `canonicalurl` it already trusts. [model.json](model.json) declares the `maturity` enumeration as `strict`, so a Registry rejects values outside this set. A Consumer that nonetheless encounters one, for example from a federated Registry, MUST NOT rank it above `Experimental`. This specification defines no precedence for it.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.6. Provenance and Selection Metadata

requirements.text: These attributes are advisory and unverified assertions by the Resource's writer about the document's origin and maturity. This specification defines no mechanism for a Registry to validate a `publisher` or `standardsbody` claim. A Registry MUST NOT be assumed to have validated one.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.6. Provenance and Selection Metadata

requirements.text: A Consumer MUST NOT treat these attributes as authenticated provenance. The preference order only breaks ties among documents the Consumer already trusts, whether by Group, writer identity or an out-of-band signature. It MUST NOT be used to establish trust in a document from an untrusted writer.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.6. Provenance and Selection Metadata

requirements.text: One `wotid` MAY legitimately match several Resources written by different parties ([Section 5.3](#53-lookup)), so a Consumer can face this choice. See also [Section 7](#7-security).

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. WoT Registry / 4.6. Provenance and Selection Metadata

requirements.text: These attributes are also not part of a document's semantic identity. A registry MUST NOT treat two documents as the same document because their provenance attributes agree, nor as different documents because they differ: identity is `wotid` alone ([Section 5.1](#51-wot-identifiers-and-registry-ids)).

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.1. WoT Identifiers and Registry Ids

requirements.text: These identifiers serve a similar purpose but follow different grammars. `https://fabrikam.example/things/lamp-42` is not a valid entity id or `xid` component. An `xid` is not what a Thing author writes. Where an authored identifier satisfies the id grammar, a client MAY use it as the Resource id. A Registry cannot rely on that choice.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.1. WoT Identifiers and Registry Ids

requirements.text: A deployment MAY derive its Resource ids from `wotid` values by a convention of its own. The [OpenUSD Artifact Registry][OpenUSD Draft] working draft defines one such construction. No convention is mandated by this specification, and a Consumer MUST NOT assume that an id it did not assign was produced by one.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.1. WoT Identifiers and Registry Ids

requirements.text: A `wotid` MUST NOT encode a compatible revision of the document it names. A Thing Model's major version MUST be included in that stable identity, for example `urn:fabrikam:lamp:v1` or `https://fabrikam.example/tm/lamp/v1`. Minor and patch revisions are carried by `versionid` and `version.model`, not appended to the identifier. No particular spelling of the major-version token is mandated.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.1. WoT Identifiers and Registry Ids

requirements.text: When a document is revised compatibly, its `wotid` and Resource id MUST remain unchanged, and a new Version is created under the same Resource. A Thing Model breaking revision uses a distinct major-version `wotid` as specified in [Section 5.1.1](#511-breaking-changes-and-successor-identifiers). A Thing Description major revision remains under its existing `id` and `wotid`. A new TD identifier names a different concrete Thing.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.1. WoT Identifiers and Registry Ids

requirements.text: A `wotid` is REQUIRED, and the rule for populating it depends on the document:

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.1. WoT Identifiers and Registry Ids

requirements.text: - Where the document carries an `id` member, `wotid` MUST equal it verbatim. A registry that parses the stored document MUST reject a write whose `wotid` differs from that `id`, rather than storing two identities for one document. A registry that does not parse the document cannot detect the disagreement. Both types of registry MUST NOT rewrite either value to resolve the disagreement, because [Section 5.2](#52-preserving-customer-documents) forbids editing the document.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.1. WoT Identifiers and Registry Ids

requirements.text: - Where the document carries no `id` member — which [WoT-TD 1.1][WoT-TD-1.1] permits for TDs served from a fixed URL, and which is common for TMs — the Producer MUST supply a `wotid` at write time, and that supplied value is thereafter the document's identity in this registry.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.1. WoT Identifiers and Registry Ids

requirements.text: - A registry MUST reject a write that supplies neither an `id` member nor a `wotid`, rather than inventing one, because an invented identifier is not stable across registries.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.1. WoT Identifiers and Registry Ids / 5.1.1. Breaking Changes and Successor Identifiers

requirements.text: A breaking Thing Model change MUST use a new major-version `wotid` and a distinct Resource. The predecessor's `wotid` MUST NOT be modified. A major Thing Description revision remains a Version of the same concrete Thing under the same `id`, `wotid`, and Resource. A distinct TD `id` and `wotid` identify a different concrete Thing, not a breaking revision of the existing one.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.1. WoT Identifiers and Registry Ids / 5.1.1. Breaking Changes and Successor Identifiers

requirements.text: The predecessor Resource MUST be marked with Core's [`deprecated`][xRegistry deprecated] attribute, whose `alternative` MUST be the successor Resource's URL. Its Versions MUST remain retrievable. Deprecation alone MUST NOT cause the resolver to redirect a reference to the successor. A Consumer MAY inspect the successor and explicitly choose to adopt its different identity.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.2. Preserving Customer Documents

requirements.text: - A registry MUST store the WoT document byte-for-byte as supplied, apart from transformations the client explicitly requested.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.2. Preserving Customer Documents

requirements.text: - A registry MUST NOT rewrite the document's `id` member, its `links[].href` values, its `tm:extends` or `tm:ref` targets, or any other identifier internal to the document, into registry-specific identifiers.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.2. Preserving Customer Documents

requirements.text: - A retrieval of a stored Version through the document view MUST return the exact bytes supplied, as the xRegistry Core document view already requires. Re-serializing the document — reordering members, re-indenting, or normalizing its JSON-LD — is not permitted.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.2. Preserving Customer Documents

requirements.text: `derivedfrom` is a producer-supplied *index* of the document's references, not an authority over them. A registry MAY verify that it matches the `tm:extends`, `tm:submodel`, `tm:ref` and `links[].rel="type"` targets in the stored document, and SHOULD reject a write where the two disagree. Where a registry does not verify, the document is authoritative.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.2. Preserving Customer Documents

requirements.text: When making a trust, allow-list or compliance decision about a document's lineage, a Consumer MUST derive that lineage from the document itself and MUST NOT rely on `derivedfrom` alone.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.3. Lookup

requirements.text: An implementation SHOULD serve this query in time that does not grow with collection size, in practice by indexing `wotid` on both `thingdescriptions` and `thingmodels`. A linear scan for each reference would make TD composition slower as the collection grows.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.3. Lookup

requirements.text: A `wotid` SHOULD be unique within a Group, so that a Group-scoped query for one identifies a single Resource. Across Groups a `wotid` MAY repeat — the same vendor TM legitimately appears in two tenants' Groups. A registry-wide query MAY therefore match more than one Resource. A caller that needs exactly one narrows the query by naming the Group.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.3. Lookup

requirements.text: A Registry-wide query MUST return every matching Resource rather than an arbitrary one of them. [Section 4.6](#46-provenance-and-selection-metadata) governs how a Consumer chooses among them.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.3. Lookup

requirements.text: A request to the Resource URL without a Version returns the Core default, even when [`defaultversionsticky`][Core defaultversionsticky] is true. A registry MUST serve that default when no Version is named.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.3. Lookup

requirements.text: For reference resolution, a resolver MUST use [Section 5.4](#54-versioned-reference-resolution), not lexical id order, publication time or an assumption that the default satisfies the reference.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.3. Lookup

requirements.text: Callers SHOULD NOT fold the identifier and version into one opaque string. When carrying both through a transport, such as message headers, a caller SHOULD use separate values, for example a `wotid` header and a `versionid` header, rather than a single compound token like `urn:fabrikam:lamp@3` that every recipient has to take apart. The identifier stays a WoT identifier, and the version stays a `versionid` the recipient can put straight into a URL.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.4. Versioned Reference Resolution / 5.4.1. Floors and Pins

requirements.text: A reference MAY carry a minimum SemVer, called its floor, but MUST NOT carry a version range. `tm:minVersion` is a member of `tm:extends` or `tm:submodel` links and a sibling of `tm:ref`. `td:minVersion` is a member of `td:extends` or `td:subthing` links and a sibling of `td:ref`.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.4. Versioned Reference Resolution / 5.4.1. Floors and Pins

requirements.text: A floor MUST be a SemVer 2.0.0 string without build metadata and within Core's 128-character [id limit][Core id constraints]. It MUST NOT have the generated `0.0.0-N` form. Invalid syntax or a generated floor MUST produce `invalid-version`. `td:minVersion` on a TM reference and `tm:minVersion` on a TD-to-TD reference MUST produce `invalid-floor`.

review.note: The public selection helper validates parsed floor syntax, the Core length boundary and the target-kind discriminator. Section 1.3 defines generated N as positive, so 0.0.0-0 remains an authored prerelease rather than a generated floor. Reference extraction and provider acquisition are separate obligations. Re-reviewed against PR #571 at 514f6eac: this floor clause and its context are unchanged; the successor clarifies the separate incomplete closure profile in section 5.4.4.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.4. Versioned Reference Resolution / 5.4.1. Floors and Pins

requirements.text: For a TD with exactly one `rel: "type"` link, its `version.model`, when present, is the implicit floor of that link. If the link also has an explicit `tm:minVersion`, the greater value by SemVer precedence is the effective floor. An explicit lower value MUST NOT weaken the implicit floor. If only one floor is present, that floor applies.

review.note: For an already identified TM type link, selection derives the greater parsed implicit/explicit floor and preserves either floor when supplied alone. Sticky-default failures distinguish floor enforcement from merely choosing the highest Version. URI/context parsing and link extraction remain separate. Re-reviewed against PR #571 at 514f6eac: this floor clause and its context are unchanged; the successor clarifies the separate incomplete closure profile in section 5.4.4.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.4. Versioned Reference Resolution / 5.4.1. Floors and Pins

requirements.text: For a TD with several type links and `version.model`, every type link MUST carry its own `tm:minVersion`. Otherwise, resolution MUST fail as `ambiguous-floor`, including when resolving a different, fully specified link. When every link has a floor, each link MUST use the greater of its own floor and `version.model`.

review.note: The selection request carries the parsed total link count and whether every link has a floor. The helper reports ambiguity even for a specified link, before malformed individual floors, and raises complete links to version.model. Deriving these inputs from customer documents is not claimed. Re-reviewed against PR #571 at 514f6eac: this floor clause and its context are unchanged; the successor clarifies the separate incomplete closure profile in section 5.4.4.

source.section: WoT Registry Service - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Identity and Resolution / 5.4. Versioned Reference Resolution / 5.4.1. Floors and Pins

requirements.text: For several type links without `version.model`, each link uses its own floor if present. An omitted floor MUST NOT produce `ambiguous-floor`.

review.note: With no parsed TD model version, missing floors on other type links do not cause ambiguity. A supplied floor still constrains selection and fails when unmet.
